body.text: Vimalakīrtinirdeśa
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> (The Teaching of Vimalakīrti)

body.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!

body.text: Vkn 1.1 evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān vaiśālyāṃ viharati sma, āmrapālīvane mahatā bhikṣusamghena sārdham aṣṭābhir bhikṣusahasraiḥ,
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.1) Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Vaiśālī</s>, in <s>Āmrapālī</s>'s grove, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), eight thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>,

body.text: Vkn 1.2 sarvair arhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravair niḥkleśair vaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñair ājāneyair mahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyair apahṛtabhārair anuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasamyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramiprāptaiḥ,
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.2) all of them <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones), with <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) exhausted, free from afflictions, self-mastered, with minds well-liberated, with wisdom well-liberated, thoroughbreds, great elephants, who had done what was to be done, accomplished their task, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, with the fetters of becoming completely exhausted, with minds well-liberated through perfect knowledge, who had reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all minds,

body.text:
Vkn 1.3 dvātriṃśatā ca bodhisatvasahasrair abhijñānābhijñātaiḥ sarvair mahābhijñāparikarmaniryātaiḥ, buddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitaiḥ, saddharmanagarapālaiḥ, saddharmaparigrāhakaiḥ, mahāsiṃhanādanādibhiḥ, daśadigvighuṣṭaśabdaiḥ, sarvasatvānadhyeṣitakalyāṇamitraiḥ, triratnavaṃśānupacchetṛbhiḥ, nihatamārapratyarthikaiḥ, sarvaparapravādyanabhibhūtaiḥ, smṛtisamādhidhāraṇīsaṃpannaiḥ, sarvanivaraṇaparyutthānavigataiḥ, anāvaraṇavimokṣapratiṣṭhitaiḥ, anācchedyapratibhānaiḥ, dānadamaniyamasaṃyamaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyaniryātaiḥ, anupalambhānutpattikadharmakṣāntisamanvāgataiḥ, avaivartikadharmacakrapravartakaiḥ, alakṣaṇamudrāmudritaiḥ, sarvasatvendriyajñānakuśalaiḥ, sarvaparṣadanabhibhūtavaiśāradyavikrāmibhiḥ, mahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacitaiḥ, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasamalaṃkṛtakāyaiḥ, paramarūpadhāribhiḥ, apagatabhūṣaṇaiḥ, meruśikharābhyudgatayaśaḥkīrtisamudgataiḥ, dṛḍhavajrādhyāśayābhedyabuddhadharmaprasādapratilabdhaiḥ, dharmaratnavikaraṇāmṛtajalasaṃpravarṣakaiḥ, sarvasatvarutaravitasvarāṅgaghoṣaviśuddhasvaraiḥ, gambhīradharmapratītyāvatārāntānantadṛṣṭivāsanānusaṃdhisamucchinnaiḥ, vigatabhayasiṃhopamanādibhiḥ, tulyātulyasamatikrāntaiḥ, dharmaratnaprajñāsamudānītamahāsārthavāhaiḥ ṛjusūkṣmamṛdudurdṛśaduranubodhasarvadharmakuśalaiḥ, āgatisatvāśayamatimanupraviṣṭajñānaviṣayibhiḥ,
asamasamabuddhajñānābhiṣekābhiṣiktaiḥ, daśabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmādhyāśayagataiḥ sarvāpāyadurgativinipātotkṣiptaparikhaiḥ, saṃcintyabhavagatyupapattisaṃdarśayitṛbhiḥ, mahāvaidyarājaiḥ, sarvasatvavinayavidhijñaiḥ, yathārhadharmabhaiṣajyaprayogaprayuktaiḥ, anantaguṇākarasamanvāgataiḥ, anantabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasamalaṃkṛtaiḥ, amoghaśravaṇadarśanaiḥ, amoghapadavikramaiḥ, aparimitakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraguṇaparikīrtanāparyantaguṇaughaiḥ /
body.translated_text:
(Vkn 1.3) and with thirty-two thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, recognized through their <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), all accomplished through the practice of the great <s>abhijñās</s>; established through the sustaining power of the <s>Buddhas</s>; guardians of the city of the true <s>Dharma</s>; upholders of the true <s>Dharma</s>; uttering the great lion's roar; their fame resounding in the ten directions; unsolicited spiritual friends of all beings; preservers of the unbroken lineage of the Three Jewels; conquerors of <s>Māra</s> and his adversaries; unconquered by all rival doctrines; endowed with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention); free from all hindrances and secondary defilements; established in unobstructed liberation; with unbreakable eloquence; accomplished in <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), <s>niyama</s> (discipline), <s>saṃyama</s> (control), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means); endowed with the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas) through non-apprehension; turners of the irreversible <s>Dharmacakra</s> (wheel of the Dharma); sealed with the seal of signlessness; skilled in knowing the faculties of all beings; undaunted in the confidence of fearlessness before all assemblies; enriched by the great accumulation of merit and knowledge; their bodies adorned with the [thirty-two] marks and [eighty] secondary characteristics; bearers of supreme beauty; having transcended [need for] ornaments; with fame and renown risen higher than the peak of <s>Meru</s>; having obtained unbreakable faith in the <s>Buddha-dharma</s> through diamond-firm resolve; raining down the nectar-water that distributes the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>; their voices pure among all sounds, utterances, tones, and resonances of all beings; having entered the depths of profound <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and cut off the continuity of all views, infinite and endless; with fearless roars like lions; having transcended the equal and the unequal; great caravan-leaders who bring forth the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s> through wisdom; skilled in all <s>dharmas</s> that are straight, subtle, soft, difficult to see, and difficult to understand; having entered the domain of knowledge that penetrates the dispositions, intentions, and minds of beings;
anointed with the consecration of the wisdom of the <s>Buddhas</s>, equal to the unequaled; having entered the aspiration toward the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), the [four] fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and the unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>); with moats raised against all miserable states, evil destinies, and downfalls; manifesting birth in various realms of existence by deliberate intention; great kings of physicians; knowing the methods for disciplining all beings; applying the appropriate medicine of the <s>Dharma</s> as suitable; endowed with an inexhaustible mine of virtues; adorned with the splendid array of virtues of immeasurable <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields); whose sight and hearing are never in vain; whose steps are never purposeless; with a flood of virtues whose enumeration is inexhaustible even through hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of <s>kalpas</s> (eons).

body.text: Vkn 1.4 tadyathā samadarśinā ca nāma bodhisatvena mahāsatvena samaviṣamadarśinā ca, samādhivikurvaṇarājena ca, dharmeśvareṇa ca, dharmaketunā ca, prabhāketunā ca, prabhāvyūhena ca, mahāvyūhena ca, ratnakūṭena ca, pratibhānakūṭena ca, ratnamudrāhastena ca, nityotkṣiptahastena ca, nityotpalakṛtahastena ca, nityotkaṇṭhitena ca, nityaprahasitapramuditendriyeṇa ca, prāmodyarājena ca, devarājena ca, praṇidhiprayātaprāptena ca, pratisaṃvitpraṇādaprāptena ca, gaganagañjena ca, ratnolkādhāriṇā ca, ratnavīreṇa ca, ratnaśriyā ca, ratnanandinā ca, indrajālinā ca, jāliniprabheṇa ca, anāraṃbaṇadhyāyinā ca, prajñākūṭena ca, ratnajahena ca, mārapramardinā ca, vidyuddevena ca, vikurvaṇarājena ca, lakṣaṇakūṭena ca, lakṣaṇakūṭasamatikrāntena ca, siṃhaghoṣābhigarjitasvareṇa ca, śailaśikharasaṃghaṭṭanarājena ca, gandhahastinā ca, gajagandhahastinā ca, satatodyuktena ca, anikṣiptadhureṇa ca, sumatinā ca, sujātena ca, padmaśrīgarbheṇa ca, padmavyūhena ca, avalokiteśvareṇa ca, mahāsthāmaprāptena ca, brahmajālinā ca, ratnayaṣṭinā ca, mārajitena ca, kṣetrālaṃkṛtena ca, maṇiratnacchatreṇa ca, suvarṇacūḍena ca, maṇicūḍena ca, maitreyeṇa ca, mañjuśriyā ca kumārabhūtena bodhisatvena mahāsatvena, evaṃpramukhair dvātriṃśatā bodhisatvasahasraiḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.4) Namely: the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Samadarśin</s> (Equal-Seeing), <s>Samaviṣamadarśin</s> (Equal-and-Unequal-Seeing), <s>Samādhivikurvaṇarāja</s> (King of Samādhi Transformations), <s>Dharmeśvara</s> (Lord of Dharma), <s>Dharmaketu</s> (Banner of Dharma), <s>Prabhāketu</s> (Banner of Radiance), <s>Prabhāvyūha</s> (Array of Radiance), <s>Mahāvyūha</s> (Great Array), <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> (Jewel-Peak), <s>Pratibhānakūṭa</s> (Peak of Eloquence), <s>Ratnamudrāhasta</s> (Jewel-Seal Hand), <s>Nityotkṣiptahasta</s> (Ever-Raised Hand), <s>Nityotpalakṛtahasta</s> (Ever-Lotus-in-Hand), <s>Nityotkaṇṭhita</s> (Ever-Yearning), <s>Nityaprahasitapramuditendriya</s> (Ever-Smiling with Joyful Faculties), <s>Prāmodyarāja</s> (King of Delight), <s>Devarāja</s> (King of Gods), <s>Praṇidhiprayātaprāpta</s> (Attained through the Course of Vows), <s>Pratisaṃvitpraṇādaprāpta</s> (Attained through the Roar of Analytical Knowledge), <s>Gaganagañja</s> (Sky-Treasury), <s>Ratnolkādhārin</s> (Jewel-Torch Bearer), <s>Ratnavīra</s> (Jewel-Hero), <s>Ratnaśrī</s> (Jewel-Glory), <s>Ratnananda</s> (Jewel-Joy), <s>Indrajālin</s> (Net of Indra), <s>Jāliniprabha</s> (Net-Radiance), <s>Anāraṃbaṇadhyāyin</s> (Meditator without Support), <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> (Peak of Wisdom), <s>Ratnajaha</s> (Jewel-Abandoner), <s>Mārapramardin</s> (Crusher of Māra), <s>Vidyuddeva</s> (Lightning God), <s>Vikurvaṇarāja</s> (King of Transformations), <s>Lakṣaṇakūṭa</s> (Peak of Marks), <s>Lakṣaṇakūṭasamatikrānta</s> (Transcender of the Peak of Marks), <s>Siṃhaghoṣābhigarjitasvara</s> (Voice of the Lion's Thunderous Roar), <s>Śailaśikharasaṃghaṭṭanarāja</s> (King of Mountain-Peak Collision), <s>Gandhahasti</s> (Fragrant Elephant), <s>Gajagandhahasti</s> (Elephant-Fragrant Elephant), <s>Satatodyukta</s> (Ever-Zealous), <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s> (Never-Abandoning the Yoke), <s>Sumati</s> (Good-Minded), <s>Sujāta</s> (Well-Born), <s>Padmaśrīgarbha</s> (Lotus-Glory Womb), <s>Padmavyūha</s> (Lotus Array), <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, <s>Brahmajālin</s> (Brahmā's Net), <s>Ratnayaṣṭi</s> (Jewel-Staff), <s>Mārajita</s> (Conqueror of Māra), <s>Kṣetrālaṃkṛta</s> (Field-Adorner), <s>Maṇiratnacchattra</s> (Jewel-Gem Parasol), <s>Suvarṇacūḍa</s> (Golden Crest), <s>Maṇicūḍa</s> (Jewel Crest), <s>Maitreya</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful — headed by these, thirty-two thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: Vkn 1.5 daśabhiś ca brahmasahasrair jaṭibrahmapramukhaiḥ, anekāc caturmahādvīpakāl lokadhātor abhyāgatair bhagavato darśanāyai vandanāyai paryupāsanāyai dharmaśravaṇāya ca / te tatraiva parṣadi saṃnipatitāḥ / dvādaśa ca śakrasahasrāṇy anyānyebhyaś caturmahādvīpakebhyo 'bhyāgatāni tatraiva parṣadi saṃnipatitāny abhūvan / tathānye 'pi maheśākhyamaheśākhyāḥ śakrabrahmalokapāladevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragās tatraiva parṣadi saṃnipatitā abhūvan saṃnisaṇṇāḥ / tathā catasraḥ parṣado bhikṣubhiksūṇyupāsakopāsikāś copasaṃkrāntā abhūvan /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.5) And ten thousand <s>Brahmās</s>, headed by <s>Jaṭibrahmā</s> (the Matted-Hair Brahmā), who had come from many world-systems of four great continents, for the purpose of seeing, honoring, attending upon, and hearing the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s>. They had gathered together in that very assembly. And twelve thousand <s>Śakras</s> (Indras), who had come from other world-systems of four great continents, had also gathered together in that very assembly. Likewise, other great lords and minor lords — <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), <s>Devas</s> (gods), <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>Asuras</s> (titans), <s>Garuḍas</s> (eagle-beings), <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> (great serpents) — had also gathered together and were seated in that very assembly. Likewise, the four assemblies — <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (laymen), and <s>upāsikās</s> (laywomen) — had also approached.

body.text: Vkn 1.6 tatra bhagavān anekaśatasahasrayā parṣadā parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayati sma / sumerur iva parvatarājaḥ sāgaramadhyād abhyudgataḥ sarvaparṣadam abhibhūya bhāsate tapati virocate śrīgarbhe siṃhāsane niṣaṇnaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.6) There the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded and honored by an assembly of many hundreds of thousands, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Like Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, risen from the midst of the ocean, outshining the entire assembly, he blazed, shone, and radiated, seated upon a lion-throne within the shrine of <s>Śrī</s> (glory).

body.text: Vkn 1.7 atha ratnākaro bodhisatvo licchavikumāraḥ sārdhaṃ pañcamātrair licchavikumāraśataiḥ saptaratnamayāni cchatrāṇi gṛhītvā vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ niṣkramya yenāmrapālīvanaṃ yena ca bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ saptakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathā parigṛhītais taiś chatrair bhagavantam abhicchādayati sma / abhicchādyaikānte sthito 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.7) Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ratnākara</s>, a <s>Licchavi</s> youth, together with approximately five hundred <s>Licchavi</s> youths, taking parasols made of the seven precious substances, went forth from the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> and approached <s>Āmrapālī</s>'s grove and the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> seven times, and covered the <s>Bhagavān</s> with those parasols that he had brought. Having covered him, he stood to one side.

body.text: Vkn 1.8 samantaraniḥsṛṣṭāni ca tāni ratnacchatrāṇy atha tāvad eva buddhānubhāvenaikaṃ mahāratnacchatraṃ saṃsthitam / tena ca mahāratnacchatreṇāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ sarvaḥ saṃchāditaḥ saṃdṛśyate sma / yaś cāsmiṃs trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātāv āyāmavistāraḥ, sa tasmin mahāratnacchatre saṃdṛśyate sma / ye ceha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sumeravo mahāparvatarājā himavanmucilindamahāmucilindagandhamādanaratnaparvatā vā cakravāḍamahācakravāḍāḥ, te 'pi sarve tasminn evaikamahāratnacchatre saṃdṛśyante sma / ye 'pīha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau mahāsamudrā vā sarastaḍāgāni vā nadīkunadyaḥ sravantyo vā pravahanti, tā api sarvās tasminn evaikamahāratnacchatre saṃdṛśyante sma / yāny apīha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sūryācandramasāṃ vimānāni tārārūpāṇi vā devabhavanāni vā nāgabhavanāni vā yakṣabhavanāni vā gandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragabhavanāni vā cāturmahārājabhavanāni vā grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānyo vā, tāny api sarvāṇi tasminn evaikamahāratnacchatre saṃdṛśyante sma / yāpi ca daśadiśi loke buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā pravartate, sāpi tasmād evaikamahāratnacchatrān niścarantī śrūyate sma /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.8) And when those jeweled parasols had been released simultaneously, then at that very moment, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, they merged into a single great jeweled parasol. And under that great jeweled parasol, this entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world system) was seen to be covered. And whatever is the length and breadth of this billion-world system, that was seen within that great jeweled parasol. And whatever great mountain-kings <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Himavat</s>, <s>Mucilinda</s>, <s>Mahāmucilinda</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>, <s>Ratnaparvata</s>, <s>Cakravāḍa</s>, and <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s> exist in this billion-world system — all those too were seen within that single great jeweled parasol. And whatever great oceans, lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, and flowing waters exist in this billion-world system — all those too were seen within that single great jeweled parasol. And whatever palaces of the sun and moon, constellations, star-forms, divine abodes, <s>Nāga</s>-abodes, <s>Yakṣa</s>-abodes, <s>Gandharva</s>-abodes, <s>Asura</s>-abodes, <s>Garuḍa</s>-abodes, <s>Kinnara</s>-abodes, <s>Mahoraga</s>-abodes, <s>Cāturmahārāja</s>-abodes, or villages, towns, market-towns, kingdoms, and capital cities exist in this billion-world system — all those too were seen within that single great jeweled parasol. And whatever <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, was being proclaimed in the ten directions of the world — that too was heard issuing from that single great jeweled parasol.

body.text: Vkn 1.9 tatra sā sarvā parṣad āścaryaprāptā bhagavato 'ntikād idam evaṃrūpaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭodagrāttamanāḥ pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā tathāgataṃ namasyatī sthitānimiṣaṃ prekṣamāṇā /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.9) Then that entire assembly, having witnessed this extraordinary great miracle from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, was delighted, elated, uplifted in mind, joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, and stood worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s>, gazing without blinking.

body.text: Vkn 1.10 atha khalu ratnākaro licchavikumāro bhagavato 'ntikād idam evaṃrūpaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvaikāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir abhyaṣṭāvīt:
body.translated_text: Vkn 1.10 Then the Licchavi youth <s>Ratnākara</s>, having seen this great miraculous display from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms in the direction of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

body.text: śubhaśuddhakamalavarapatraviśālanetra śuddhāśayā śamathapāramitāgraprāpta / śubhakarmasaṃcaya viśālaguṇāprameya vandāmi tvāṃ śramaṇaśāntipathapraṇetum // 1 //
body.translated_text: O you whose broad eyes are like the petals of a pure and beautiful lotus, whose intentions are purified, who have reached the highest <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection), who have accumulated excellent deeds, whose vast virtues are immeasurable — I bow to you, the guide on the path of ascetic peace. // 1 //

children.text: paśyatha ṛddhi puruṣarṣabhanāyakasya saṃdṛśyate sugatakṣetravaraprakāśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Behold the miraculous power of this bull among men, the leader! The radiant displays of the excellent <s>Sugata</s>-fields appear,

children.text: amṛtaṃgamā ca varadharmakathā udārā sā sarva śrūyati ito gaganatalātaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: and the sublime teaching of the excellent <s>Dharma</s>, leading to the deathless, is heard everywhere from the vault of the sky. // 2 //

children.text: dharmeṇa te jitam idaṃ varadharmarājyaṃ dharmaṃ dhanaṃ ca dadase jagato jitāre /
children.translated_text: By <s>Dharma</s> you have conquered this excellent kingdom of <s>Dharma</s>; you give <s>Dharma</s> and wealth to the world, O conqueror.

children.text: dharmaprabhedakuśalaṃ paramārthadarśin dharmeśvaraṃ śirasi vandami dharmarājam // 3 //
children.translated_text: Skilled in the analysis of <s>Dharma</s>, seer of the ultimate truth — I bow my head to the lord of <s>Dharma</s>, the king of <s>Dharma</s>. // 3 //

children.text: na ca nāma asti na ca nāsti giraṃ prabhāṣi hetuṃ pratītya imi saṃbhavi sarvadharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: You teach that things neither truly exist nor do not exist; all <s>dharmas</s> arise dependent on causes.

children.text: naivātra ātmana ca kāraku vedako vā na ca karmu naśyati śubham aśubhaṃ ca kiṃcit // 4 //
children.translated_text: There is herein neither a self, nor an agent, nor an experiencer, yet no action, whether good or bad, ever perishes. // 4 //

children.text: māras tvayāstu vijitas sabalo munīndraḥ prāptā śivā amṛtaśāntavarāgrabodhiḥ /
children.translated_text: O chief of sages, <s>Māra</s> together with his forces has been conquered by you; the blessed, deathless, peaceful, supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) has been attained,

children.text: yasminn avedita na cittamanaḥpracārā sarvakutīrthikagaṇāś ca na yānti gāhaṃ // 5 //
children.translated_text: wherein the movements of mind and thought are not apprehended, and all the hosts of non-Buddhist teachers cannot fathom it. // 5 //

children.text: cakraṃ ca te triparivarti bahuprakāraṃ prāvartitaṃ praśamanaṃ prakṛtīviśuddham /
children.translated_text: The wheel has been turned by you in three revolutions, of many kinds, bringing pacification, pure by nature,

children.text: pratyakṣa devamanujādbhutadharmarājā ratnāni trīṇi upadarśita tatra kāle // 6 //
children.translated_text: and in the presence of gods and humans, O wondrous king of <s>Dharma</s>, the three jewels were revealed at that time. // 6 //

children.text: ye tubhya dharmaratanena vinīta samyak teṣām akalpana punaḥ satate praśāntā /
children.translated_text: Those who have been properly trained by your jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, for them conceptual fabrication is forever pacified.

children.text: vaidyottamaṃ maraṇajātijarāntakāriṃ śirasā nato 'smi guṇasāgaram aprameyam // 7 //
children.translated_text: I bow my head to the supreme physician who puts an end to death, birth, and old age — the immeasurable ocean of virtues. // 7 //

children.text: satkārasatkṛta na vedhasi merukalpa duḥśīlaśīlavati tulyagatādhimaitrī /
children.translated_text: You are not moved by honor or dishonor, steady as <s>Meru</s>; your loving-kindness extends equally to the immoral and the virtuous.

children.text: gaganaprakāśamanase samatāvihārī ko nāma satvaratane 'smi na kuryu pūjām // 8 //
children.translated_text: Dwelling in equanimity, with a mind like the open sky — who would not make offerings to this jewel among beings? // 8 //

children.text: samāgatā te janatā mahāmune mukham udīkṣanti prasannamānasā /
children.translated_text: The people have gathered, O great sage, and gaze upon your face with joyful minds.

children.text: sarve ca paśyanti jinaṃ purastāj jinasya āveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // 9 //
children.translated_text: And all behold the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) before them — this is the distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-characteristic of the <s>Jina</s>. // 9 //

children.text: ekāṃ ca vācaṃ bhagavān pramuñcase nānārutaṃ ca pariṣad vijānati /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> utters a single speech, yet the assembly understands it in diverse languages,

children.text: yathāsvakaṃ cārtha vijānate jano jinasya āveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // 10 //
children.translated_text: and each person comprehends the meaning according to their own capacity — this is the distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-characteristic of the <s>Jina</s>. // 10 //

children.text: ekāya vācāya udīritāya vāsesi eke apare nividyasi /
children.translated_text: By a single utterance, some you inspire with confidence, others you cause to feel a sense of spiritual urgency,

children.text: ākāṅkṣatāṃ kāṅkṣa śamesir nāyako jinasya āveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // 11 //
children.translated_text: and for those who are in doubt, O leader, you bring their doubts to rest — this is the distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-characteristic of the <s>Jina</s>. // 11 //

children.text: vandāmi tvāṃ daśabala satyavikramaṃ vandāmi tvām abhayagataṃ viśāradam /
children.translated_text: I bow to you, O possessor of the ten powers, whose valor is truth; I bow to you who have attained fearlessness, who are confident.

children.text: dharmeṣu āveṇikaniścayaṃ gataṃ vandāmi tvāṃ sarvajagatpraṇāyakam // 12 //
children.translated_text: I bow to you who have reached certainty in the distinctive <s>dharmas</s>; I bow to you, the guide of all the world. // 12 //

children.text: vandāmi samyojanabandhanacchidaṃ vandāmi tvāṃ pāragataṃ sthale sthitam /
children.translated_text: I bow to the cutter of the bonds and fetters; I bow to you who have gone beyond and stand on firm ground.

children.text: vandāmi khinnasya janasya tārakaṃ vandāmi saṃsāragatāv aniśritam // 13 //
children.translated_text: I bow to the rescuer of weary beings; I bow to you who do not dwell in the course of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). // 13 //

children.text: satvair samādhānagataṃ gatīgatam gatīṣu sarvāsu vimuktamānasam /
children.translated_text: You have gone among beings in meditative absorption, entering all realms of existence yet with a mind completely liberated.

children.text: jaleruhaṃ vā salile na lipyase niṣevitā te munipadma śūnyatā // 14 //
children.translated_text: Like a lotus in water, you are unstained — O sage-lotus, you have cultivated <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). // 14 //

children.text: vibhāvitā sarvanimitta sarvaśo na te kahiṃcit praṇidhāna vidyate /
children.translated_text: All conceptual signs have been thoroughly transcended; you have no attachment to any object whatsoever.

children.text: acintiyaṃ buddhamahānubhāvaṃ vande 'ham ākāśasamam aniśritam // 15 //
children.translated_text: I bow to the inconceivable great power of the <s>Buddha</s>, equal to space, without any support. // 15 //

body.text: Vkn 1.11 atha ratnākaro licchavikumāro bhagavantam ābhir gāthābhir abhiṣṭutya bhagavantam etad avocat: imāni bhagavan pañcamātrāṇi licchavikumāraśatāni sarvāṇy anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāni / tāni cemāni buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ paripṛcchanti ḥ katamā bodhisatvānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhir iti / tat sādhu bhagavan deśayatu tathāgato 'mīṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhim /
body.translated_text: Vkn 1.11 Then the Licchavi youth <s>Ratnākara</s>, having praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these verses, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Bhagavān</s>, these five hundred Licchavi youths have all set out toward unsurpassed <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect complete awakening). They wish to inquire about the purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field): What is the purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>? May the <s>Bhagavān</s> please teach these <s>bodhisattvas</s> about the purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>."

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān ratnākarāya licchavikumārāya sādhukāram adāt: sādhu sādhu kumāra / sādhu khalu punas tvaṃ kumāra yas tvaṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhim ārabhya tathāgataṃ paripṛcchasi / tena hi kumāra śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te yathā bodhisatvānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhim ārabhya /
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave his approval to the Licchavi youth <s>Ratnākara</s>: "Excellent, excellent, young man! It is truly excellent that you ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about the purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field). Therefore, young man, listen well and attend carefully. I shall explain to you the purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>."

body.text: sādhu bhagavann iti ratnākaro licchavikumāras tāni ca pañcamātrāṇi licchavikumāraśatāni bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ /
body.translated_text: "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," replied the Licchavi youth <s>Ratnākara</s>, and those five hundred Licchavi youths listened attentively to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: bhagavāṃs teṣām etad avocat:
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to them:

body.text: Vkn 1.12 satvakṣetraṃ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram / tat kasya hetoḥ / yāvantaṃ bodhisatvaḥ satveṣūpacayaṃ karoti tāvad buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇāti / yādṛśaḥ satvānāṃ vinayo bhavati tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhnāti / yādṛśena buddhakṣetrāvatāreṇa satvā buddhajñānam avataranti tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhnāti / yādṛśena buddhakṣetrāvatāreṇa satvānām āryākārāṇīndriyāṇy utpadyante tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇāti / tat kasya hetoḥ / satvārthanirjātaṃ hi kulaputra bodhisatvānāṃ buddhakṣetram / tadyathā ratnākara yādṛśam icched ākāśaṃ māpayituṃ tādṛśaṃ māpayeta, na cākāśaṃ śakyate māpayituṃ nāpy alaṃkartum / evam eva ratnākara ākāśasamān sarvadharmāñ jñātvā / yādṛśam icched bodhisatvaḥ satvaparipākāya buddhakṣetraṃ māpayituṃ tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ māpayati, na ca buddhakṣetrākāśatā śakyaṃ māpayituṃ nāpy alaṃkartum /
body.translated_text: Vkn 1.12 "The field of sentient beings, son of good family, is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field) of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Why is that? To the extent that a <s>bodhisattva</s> accumulates merit among sentient beings, to that extent does he embrace his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>. According to the manner of disciplining sentient beings, so does he embrace his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>. According to the kind of entry into the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> through which sentient beings enter <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, so does he embrace his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>. According to the kind of entry into the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> through which the noble faculties of sentient beings arise, so does he embrace his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>. Why is that? Because, son of good family, the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> arises from the purpose of benefiting sentient beings. For example, <s>Ratnākara</s>, if one wished to build in empty space, one could build as one wished, yet empty space can neither be built upon nor adorned. In just the same way, <s>Ratnākara</s>, knowing all <s>dharmas</s> to be like empty space, a <s>bodhisattva</s> may construct a <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> for the maturation of sentient beings however he wishes, yet the space-like nature of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> can neither be constructed nor adorned."

body.text: Vkn 1.13 api ca ratnākara,
body.translated_text: Vkn 1.13 "Furthermore, <s>Ratnākara</s>,

body.text: āśayakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasyāśaṭhā amāyāvinaḥ satvā buddhakṣetra upapadyante /
body.translated_text: the field of intention is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field) of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), beings who are sincere and without deceit are reborn in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: adhyāśayakṣetraṃ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvakuśalasaṃbhāropacitāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The field of superior intention, son of good family, is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who have accumulated all roots of wholesome merit are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: prayogakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvakuśaladharmopasthitāḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetra upapadyante /
body.translated_text: The field of practice is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who are established in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are reborn in that <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: udāro bodhisatvasya bodhicittotpādo buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya mahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The exalted arising of the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicittotpāda</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> is his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who have set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) are born in that <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: dānakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvaparityāginaḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The field of generosity (<s>dāna</s>) is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who relinquish everything are born in that <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: śīlakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvābhiprāyasaṃpannā daśakuśalakarmapathasaṃrakṣakāḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The field of moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>) is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who are endowed with all good intentions and who guard the ten wholesome courses of action are born in that <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: kṣāntikṣetraṃ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya dvātriṃśallakṣanālaṃkṛtāḥ kṣāntidamaśamathapāramiprāptāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The field of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), son of good family, is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who are adorned with the thirty-two marks and who have attained the perfection of patience, self-control, and tranquility are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: vīryakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvakuśalaparyeṣṭiṣv ārabdhavīryāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The field of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who have exerted vigorous effort in the pursuit of all wholesome qualities are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: dhyānakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya smṛtisaṃprajanyasamāhitāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The field of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who are concentrated through mindfulness and clear comprehension are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: prajñākṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya samyaktvaniyatāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The field of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who are fixed in the certainty of the correct path are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: catvāry apramāṇāni ca bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāvihārinaḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) are the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who abide in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: catvāri saṃgrahavastūni kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvavimuktisaṃgṛhītāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), son of good family, are the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who are embraced by all forms of liberation are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: upāyakauśalyaṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvopāyamīmāṃsākuśalāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: Skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) is the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>; when he attains <s>bodhi</s>, beings who are skilled in the investigation of all expedient methods are born in his <s>buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣā dharmā bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya samyaksmṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgavidhijñāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment (<s>saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣā dharmāḥ</s>) are the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field); when he attains enlightenment, beings who know the methods of the right applications of mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛtyupasthāna</s>), right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), bases of psychic power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), strengths (<s>bala</s>), limbs of enlightenment (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and the path (<s>mārga</s>) are born in his <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.

body.text: pariṇāmanācittaṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvaguṇālaṃkāraṃ buddhakṣetraṃ dṛśyate /
body.translated_text: The dedication of merit (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>) of the mind is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; when he attains enlightenment, a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> adorned with all virtues is seen.

body.text: aṣṭākṣaṇapraśamadeśanā kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvāpāyasamucchinnam aṣṭākṣaṇavigataṃ buddhakṣetraṃ saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: Teaching the pacification of the eight inopportune states (<s>aṣṭākṣaṇa</s>), O son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; when he attains enlightenment, a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> with all miserable states completely cut off and free from the eight inopportune states comes into being.

body.text: svayaṃ śikṣāpadeṣu vartamānā parāpattyacodanatā bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasyāpattiśabdo 'pi buddhakṣetre na saṃbhavati /
body.translated_text: Abiding in the training rules oneself while not charging others with offenses is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; when he attains enlightenment, even the word 'offense' (<s>āpatti</s>) does not exist in his <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.

body.text: daśakuśalakarmapathapariśuddhiḥ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram, tasya bodhiprāptasya niyatāyuṣo mahābhogā brahmacāriṇaḥ satyānuparivartinyā vācālaṃkṛtā madhuravacanā abhinnaparṣado bhinnasaṃdhānakuśalā īrṣyāvigatā avyāpannacittāḥ samyagdṛṣṭisamanvāgatāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
body.translated_text: The purification of the ten paths of wholesome action (<s>daśakuśalakarmapatha</s>), O son of good family, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; when he attains enlightenment, beings with fixed lifespan, great wealth, practicing celibacy (<s>brahmacārya</s>), adorned with speech that accords with truth, sweet-spoken, with undivided assemblies, skilled in reconciling the divided, free from envy, with unimpaired minds, endowed with right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) are born in his <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.

body.text: Vkn 1.14 iti hi kulaputra, yāvanto bodhisatvasya prayogās tāvanta āśayāḥ / yāvanta āśayās tāvanto 'dhyāśayāḥ / yāvanto 'dhyāśayās tāvantyo nidhyaptayaḥ / yāvantyo nidhyaptayas tāvantyaḥ pratipattayaḥ / yāvantyaḥ pratipattayas tāvantyaḥ pariṇāmanāḥ / yāvantyaḥ pariṇāmanās tāvanta upāyāḥ / yāvanta upāyās tāvantyaḥ kṣetrapariśuddhayaḥ / yādṛśī kṣetrapariśuddhis tādṛśī satvapariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī satvapariśuddhis tādṛśī jñānapariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī jñānapariśuddhis tādṛśī deśanāpariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī deśanāpariśuddhis tādṛśī jñānapratipattipariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī jñānapratipattipariśuddhis tādṛśī svacittapariśuddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.14) Thus, O son of good family, as many as are the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s applications (<s>prayoga</s>), so many are his intentions (<s>āśaya</s>); as many as are his intentions, so many are his higher intentions (<s>adhyāśaya</s>); as many as his higher intentions, so many are his resolves (<s>nidhyapti</s>); as many as his resolves, so many are his practices (<s>pratipatti</s>); as many as his practices, so many are his dedications (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>); as many as his dedications, so many are his skillful means (<s>upāya</s>); as many as his skillful means, so many are his field-purifications; as is his field-purification, so is his purification of beings; as is his purification of beings, so is his purification of knowledge; as is his purification of knowledge, so is his purification of teaching; as is his purification of teaching, so is his purification of the practice of knowledge; as is his purification of the practice of knowledge, so is his own mind-purification.

body.text: tasmāt tarhi kulaputra buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhayitukāmena bodhisatvena svacittapariśodhane yatnaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ / yādṛśī bodhisatvasya cittapariśuddhis tādṛśī buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ saṃbhavati /
body.translated_text: Therefore then, O son of good family, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to purify the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should make effort in the purification of his own mind. What is the reason? As is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s mind-purification, so arises the purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.

body.text: Vkn 1.15 atha buddhānubhāvenāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat: yadi yādṛśī cittapariśuddhis tādṛśī bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ saṃbhavati, tan mā āhaiva bhagavataḥ śākyamuner bodhisatvacaryāṃ carataś cittam apariśuddhaṃ yenedaṃ buddhakṣetram evam apariśuddhaṃ saṃdṛśyate /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.15) Then, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, this thought arose in the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: If as is the mind-purification, so arises the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, then surely the mind of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> was impure while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s>-career, since this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> appears so impure!

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram etad avocat: tat kiṃ manyase, śāriputra mā āhaiva sūryācandramasāv apariśuddhau yaj jātyandho na paśyati /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing through his mind the mental deliberation of the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>? Is it because the sun and moon are impure that one born blind does not see them?

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ bhagavan jātyandhāparādha eṣa na sūryacandramasoḥ /
body.translated_text: He said: No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. This is the fault of the one born blind, not of the sun and moon.

body.text: āha: evam eva śāriputra satvānām ajñānāparādha eṣa yas tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhaṃ kecit satvā na paśyanti, na tatra tathāgatasyāparādhaḥ / pariśuddhaṃ hi śāriputra tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraṃ yūyaṃ punar idaṃ na paśyatha /
body.translated_text: He said: Just so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is the fault of the ignorance of beings that some beings do not see the splendid array of virtues adorning the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>buddhakṣetra</s>; the fault is not the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s. For the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is pure, <s>Śāriputra</s>, but you do not see it.

body.text: Vkn 1.16 atha khalu jaṭī brahmā sthaviraṃ śāriputram etad avocat: mā bhadantaśāriputra tathāgatasyāpariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetram idaṃ vyāhārṣīt / pariśuddhaṃ hi bhadantaśāriputra bhagavato buddhakṣetram / tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra vaśavartināṃ devānāṃ bhavanavyūhāḥ / īdṛśān vayaṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ paśyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.16) Then the matted-hair <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Jaṭī</s>) said to the elder <s>Śāriputra</s>: Do not, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, declare this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be impure! For the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is pure, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, are the palace-arrays of the <s>Vaśavartin</s> gods — so do we see the arrays of the virtues of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sthaviraḥ śāriputro jaṭinaṃ brahmāṇam etad avocat: vayaṃ punar brahmann imāṃ mahāpṛthivīm utkūlanikūlāṃ kaṇṭakaprapātagiriśekharaśvabhragūthoḍigallapratipūrṇāṃ paśyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the matted-hair <s>Brahmā</s>: But we, O <s>Brahmā</s>, see this great earth full of ups and downs, thorns, precipices, mountain-peaks, chasms, and filled with dung.

body.text: jaṭī brahmāha: nūnaṃ bhadantaśāriputrasyotkūlanikūlaṃ cittam apariśuddhabuddhajñānāśayaṃ yenedṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ paśyasi / ye punas te bhadantaśāriputra bodhisatvāḥ sarvasatvasamacittāḥ pariśuddhabuddhajñānāśayās ta imaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pariśuddhaṃ paśyanti /
body.translated_text: The matted-hair <s>Brahmā</s> said: Because your mind, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, has ups and downs and is impure in its disposition toward <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, you see this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> in this way. But those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, who have equanimous minds toward all beings and pure dispositions toward <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge — they see this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> as pure.

body.text: Vkn 1.17 atha bhagavān pādāṅguṣṭhena imaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ parāhanti sma / atha khalu tasmin samaye 'yaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur anekaratnaśatasahasrasaṃcito 'nekaratnaśatasahasrapratyarpitaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt / tadyathāpi nāma ratnavyūhasya tathāgatasyānantaguṇaratnavyūho lokadhātus tādṛśo 'yaṃ lokadhātuḥ saṃdṛśyate sma / tatra sā sarvāvatī parṣad āścaryaprāptā ratnapadmaniṣaṇnam ātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.17) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> pressed this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world system) with his toe. At that moment, this billion-world system appeared studded with many hundreds of thousands of jewels, adorned with many hundreds of thousands of jewels. Just as the world-system of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnavyūha</s> has arrays of infinite precious jewels, so this world-system appeared. Then that entire assembly, filled with wonder, recognized itself as seated upon jeweled lotus-seats.

body.text: Vkn 1.18 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma: paśyasi tvaṃ śāriputra imān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.18) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: Do you see, <s>Śāriputra</s>, these arrays of the virtues of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>?

body.text: āha: paśyāmi bhagavan adṛṣṭāśrutapūrvā ime vyūhāḥ saṃdṛśyante /
body.translated_text: He said: I see them, <s>Bhagavān</s>! These arrays appear as never before seen or heard.

body.text: āha: īdṛśaṃ mama śāriputra sadā buddhakṣetram / hīnasatvaparipākāya tu tathāgata evaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭaṃ buddhakṣetram upadarśayati / tadyathā śāriputra devaputrāṇām ekapātryāṃ bhuñjānānāṃ yathā puṇyopacayaviśeṣeṇa sudhādevabhojanam upatiṣṭhataḥ, evam eva śāriputra ekabuddhakṣetropapannā yathā cittapariśuddhyā satvā buddhānāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān paśyanti /
body.translated_text: He said: My <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is always like this. But for the ripening of beings of inferior dispositions, the <s>Tathāgata</s> displays the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> as polluted with many faults. Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the divine food of ambrosia (<s>sudhā</s>) appears to the <s>devaputras</s> as they eat from a single bowl according to their respective merit, so too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, beings born in a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s> see the arrays of virtues of the <s>Buddhas</s>' <s>buddhakṣetras</s> according to the purity of their minds.

body.text: Vkn 1.19 asmin khalu punar buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhālaṃkāre saṃdarśyamāne caturaśīteḥ prāṇisahasrāṇām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni / yāni ca tāni ratnākareṇa licchavikumāreṇa sārdhaṃ pañca licchavikumāraśatāny āgatāni teṣām apy ānulomikyāḥ kṣānteḥ pratilaṃbho 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.19) When this display of the arrays of the adornments of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>'s virtues was being shown, eighty-four thousand beings generated the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And those five hundred <s>Licchavi</s> youths who had come together with the <s>Licchavi</s> youth <s>Ratnākara</s> also attained the acceptance of conformity (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>).

body.text: Vkn 1.20 atha bhagavān punar eva tām ṛddhiṃ pratisaṃharati sma / tataḥ punar evedaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ tatsvabhāvam eva saṃvṛtam, tatra śrāvakayānikānāṃ devamanuṣyāṇām ḥ anityā bateme sarvasaṃskārā iti viditvā dvātriṃśatā prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ virajovigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur viśuddham / aṣṭānāṃ ca bhikṣusahasrāṇām anupādāyāsravebhyaś cittāni vimuktāni / caturaśīteś ca prāṇisahasrāṇām udārabuddhadharmādhimuktānāṃ Ō viṭhapanapratyupasthānalakṣaṇāḥ sarvadharmā iti viditvānuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni // //
body.translated_text: (Vkn 1.20) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> withdrew that supernatural display (<s>ṛddhi</s>). Then this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> returned to its own natural state. Then, for those gods and humans of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, understanding that 'All conditioned things (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are impermanent,' thirty-two thousand beings had the dust-free, stain-free <s>Dharmacakṣus</s> (Dharma-eye) purified regarding <s>dharmas</s>. And for eight thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>, their minds were liberated from the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) without further clinging. And for eighty-four thousand beings with noble aspiration toward the <s>Buddhadharma</s>, understanding that 'All <s>dharmas</s> have the characteristic of being liable to decay,' the minds of supreme perfect enlightenment arose.

body.text: buddhakṣetrapariśuddhinidānaparivartaḥ prathamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the first chapter: The Purification of the <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-Field).

body.text: Vkn 2.1 tena khalu punaḥ samayena vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ vimalakīrtir nāma licchaviḥ prativasati sma / pūrvajinakṛtādhikāraḥ, avaropitakuśalamūlaḥ, bahubuddhaparyupāsitaḥ, pratilabdhakṣāntikaḥ, labdhapratibhānaḥ, mahābhijñāvikrīḍitaḥ, dhāraṇīpratilabdhaḥ, vaiśāradyaprāptaḥ, nihatamārapratyarthikaḥ, gambhīradharmanayasupraviṣṭaḥ, prajñāpāramitānirjātaḥ, upāyakauśalyagatiṃgataḥ, pratibhānasamanvāgataḥ, satvāśayacaritakuśalaḥ, indriyaparāparajñānaniryātaḥ, yathāpratyarhadharmadeśakaḥ, kṛtaniścayaḥ kṛtaśrama iha mahāyāne, suparīkṣitakarmakārī, buddheryāpathapratiṣṭhitaḥ, sāgaravarabuddhyanupraviṣṭaḥ, sarvabuddhastutastomitapraśaṃsitaḥ, sarvaśakrabrahmalokapālanamaskṛtaḥ, sa satvaparipākāyopāyakauśalyena vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ prativasati sma /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 2.1) At that time, in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, there dwelt a <s>Licchavi</s> named <s>Vimalakīrti</s>. He had served former <s>Jinas</s> (Victors); he had planted roots of virtue; he had attended upon many <s>Buddhas</s>; he had obtained patience (<s>kṣānti</s>); he had attained eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>); he sported with great superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>); he had obtained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retentive power); he had reached fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya</s>); he had defeated <s>Māra</s> and his adversaries; he had entered deeply into the profound method of the <s>Dharma</s>; he had mastered the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>); he had reached the course of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>); he was endowed with eloquence; skilled in the dispositions and conduct of beings; experienced in discerning the superior and inferior faculties of beings; a teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> as befitting the audience; resolute in determination and zealous in effort in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; well-examined in all his actions; established in the deportment of a <s>Buddha</s>; having entered the ocean-like supreme wisdom; praised, extolled, and lauded by all <s>Buddhas</s>; honored by all <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians) — he dwelt in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> through skillful means for the ripening of beings.

body.text: Vkn 2.2 akṣayabhogo daridrānāthasatvasaṃgrahāya / pariśuddhaśīlo duḥśīlasaṃgrahāya / kṣamadamaprāpto duṣṭapraduṣṭavyāpannakrudhacittānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya / uttaptavīryaḥ kusīdānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya / dhyānasmṛtisamādhisthito vibhrāntacittānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya / prajñāniścayaprāpto duḥprajñānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.2 With inexhaustible enjoyments, for the benefit of the poor and destitute beings. With perfectly pure morality, for the benefit of those of bad morality. Having attained patience and self-control, for the benefit of beings whose minds are corrupted, hostile, malicious, and angry. With blazing vigor, for the benefit of lazy beings. Established in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), for the benefit of beings with distracted minds. Having attained the certainty of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), for the benefit of those of poor wisdom.

body.text: Vkn 2.3 avadātavastradhārī śramaṇeryāpathasaṃpannaḥ / gṛhavāsasthitaḥ kāmadhāturūpadhātvārūpyadhātvasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ / bhāryāputradārāṃś ca saṃdarśayati, sadā ca brahmacārī / parivāraparivṛtaś ca bhavati, sadā ca vivekacārī / ābharaṇavibhūṣitaś ca saṃdṛśyate, sadā ca lakṣaṇaparicchinnaḥ / annapānabhojanajīvaḥ saṃdṛśyate, sadā ca dhyānāhāraḥ / sarvadyūtakaraśālāsu ca saṃdṛśyate, dyūtakrīḍāsaktacittāṃś ca satvān paripācayati, sadā cāpramādacārī / sarvapāṣaṇḍapratyeṣakaś ca / buddhe cābhedyāśayaḥ / sarvalaukikalokottaraśāstravidhijñaś ca / sadā ca dharmārāmaratirataḥ / sarvasaṃgaṇikāsu ca saṃdṛśyate, sarvatra cāgrapūjitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.3 He wore white garments yet was endowed with the conduct of a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic). He dwelt as a householder yet was unattached to the realm of desire, the realm of form, and the formless realm. He displayed a wife, sons, and household, yet was always a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate). He was surrounded by an entourage, yet was always one who delighted in solitude. He appeared adorned with ornaments, yet was always distinguished by the [thirty-two] marks. He appeared to live on food and drink, yet always nourished himself on <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). He appeared in all gambling halls, yet matured those beings whose minds were attached to gambling, while himself always practicing diligence. He visited all heterodox teachers, yet his devotion to the <s>Buddha</s> remained unshakeable. He was learned in all worldly and supramundane treatises and sciences, yet always delighted in the joy of the <s>Dharma</s>-garden. He appeared in all public assemblies, yet everywhere received the highest honor.

body.text: Vkn 2.4 dharmavādī ca vṛddhamadhyadahrasahāyakaś ca lokānuvartanāya /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.4 He was a <s>Dharma</s>-speaker and a companion to the old, the middle-aged, and the young, in order to conform to the world.

body.text: sarvavyavahārodyuktaś ca na ca lābhabhogābhilāṣī /
body.translated_text: He was engaged in all worldly transactions, yet had no desire for profit or enjoyment.

body.text: sarvacatvaraśrṅgāṭakeṣu ca saṃdṛśyate sarvasatvavainayikatāyai /
body.translated_text: He appeared at every crossroads and intersection in order to guide all beings.

body.text: rājakāryānupraviṣṭaś ca satvārakṣāyai /
body.translated_text: He entered into the affairs of the king in order to protect beings.

body.text: sarvadharmaśravaṇasāṃkathyeṣu ca saṃdṛśyate hīnayānavicchandanāya mahāyāne samādāpanatayā /
body.translated_text: He appeared at all gatherings for hearing and discussing the <s>Dharma</s>, in order to turn [beings] away from the <s>Hīnayāna</s> (lesser vehicle) and establish them in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle).

body.text: sarvalipiśālāsu copasaṃkrāmati dārakaparipācanāya /
body.translated_text: He visited all writing schools in order to mature the children.

body.text: sarvagaṇikākulāni ca praviśati kāmadoṣasaṃdarśanāya /
body.translated_text: He entered all the houses of courtesans in order to show the dangers of desire.

body.text: sarvakallavālagṛhāṇi ca praviśati smṛtisaṃprajanyopasthāpanāya /
body.translated_text: He entered all the taverns in order to establish <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear awareness).

body.text: Vkn 2.5 śreṣṭhiṣu ca śreṣṭhisaṃmataḥ śreṣṭhadharmārocanatāyai /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.5 Among merchants, he was honored as a leading merchant, in order to inspire them with the highest <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: gṛhapatiṣu ca gṛhapatisaṃmataḥ sarvagrāhodgrahaparicchedāya /
body.translated_text: Among householders, he was honored as a householder, in order to cut off all attachment and grasping.

body.text: kṣatriyeṣu ca kṣatriyasaṃmataḥ kṣāntisauratyabalapratiṣṭhāpanāya /
body.translated_text: Among <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors), he was honored as a <s>kṣatriya</s>, in order to establish patience, gentleness, and strength.

body.text: brāhmaṇeṣu ca brāhmaṇasaṃmato mānamadadarpanirghātanāya /
body.translated_text: Among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, he was honored as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in order to crush pride, conceit, and arrogance.

body.text: āmātyeṣu cāmātyasaṃmataḥ sarvarājakāryasahadharmamyojanāya /
body.translated_text: Among ministers, he was honored as a minister, in order to apply righteous principles to all royal affairs.

body.text: kumāreṣu ca kumārasaṃmato rājabhogaiśvaryābhilāṣavinivartanāya /
body.translated_text: Among princes, he was honored as a prince, in order to turn them away from the desire for royal pleasures and sovereignty.

body.text: antaḥpureṣu ca kāñcukīyasaṃmataḥ strīkumārikāparipācanāya /
body.translated_text: In the inner palace, he was honored as a eunuch-chamberlain, in order to mature the women and maidens.

body.text: Vkn 2.6 prākṛtajanānuvartakaś ca sāmānyapuṇyaviśiṣṭādhyālaṃbanāya /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.6 He conformed to common people, in order to inspire them with [the aspiration for] general and special merit.

body.text: śakreṣu ca śakrasaṃmata aiśvaryānityatvasaṃdarśanāyau /
body.translated_text: Among the <s>Śakras</s> (Indras), he was honored as a <s>Śakra</s>, in order to show the impermanence of sovereignty.

body.text: brahmasu ca brahmasaṃmato viśeṣajñānasaṃdarśanāya /
body.translated_text: Among the <s>Brahmās</s>, he was honored as a <s>Brahmā</s>, in order to show them special knowledge.

body.text: lokapāleṣu ca lokapālasaṃmataḥ sarvasatvaparipālanāya /
body.translated_text: Among the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), he was honored as a <s>Lokapāla</s>, in order to protect all beings.

body.text: iti hi vimalakīrtir licchavir evam apramāṇopāyakauśalajñānasamanvāgato vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ prativasati sma /
body.translated_text: Thus indeed did <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, endowed with such immeasurable knowledge of <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), dwell in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text: Vkn 2.7 sa upāyakauśalyena glānam ātmānam upadarśayati sma / tasya glānasya vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ rājarājamahāmātrāmātyakumārapāriṣadyā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ śreṣṭhinaigamajānapadās tadanyāni ca bahūni prāṇisahasrāṇi glānaparipṛcchakāny upasaṃkrāmanti sma /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.7 Through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), he displayed himself as ill. And to visit that sick man in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, kings, great ministers, officials, princes, courtiers, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, merchants, guild-leaders, and townspeople, as well as many other thousands of living beings, came to inquire after his illness.

body.text: Vkn 2.8 teṣām upasaṃkrāntānāṃ vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ / imam eva cāturmahābhautikaṃ kāyam ārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati sma: evam anityo 'yaṃ mārṣāḥ kāyaḥ / evam adhruvaḥ, evam anāsvāsikaḥ, evaṃ durbalaḥ, evam asāraḥ / evaṃ jarjaraḥ, evam itvaraḥ, evaṃ duḥkhaḥ, evam ābādhikaḥ, evaṃ vipariṇāmadharmā, evaṃ bahurogabhājano 'yaṃ mārṣāḥ kāyaḥ / tatra paṇḍitena niśrayo na kartavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.8 To those who had come, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> beginning with this very body made of the four great elements: 'Sirs, this body is impermanent; it is unreliable, it is untrustworthy, it is weak, it is without essence; it is fragile, it is perishable, it is painful, it is prone to illness, it is subject to change — this body, sirs, is a receptacle of many diseases. A wise person should place no reliance upon it.'

body.text: Vkn 2.9 phenapiṇḍopamo 'yaṃ mārṣāḥ kāyo 'parimardanakṣamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.9 'This body, sirs, is like a mass of foam — unable to withstand being pressed.',

body.text: budbudopamo 'yaṃ kāyo 'cirasthitikaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a bubble — not enduring for long.'

body.text: marīcyupamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ kleśatṛṣṇāsaṃbhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a mirage — born from the thirst of the <s>kleśas</s> (defilements).'

body.text: kadalīskandhopamo 'yaṃ kāyo 'sārakatvāt /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a plantain trunk — without core.'

body.text: yantrabhūto batāyaṃ kāyo 'sthisnāyuvinibaddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Alas, this body is a mere mechanism — bound together by bones and sinews.'

body.text: māyopamo 'yaṃ kāyo viparyāsasaṃbhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like an illusion — born from <s>viparyāsa</s> (delusion).'

body.text: svapnopamo 'yaṃ kāyo vitathadarśanaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a dream — appearing as something unreal.'

body.text: pratibhāsopamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ pūrvakarmapratibhāsatayā saṃdṛśyate /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a reflection — appearing as the reflection of past <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: pratiśrutkopamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ pratyayādhīnatvāt /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like an echo — dependent upon conditions (<s>pratyayas</s>).'

body.text: meghopamo 'yaiḥ kāyaś cittākulavigamalakṣaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a cloud — characterized by the confusion and dissolution of the mind.'

body.text: vidyutsadṛśo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgayukto 'navasthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like lightning — momentary in its destruction and unstable.'

body.text: asvāmiko 'yaṃ kāyo nānāpratyayasaṃbhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is without an owner — born from various conditions (<s>pratyayas</s>).'

body.text: Vkn 2.10 nirvyāpāro 'yaṃ kāyaḥ pṛthivīsadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.10 'This body is without activity — like earth.'

body.text: anātmo 'yaṃ kāyo 'psadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is without self (<s>anātman</s>) — like water.'

body.text: nirjīvo 'yaṃ kāyas tejaḥsadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is without life — like fire.'

body.text: niṣpudgalo 'yaṃ kāyo vāyusadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is without a person (<s>pudgala</s>) — like wind.'

body.text: niḥsvabhāvo 'yaṃ kāya ākāśasadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is without inherent nature — like space.'

body.text: Vkn 2.11 asaṃbhūto 'yaṃ kāyo mahābhūtānām ālayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.11 'This body is unproduced — [merely] a dwelling place of the great elements.'

body.text: śūnyo 'yaṃ kāya ātmātmīyavigataḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is empty (<s>śūnya</s>) — devoid of self and what belongs to self.'

body.text: jaḍo 'yaṃ kāyas tṛṇakāṣṭhakuḍyaloṣṭapratibhāsasadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is inert — like grass, wood, walls, and clods of earth.'

body.text: niśceṣṭo 'yaṃ kāyo vātayantrayukto vartate /
body.translated_text: 'This body is without volition — it operates like a machine driven by wind.'

body.text: rikto 'yaṃ kāyo 'śucipūtisaṃcayaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is hollow — [merely] an accumulation of impurity and foulness.'

body.text: tuccho 'yaṃ kāya ucchādanaparimardanavikiraṇavidhvansanadharmā /
body.translated_text: 'This body is vain — subject to being rubbed away, massaged away, scattered, and demolished.'

body.text: upadruto 'yaṃ kāyaś caturuttaraiś caturbhī rogaśataiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is afflicted — by four hundred and four diseases.'

body.text: jīrṇodapānasadṛśo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ sadā jarābhibhūtaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a dried-up well — always overwhelmed by old age.'

body.text: paryantasthāyī batāyaṃ kāyo maraṇaparyavasānaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Alas, this body abides only to its end — culminating in death.'

body.text: vadhakāśīviṣaśūnyagrāmopamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ skandhadhātvāyatanaparigṛhītaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This body is like a murderer, a venomous serpent, and an empty village — seized upon by the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases).'

body.text: tatra yuṣmābhir evaṃrūpe kāye nirvidvirāga utpādayitavyas tathāgatakāye ca spṛhotpādayitavyā /
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, toward such a body, you should generate disenchantment and dispassion, and generate aspiration for the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 2.12 dharmakāyo hi mārṣāḥ tathāgatakāyo dānanirjātaḥ śīlanirjātaḥ samādhinirjātaḥ prajñānirjāto vimuktinirjāto vimuktijñānadarśananirjātaḥ / maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣānirjātaḥ / dānadamasaṃyamanirjātaḥ kṣāntisauratyanirjāto dṛḍhavīryakuśalamūlanirjāto dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattinirjātaḥ śrutaprajñopāyanirjātaḥ / saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyanirjātaḥ śamathavidarśanānirjāto daśabalanirjātaś caturvaiśāradyanirjātaḥ / aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmanirjātaḥ sarvapāramitānirjātaḥ / abhijñāvidyānirjātaḥ sarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇāya nirjātaḥ sarvakuśaladharmaparigrahanirjātaḥ satyanirjāto bhūtanirjāto 'pramādanirjātaḥ / apramāṇaśubhakarmanirjāto mārṣās tathāgatakāyas tatra yuṣmābhiḥ spṛhā kartavyā / sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvakleśavyādhiprahāṇāyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpādayitavyāni /
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.12 'For the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, sirs, is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (body of the Dharma) — born from <s>dāna</s> (generosity), born from <s>śīla</s> (morality), born from <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), born from <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), born from <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), born from <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (the knowledge and vision of liberation); born from <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity); born from <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), and <s>saṃyama</s> (discipline); born from <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and <s>sauratya</s> (gentleness); born from firm <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) and roots of merit; born from <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment); born from <s>śruta</s> (learning), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means); born from the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s> (factors of awakening); born from <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vidarśanā</s> (insight); born from the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>); born from the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>); born from the eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>); born from all the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); born from <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) and <s>vidyā</s> (true knowledge); born for the abandonment of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; born for the acquisition of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; born from truth, born from reality, born from diligence — sirs, the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is born from immeasurable meritorious deeds. You should aspire toward it, and for the elimination of all <s>kleśa</s>-diseases (affliction-diseases) of all beings, you should generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).'

body.text: Vkn 2.13 evaṃ vimalakīrtir licchavis tathā saṃnipatitānāṃ teṣāṃ glānaparipṛcchakānāṃ tathā tathā dharmaṃ deśayati yad bahūni satvaśatasahasrāṇy anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpādayanti // //
body.translated_text: Vkn 2.13 Thus did <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> to those who had gathered to inquire after his illness, in such a manner that many hundreds of thousands of beings generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). //

body.text: acintyopāyakauśalyaparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, called <s>Acintyopāyakauśalya</s> (Inconceivable Skillful Means). //

body.text: Vkn 3.1 atha vimalakīrter licchaver etad abhavat: ahaṃ ca glāna ābādhiko mañcasamārūḍhaḥ, na ca māṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ samanvāharati, na ca me glānaparipṛcchakaṃ kaṃcit preṣayaty anukaṃpām upādāya /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.1 Then this thought occurred to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'I am ill, ailing, and confined to my bed, yet the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, does not attend to me, nor does he send anyone to inquire after my illness out of compassion.'

body.text: Vkn 3.2 samanvāhṛtaś ca bhagavatā vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ / atha bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ śāriputra vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.2 The <s>Bhagavān</s> was indeed aware of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Go, <s>Śāriputra</s>, and inquire after the illness of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>.'

body.text:
evam ukta āyuṣmāñ śāriputro bhagavantam etad avocat: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasya hetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye 'nyatamasmin vṛkṣamūle pratisaṃlīno 'bhūvam /
vimalakīrtiś ca licchavir yena tad vṛkṣamūlaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mām etad avocat:
Vkn 3.3 na bhadantaśāriputra evaṃ pratisaṃlayanaṃ saṃlātavyaṃ yathā tvaṃ pratisaṃlīnaḥ / api tu tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā traidhātuke na kāyaś cittaṃ vā saṃdṛśyate / tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā nirodhāc ca na vyuttiṣṭhasi sarveryāpatheṣu ca saṃdṛśyase / tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā prāptilakṣaṇaṃ ca na vijahāsi pṛthagjanalakṣaṇeṣu ca saṃdṛśyase / tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā te na cādhyātmaṃ cittam avasthitaṃ bhaven na bahirdhopavicaret / tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā sarvadṛṣṭigatebhyaś ca na calasi saptatriṃśatsu ca bodhipakṣyeṣu dharmeṣu saṃdṛśyase / tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā saṃsārāvacarāṃś ca kleśān na prajahāsi nirvāṇasamavasaraṇaś ca bhavasi / ye bhadantaśāriputra evaṃ pratisaṃlayanaṃ pratisaṃlīyante teṣāṃ bhagavān pratisaṃlayanam anujānāti /
body.translated_text:
When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that at one time I was sitting in meditative absorption (<s>pratisaṃlīna</s>) at the foot of a certain tree.
Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached that tree-root and said to me:
(Vkn 3.3) 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, meditative absorption should not be practiced in the way you are practicing it. Rather, one should practice absorption in such a way that neither body nor mind appears in the three realms. One should practice absorption in such a way that, without rising from cessation, one is still seen in all postures. One should practice absorption in such a way that, without abandoning the characteristics of attainment, one is still seen in the characteristics of an ordinary person. One should practice absorption in such a way that the mind is neither established internally nor wanders externally. One should practice absorption in such a way that, without moving from all views, one is still seen in the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>). One should practice absorption in such a way that, without abandoning the defilements that course through <s>saṃsāra</s>, one still enters <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those who practice absorption in this way — their absorption the <s>Bhagavān</s> approves.'

body.text: Vkn 3.4 so 'haṃ bhagavan etāṃ śrutvā tūṣṇīm evābhūvam / na tasya śaknomy uttare prativacanaṃ dātum / tan nāham utsahe tasya kulaputrasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.4) And I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, upon hearing this, remained completely silent. I was unable to give him a reply. Therefore I am not able to go to that son of good family to inquire about his illness.

body.text: Vkn 3.5 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ maudgalyāyana vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.5) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Go, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: maudgalyāyano 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasya hetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryām anyatamasmin vīthīmukhe gṛhapatibhyo dharmaṃ deśayāmi / tatra māṃ vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkrāmyaivam āha:
body.translated_text: <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that at one time I was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to householders at a certain crossroads in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached me and said:"

body.text: Vkn 3.6 na bhadantamaudgalyāyana gṛhibhyo 'vadātavasanebhya evaṃ dharmo deśayitavyo yathā bhadanto deśayati / api tu tathā bhadantamaudgalyāyana dharmo deśayitavyo yathaiva sa dharmaḥ / dharmo hi bhadantamaudgalyāyana asatvaḥ satvarajovigataḥ, nairātmyo rāgarajovigataḥ, nirjīvo jāticyutivigataḥ, niṣpudgalaḥ pūrvāntāparāntaparicchinnaḥ, śānta upaśāntalakṣaṇaḥ, virāgo 'nārambaṇagatikaḥ, anakṣaraḥ sarvavākyacchedaḥ, anudāhāraḥ sarvormivigataḥ, sarvatrānugata ākāśasamasadṛśaḥ, avarṇaliṅgasaṃsthānaḥ sarvapracāravigataḥ, amamo mamakāravigataḥ, avijñaptiś cittamanovijñānavigataḥ, asadṛśo niṣpratipakṣatvāt, hetuvilakṣaṇaḥ pratyayāsamāropaḥ, dharmadhātusamavasaraṇaḥ sarvadharmasamāhitaḥ, tathatānugato 'nanugamanayogena, bhūtakoṭipratiṣṭhito 'tyantācalitatvāt, acalitaḥ ṣaḍviṣayāniśritatvāt, na kvacid gamanāgamano 'navasthitatvāt, śūnyatāsamāhita ānimittaprabhāvito 'praṇihitalakṣaṇaḥ, ūhāpohavigataḥ, anutkṣepo 'prakṣepaḥ, utpādabhaṅgavigataḥ, anālayaś cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaḥpathasamatikrāntaḥ, anunnato 'navanataḥ, sthito 'neñjyaṃ prāptaḥ, sarvapracāravigataḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.6) 'Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> should not be taught to white-robed householders in the way you are teaching it. Rather, venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> should be taught in a way that accords with the <s>Dharma</s> itself. For the <s>Dharma</s>, venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, is without beings, being free from the dust of beings; it is without self, being free from the dust of passion; it is without life, being free from birth and death; it is without a person (<s>pudgala</s>), being cut off in its prior and posterior limits; it is peaceful, having the characteristic of quiescence; it is free from passion, having no course of support; it is without syllables, being the cessation of all speech; it is beyond expression, being free from all waves; it is everywhere-pervading, similar to space; it is without color, mark, or shape, being free from all activity; it is without "mine," being free from possessiveness; it is beyond indication (<s>avijñapti</s>), being free from mind, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness; it is without comparison, because it has no opposite; it is unlike any cause, because it does not rest upon conditions; it enters into the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas), being composed of all dharmas; it follows <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) through the practice of non-following; it is established at the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) because of its utter immovability; it is unshaken, because it does not depend on the six sense-objects; it has no coming or going, because of its non-abiding; it is composed of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), made effective through signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), having the characteristic of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>); it is free from deliberation and counter-deliberation; it is neither elevated nor depressed; it is free from arising and destruction; it is without attachment, having transcended the paths of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; it is neither high nor low; it is stable, having attained the immovable; it is free from all activity.'

body.text: Vkn 3.7 īdṛśasya bhadantamahāmaudgalyāyana dharmasya kīdṛśī deśanā / dharmadeśaneti bhadantamahāmaudgalyāyana samāropapadam etat / ye 'pi śṛṇvanti te 'pi samāropenaiva śṛṇvanti / yatra bhadantamaudgalyāyana asamāropapadaṃ na tatra deśyate na śrūyate na vijñāyate / tadyathā māyāpuruṣo māyāpuruṣebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.7) 'Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, for a <s>Dharma</s> of such nature, what kind of teaching is possible? "Dharma-teaching," venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, is itself a term of superimposition. Those who listen also listen through superimposition. Where, venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, there is no term of superimposition, there nothing is taught, nothing is heard, nothing is known. It is as if a magical person were to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to magical persons.'

body.text: Vkn 3.8 evaṃ hi cittāvasthānena dharmo deśayitavyaḥ / satvendriyakuśalena ca te bhavitavyam, sudṛṣṭaprajñādarśanena mahākaruṇāmukhībhūtena mahāyānasaṃvarṇakena buddhekṛtajñena śuddhāśayena dharmaniruktividhijñena, triratnavaṃśānupacchedāya ca te dharmo deśayitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.8) 'In this way, with such a mental disposition, the <s>Dharma</s> should be taught. And one must be skilled in the faculties of beings, with the vision of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) rightly seen, with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) as the foremost, praising the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), grateful to the <s>Buddha</s>, pure in intention, knowing the method of <s>Dharma</s>-explanation; and the <s>Dharma</s> should be taught for the unbroken continuity of the lineage of the Three Jewels.'

body.text: Vkn 3.9 tena bhagavan tathā tathā dharmo deśito yathā tato gṛhapatiparsado 'ṣṭānāṃ gṛhapatiśatānām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni / ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.9) 'By him, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> was taught in such a way that from that householder assembly, the minds of eight hundred householders were aroused toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). And I was struck speechless. Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: Vkn 3.10 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ mahākāśyapa vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.10) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: 'Go, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: mahākāśyapo 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan daridravīthyāṃ piṇḍāya carāmi / tatra māṃ vimalakirtir licchavir upasaṃkramyaivam āha:
body.translated_text: <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that I was going for alms in the street of the poor. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> approached me and said:'

body.text: Vkn 3.11 prādeśikī bhadantamahākāśyapasya karuṇāmaitrī, yan mahākulāny utsṛjya daridrakulāny upasaṃkrāmasi / api tu bhadantamahākāśyapa dharmasamatāpratiṣṭhitena te bhavitavyam / sarvadā sarvasatvasamanvāhāreṇa piṇḍapātaḥ paryeṣṭavyaḥ / anāhāreṇa cāhāraḥ paryeṣṭavyaḥ / parapiṇḍagrāhāpanayāya ca te piṇḍāya caritavyam / śūnyagrāmādhiṣṭhitena ca grāmaḥ praveṣṭavyaḥ / naranārīparipākāya ca te nagaraṃ praveṣṭavyam / buddhakulakulīnena ca te kulāny upasaṃkramitavyāni /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.11) 'Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, your compassion and loving-kindness are provincial, in that you bypass wealthy families and approach poor families. But, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, you should be established in the equality of the <s>Dharma</s>. The alms-food should be sought always with the equal benefit of all beings in mind. The alms-food should be sought without eating. You should go for alms in order to remove the grasping of others' food. You should enter the village while established in the empty village. The city should be entered for the ripening of men and women. You should approach families as one born into the family of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 3.12 apratigrahaṇatayā ca piṇḍapātaḥ pratigrāhyaḥ / jātyandhasamatayā ca rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni / pratiśrutakopamatayā ca śabdāḥ śrotavyāḥ / vātasamatayā ca gandhā ghrātavyāḥ / avijñaptito rasā āsvādayitavyāḥ / jñānāsparśanatayā ca sparśāḥ spraṣṭavyāḥ / māyāpuruṣavijñāptyā ca dharmā vijñātavyāḥ / yo 'svabhāvo 'parabhāvaś ca tad anujjvalitam / yad anujjvalitaṃ tan na śāmyati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.12) 'The alms-food should be received with the attitude of non-receiving. Forms should be seen with the equanimity of one blind from birth. Sounds should be heard with the equanimity of an echo. Smells should be smelled with the equanimity of the wind. Tastes should be tasted without discrimination.
