Touches should be touched with the awareness of non-contact. <s>Dharmas</s> should be known with the knowledge of a magical person. That which has no own-nature and no other-nature — that is unignited. What is unignited does not cease.'

body.text: Vkn 3.13 yadi sthaviro mahākāśyapo 'ṣṭau ca mithyātvāni samatikrāmet, aṣṭau ca vimokṣān samāpadyeta, mithyāsamatayā ca samyaktvasamatām avataret, ekena ca piṇḍapātena sarvasatvān pratipādayet, sarvabuddhān sarvāryāṃś ca pratipādya paścād ātmanā paribhuñjīta, tathā ca paribhuñjīta yathā na saṃkleśo na vigatakleśaḥ, paribhuñjīta na samāhito na vyutthitaḥ, na saṃsārasthito na nirvāṇasthitaḥ paribhuñjīta / ye ca bhadantāya piṇḍapātaṃ dadati te teṣāṃ nālpaphalaṃ na mahāphalaiḥ bhavet / na ca hānāya na viśeṣāya gacchet, buddhagatisamavasaraṇāya ca bhaveta na śrāvakagatisamavasaraṇāya / evaṃ sthaviro mahākāśyapo 'moghaṃ rāṣṭrapiṇḍaṃ paribhuñjīta /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.13) 'If the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> were to transcend the eight wrong states and enter the eight liberations, and through the equanimity of the wrong, enter the equanimity of the right; and with a single alms-portion nourish all beings; and having nourished all <s>Buddhas</s> and all noble ones, only then eat himself; and were to eat in such a way that there is neither defilement nor freedom from defilement; were to eat neither in concentration nor risen from concentration; were to eat neither abiding in <s>saṃsāra</s> nor abiding in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — and those who give the alms-food to the venerable one would find that it yields neither small fruit nor great fruit; neither would it lead to loss nor to distinction, but would lead to the course of <s>Buddhahood</s>, not to the course of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) — thus, elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, should one partake of the country's alms-food without it being in vain.'

body.text: Vkn 3.14 so 'haṃ bhagavan imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptaḥ sarvabodhisatvān namasyāmi / gṛhiṇo 'pi nāmaivaṃrūpaṃ pratibhānam, ko 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpādayet / tataḥ prabhṛti me na kaścit satvaḥ śrāvakayāne pratyekabuddhayāne vā samādāpitapūrvo 'nyatra mahāyānāt / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya kulaputrasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.14) 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, upon hearing this teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, was filled with wonder and worshipped all <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Even a layperson has such eloquence — who would not arouse the mind toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)? From that time onward, I have never directed any being toward the <s>śrāvakayāna</s> (vehicle of the hearers) or the <s>pratyekabuddhayāna</s> (vehicle of the solitary buddhas), but only toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that son of good family to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: Vkn 3.15 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ subhūte vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.15) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Go, <s>Subhūti</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: subhūtir apy āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasya hetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ piṇḍāya carāmi / vimalakīrter licchaver niveśanaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ / tasya me vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ pātraṃ gṛhītvā praṇītena bhojanena pratipūryaivam āha:
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that at one time I was going for alms in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. I entered the dwelling of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> for alms. Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> took my bowl, filled it with excellent food, and said to me:'

body.text: Vkn 3.16 sacet tvaṃ bhadantasubhūte āmiṣasamatayā sarvadharmasamatām anugataḥ sarvadharmasamatayā ca buddhadharmasamatām anugata eva, tvam imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ pratigṛhnīṣva / sacet tvaṃ bhadantasubhūte na rāgadoṣamohaprahīṇo na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃvasasi / saced evam asy avikopya satkāyam ekāyanaṃ mārgam anugataḥ / na ca te 'vidyā bhavatṛṣṇā ca samudghātitā na ca vidyāvimuktī utpādite / ānantaryasamatayā ca te samādhivimuktiḥ / na cāsi mukto na baddhaḥ / na ca te catvāry āryasatyāni dṛṣṭāni na ca na dṛṣṭasatyaḥ / na prāptaphalo na pṛthagjanasamavasaraṇaḥ / na cāsy āryo nānāryaḥ / na sarvadharmasamanvāgataś ca sarvadharmasamadhigataś ca /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.16) 'If you, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, have followed the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> through the equality of material things, and have followed the equality of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> through the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, then you may accept this alms-food. If you, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, have not abandoned passion, hatred, and delusion, yet do not dwell together with them. If thus you have followed the direct path without disturbing the <s>satkāya</s> (aggregate of being). If <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) have not been eradicated in you, yet <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>vimukti</s> (liberation) have not been produced. If through the equality of the <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous deeds) you attain <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>vimukti</s> (liberation). If you are neither liberated nor bound. If you have neither seen the four <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths), nor are you one who has not seen the truth. If you have neither attained the fruits nor gathered among ordinary persons. If you are neither noble nor ignoble. If you are not endowed with all <s>dharmas</s> yet have realized all <s>dharmas</s> —'

body.text: Vkn 3.17 na ca te śāstā dṛṣṭo na dharmaḥ śruto na saṃghaḥ paryupāsitaḥ / ye ca te ṣaṭ śāstāras tadyathā pūraṇaḥ kāśyapaḥ, maskarī gośālīputraḥ, saṃjayo vairāṣṭrikaputraḥ, kakudaḥ kātyāyanaḥ, ajitaḥ keśakambalaḥ, nirgrantho jñātiputraḥ, te ca bhadantasya śāstāras tāṃś ca niśritya pravrajito yadgāminas te ṣaṭ śāstāras tadgāmy evāryasubhūtiḥ,
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.17) 'If you have not seen the Teacher, nor heard the <s>Dharma</s>, nor attended the <s>Saṃgha</s>. And the six teachers — namely, <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Saṃjaya Vairāṣṭrikaputra</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, and <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s> — those are the venerable one's teachers, and relying on them you have gone forth; wherever those six teachers go, there too goes the noble <s>Subhūti</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 3.18 sarvadṛṣṭigateṣu cāryaman antargato na cāntamadhyaprāptaḥ, aṣṭākṣaṇasamavasaraṇaś cāsi na cāsi lakṣaṇam anuprāptaḥ, saṃkleśena cāsi samo 'vyavadānam adhigataḥ, yā ca sarvasatvānām araṇā sā bhadantasyāpy araṇā, na ca tvayā dakṣiṇā viśodhyate, ye ca bhadantāya piṇḍapātaṃ dadati tāṃś ca vinipātayasi, sarvamāraiś ca te sārdham ekahastaḥ kṛtaḥ / sarvakleśāś ca te sahāyāḥ, yatsvabhāvāś ca kleśās tatsvabhāvo bhadantaḥ, sarvasatveṣu te vadhakacittaṃ pratyupasthitam, sarvabuddhāś ca te 'bhyākhyātāḥ, sarvabuddhadharmāṃś ca pratikrośasi, na cāsi saṃghapratisaraṇaḥ, na ca jātu parinirvāsyasi / evaṃ tvam imaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ pratigṛhīṇa /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.18) 'You have entered into all the courses of wrong views, yet have not reached any end or middle. You have gathered in the eight inopportune states, yet have not attained the characteristics [of a fortunate rebirth]. You are equal to defilement and have not realized purification. The hostility of all beings is also your hostility, venerable one, and the offerings made to you are not purified. Those who give alms-food to the venerable one — them you cast down. You have made common cause with all <s>Māras</s>. All <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) are your companions; the nature of the defilements is your nature, venerable one. You have a murderous mind toward all beings. All <s>Buddhas</s> have been reviled by you. You repudiate all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. You do not take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s>. And you will never attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Thus should you accept this alms-food.'

body.text: Vkn 3.19 tasya me bhagavan imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvāndhakāraprāptā diśo 'bhūvan ḥ tat kim asmai nirdiśāmi, katham vā pratipadya iti / so 'haṃ tat pātram utsṛjya tato gṛhān niṣkramiṣyāmīti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.19) 'Upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the directions became dark to me — what should I say to him, and how should I respond? I was about to put down that bowl and leave the house.'

body.text: vimalakīrtir Iicchavir mām evam āha: mā bhadantasubhūte akṣarebhya uttrasīḥ, pratigṛhāṇedaṃ pātram / tat kiṃ manyase bhadantasubhūte, yadi tathāgatanirmita evam ucyeta kaccit sa uttraset /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to me: 'Do not be frightened by syllables, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>! Accept this bowl. What do you think, venerable <s>Subhūti</s> — if a <s>Tathāgata</s>-created emanation were to speak thus, would he be frightened?'

body.text: so 'ham avocam: no hīdaṃ kulaputra /
body.translated_text: I said: 'No indeed, son of good family!'

body.text: sa mām evam āha: nirmitamāyāsvabhāvebhyo bhadantasubhūte sarvadharmebhyo nottrasitavyam / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / sarvāṇi hi tāni vacanāni tatsvabhāvāni, evaṃ paṇḍitā akṣareṣu na sajjanti na tebhya uttrasyanti / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / sarvāṇi tāny akṣarāṇy anakṣarāṇi sthāpayitvā vimuktiṃ vimuktilakṣaṇāṃś ca sarvadharmān /
body.translated_text: He said to me: '(Vkn 3.19) Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, one should not be frightened by any <s>dharmas</s>, whose nature is that of illusions and magical creations. For what reason? All those words are of that very nature. Thus the wise do not cling to syllables, nor are they frightened by them. For what reason? All those syllables are non-syllables, except for <s>vimukti</s> (liberation) — all <s>dharmas</s> have the characteristic of liberation.'

body.text: Vkn 3.20 iha nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne dvayor devaputraśatayor virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur viśuddham, pañcānāṃ ca devaputraśatānām ānulomikyāḥ kṣānteḥ pratilambho 'bhūt / ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam, na cāsya śaknomy uttare prativacanaṃ dātum / tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.20) When this teaching was being expounded, the stainless, spotless <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (Dharma-eye) was purified in two hundred <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons), and five hundred <s>devaputras</s> attained the <s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s> (acquiescent patience). And I was struck speechless, unable to give him a reply. Therefore I am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: Vkn 3.21 atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇaṃ maitrāyaṇīputram āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ pūrṇa vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.21) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>: 'Go, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: pūrṇo 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye vanasyānyatamasmin pṛthivīpradeśa ādikarmikāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi /
body.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇa</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that at one time I was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beginner monks at a certain place in the forest.'

body.text: tatra vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkramya mām evam āha:
body.translated_text: There <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> approached me and said:

body.text: Vkn 3.22 samāpadya bhadantapūrṇa eteṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ cittaṃ vyavalokya dharmaṃ deśaya / mā mahāratnabhājaneṣu prati kulmāṣān prākṣaipsīḥ / jāniṣva tāvat kimāśayā ete bhikṣava iti / mā vaiḍūryaratnaṃ kācamaṇikaiḥ samānīkārṣīḥ / mā bhadantapūrṇa apratyavekṣyā satvendriyeṣu prādeśikendriyatvam upasaṃhārṣīḥ / mā akṣatāṃ kṣiṇuṣva / mā mahāmārgam avatartukāmān bhandarathyāṃ praveśaya / mā mahāsāgaraṃ goṣpade praveśaya / mā sūryaprabhāṃ khadyotakair nirvartaya / mā siṃhanādasaṃprasthitān sṛgālanāde niyojaya / api bhadantapūrṇa sarve hy ete bhikṣavo mahāyānasaṃprasthitā amuṣitabodhicittāḥ / teṣāṃ bhadantapūrṇa mā śrāvakayānam upadarśaya / kaṣṭaṃ hi śrāvakayānam / jātyandhā iva me śrāvakāḥ pratibhānti satvendriyavimātratājñāne /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.22) 'Having entered <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, first examine the minds of these monks before teaching the <s>Dharma</s>! Do not cast coarse grain into vessels fit for great jewels! First know the aspirations of these monks. Do not treat <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) as equal to glass beads! Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, do not, without examining the faculties of beings, attribute to them deficient faculties! Do not wound those who are uninjured! Do not lead those who wish to travel the great highway into a side lane! Do not put the great ocean into a cattle hoof-print! Do not extinguish sunlight with fireflies! Do not set those who have embarked on the lion's roar to the jackal's cry! For, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, all these monks have embarked on the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), with their <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) undiminished. Do not, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, show them the <s>śrāvakayāna</s> (vehicle of the hearers)! The <s>śrāvakayāna</s> is a miserable thing! The <s>śrāvakas</s> appear to me as blind from birth in their ignorance of the varying degrees of beings' faculties.'

body.text: Vkn 3.23 atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadyate sma / yathā te bhikṣavo 'nekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsam anusmaraṇti sma / te pañcabuddhaśataparyupāsitakuśalamūlāḥ samyaksaṃbodhaye, teṣāṃ tad bodhicittam āmukhībhūtam / te tasya satpuruṣasya pādau śirobhiḥ praṇamya tatraiva niṣaṇṇāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā, teṣāṃ tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yathāvaivartikāḥ saṃvṛttā anuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.23) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> at that moment entered such a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that those monks recalled their various former lives. They [realized that they] had accumulated roots of merit by attending upon five hundred <s>Buddhas</s> and were destined for <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). Their <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) was made manifest. They bowed their heads at the feet of that virtuous man, and sitting there with palms joined, he taught them the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that they became <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible) in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).

body.text: Vkn 3.24 tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.24) Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: Vkn 3.25 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ kātyāyanam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ kātyāyana vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.25) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Kātyāyana</s>: 'Go, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: kātyāyano 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: bhagavatā saṃkṣiptena bhikṣūṇām avavādo dattaḥ / teṣāṃ sūtrapadaviniścayāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi, yad idam anityārthaṃ duḥkhārtham anātmārthaṃ śāntārtham /
body.translated_text: <s>Kātyāyana</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave a brief admonition to the monks. I was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to them for the determination of the <s>sūtra</s>-passages — explaining the meaning of impermanence, the meaning of suffering, the meaning of non-self, and the meaning of peace.'

body.text: tatra vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkramya mām evam āha:
body.translated_text: There <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> approached me and said:

body.text: Vkn 3.26 mā bhadantakātyāyana sapracārām utpādabhaṅgayuktāṃ dharmatāṃ nirdiśa / yo bhadantamahākātyāyana atyantatayā na jāto na janiṣyati notpanno na niruddho na nirotsyate 'yam anityārthaḥ / yaḥ pañcānāṃ skandhānāṃ śūnyatānugamānutpādānirodhārtho 'yaṃ duḥkhārthaḥ / yad ātmānātmayor advayatvam ayam anātmārthaḥ / yo 'svabhāvo 'parabhāvas tad anujjvalitam, yad anujvalitaṃ na tac chāmyati, yo 'tyantopaśamo 'yaṃ śāntārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.26) 'Do not, venerable <s>Kātyāyana</s>, teach the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) as involving activity, as conjoined with arising and ceasing. Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the meaning of impermanence is this: that which by its utter finality has not been born and will not be born, has not arisen and has not ceased, and will not cease. The meaning of suffering is this: the meaning of the emptiness and non-arising and non-ceasing of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). The meaning of non-self is this: the non-duality of self and non-self. The meaning of peace is this: that which has no own-nature and no other-nature is unignited; what is unignited does not cease; that which is utterly quiescent — that is the meaning of peace.'

body.text: Vkn 3.27 asmin khalu punar nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇām anupādāyāsravebhyaś cittāni vimuktāni / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.27) When this teaching was being expounded, the minds of those monks were liberated from the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) without further grasping. Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: Vkn 3.28 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam aniruddham āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvam aniruddha vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.28) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>: 'Go, <s>Aniruddha</s>, to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: aniruddho 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Aniruddha</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason?'

body.text: Vkn 3.29 abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: anyatamasmiṃś caṅkrame caṅkramāmi / tatra śubhavyūho nāma brahmā daśabhir brahmasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ taṃ pradeśam avabhāsya yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasābhivandyaikānte sthitvā mām etad avocat: kiyad āyuṣmān aniruddho divyena cakṣuṣā paśyati /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.29 'I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>: I was once walking on a certain walking path. Then a <s>Brahmā</s> named <s>Śubhavyūha</s> (Glorious Array), together with ten thousand <s>Brahmās</s>, having illuminated that place, approached me, bowed his head at my feet, stood to one side, and said to me: "How far does the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> see with the divine eye?"'

body.text: tam enam aham etad avocam: ahaṃ mārṣa imaṃ triṃ sāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ bhagavataḥ śākyamuner buddhakṣetraṃ tad yathāpi nāma karatale nyastam āmalakaphalam evaṃ paśyāmi /
body.translated_text: 'To him I said this: "Sir, I see this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world system), the <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, as clearly as one sees an <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan) fruit placed in the palm of one's hand."'

body.text: Vkn 3.30 iyaṃ ca kathā pravṛttā vimalakīrtiś ca licchavis taṃ pradeśam upasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasā vanditvaivam āha: kiṃ bhadantāniruddha divyaṃ cakṣur abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam utānabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam / yady abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ tad bāhyaiḥ pañcābhijñaiḥ samam, athānabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ anabhisaṃskāro 'saṃskṛtas tena na śakyaṃ draṣṭum / tat kathaṃ sthaviraḥ paśyati /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.30 'While this conversation was taking place, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> approached that place. Having approached and bowed his head at my feet, he said: "Is the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>'s divine eye of the nature of conditioned phenomena or of the nature of unconditioned phenomena? If it is of the nature of conditioned phenomena, then it is the same as the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) of non-Buddhist [practitioners]. If it is of the nature of unconditioned phenomena — being unconditioned, it should not be possible to see with it. How then does the elder see?"'

body.text: so 'haṃ tūṣṇīm abhūvam /
body.translated_text: 'I remained silent.'

body.text: Vkn 3.31 sa ca brahmā tasya satpuruṣasyemaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptas taṃ namaskṛtyaitad avocat: ke loke divyacakṣuṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.31 'That <s>Brahmā</s>, having heard this teaching from that good man, was struck with wonder. Having paid homage to him, he said: "Who in the world possesses the divine eye?"'

body.text: āha: buddhā bhagavanto loke divyacakṣuṣo ye samāhitāvasthāṃ ca na vijahati sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi ca paśyanti / na ca dvayaprabhāvitāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'He replied: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s> (Blessed Ones), possess the divine eye in the world — they who do not abandon the state of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and yet see all <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields), and who are not influenced by duality."'

body.text: Vkn 3.32 atha sa brahmemaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā daśasahasraparivāro 'dhyāśayenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayati sma / sa māṃ vanditvā taṃ ca satpuruṣam abhivādya tatraivāntarhitaḥ / ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam / tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.32 'Then that <s>Brahmā</s>, having heard this teaching, together with his retinue of ten thousand, generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) with deep resolve. Having paid homage to me and to that good man, he vanished right there. And I was left without reply. Therefore I am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: Vkn 3.33 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam upālim āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvam upāle vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.33 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Upāli</s>: 'Go, <s>Upāli</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: upālir apy āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: anyatamau dvau bhikṣū āpattim āpannau, tau bhagavataḥ paryapatrapamāṇau bhagavantaṃ nopasaṃkrāmataḥ / tau yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntāv upasaṃkrāmya mām etad avocatām / āvāṃ bhadantopāle āpattim āpannau, tāv āvāṃ paryapatrapamāṇau bhagavantam upasaṃkramituṃ notsahāvahe / utsāhāya āyuṣmann upāle vinodayasvāvayoḥ kaukṛtyaṃ vyutthāpayasvāvām āpatteḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Upāli</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>: at one time, two <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) had committed an offense. They, being ashamed before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, did not approach him. They approached me instead and said to me: "We, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, have committed an offense. Being ashamed, we do not dare to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Please, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, encourage us, remove our remorse, and extricate us from our offense."'

body.text: Vkn 3.34 so 'haṃ bhagavaṃs tau bhikṣū dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayāmi / vimalakīrtiś ca licchavis taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ sa mām etad avocat: mā bhadantopāle etau bhikṣū āgāḍhīkārṣīḥ, vinodayānayor āpattim, mā āvilīkārṣīḥ / na hi bhadantopāle āpattir adhyātmapratiṣṭhitā na bahirdhāsaṃkrānto nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / uktaṃ hi bhagavatā cittasaṃkleśāt satvāḥ saṃkliśyante cittavyavadānād viśudhyante / cittaṃ ca bhadantopāle nādhyātmapratiṣṭhitaṃ na bahirdhā nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate / yathā cittaṃ tathāpattiḥ, yathāpattis tathā sarvadharmāḥ, tathatāṃ na vyativartante / yā bhadantopāle cittasya prakṛtir yayā cittaprakṛtyā bhadantasya cittaṃ vimuktam, kiṃ jātu sā cittaprakṛtiḥ saṃkliṣṭā /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.34 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, was counseling those two <s>bhikṣus</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, when <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> arrived at that place and said to me: "Venerable <s>Upāli</s>, do not further burden these two <s>bhikṣus</s>; remove their offense without troubling them. For, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, the offense is neither established internally, nor has it come from outside, nor is it found between the two. For what reason? The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'Through the defilement of the mind, beings are defiled; through the purification of the mind, they are purified.' The mind, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, is neither established internally, nor externally, nor is it found between the two. As is the mind, so is the offense; as is the offense, so are all <s>dharmas</s> — they do not depart from <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). That nature of the mind, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, by which nature the elder's mind is liberated — could that nature of the mind ever be defiled?"'

body.text: āha: no hidam /
body.translated_text: 'I replied: "No indeed."'

body.text: āha: tatprakṛtikāni bhadantopāle sarvasatvānāṃ cittāni /
body.translated_text: 'He said: "The minds of all beings, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, are of that very nature."'

body.text: Vkn 3.35 saṃkalpo bhadantopāle kleśaḥ / akalpāvikalpā ca prakṛtiḥ / viparyāsaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, aviparyastā ca prakṛtiḥ / ātmasamāropaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, nairātmyā ca prakṛtiḥ / utpannabhagnānavasthitā bhadantopāle sarvadharmā māyāmeghavidyutsadṛśāḥ / nirapekṣāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kṣaṇam api nāvatiṣṭhante / svapnamarīcisadṛśāḥ sarvadharmā vitathadarśanāḥ / dakacandrapratibimbasadṛśāḥ sarvadharmāś cittaparikalpenotpadyante / ye tv evaṃ jānanti te vinayadharā ity ucyante / ya evaṃ vinītās te suvinītāḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.35 '"Conceptualization, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, is <s>kleśa</s> (defilement); the absence of conceptualization and discrimination is the [original] nature. <s>Viparyāsa</s> (delusion) is defilement; freedom from delusion is the [original] nature. The superimposition of a self is defilement; <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) is the [original] nature. All <s>dharmas</s>, venerable <s>Upāli</s>, arise and break and do not remain — like illusions, clouds, and lightning. All <s>dharmas</s> are without mutual dependence and do not persist even for a moment. All <s>dharmas</s> are like dreams and mirages — appearing as something unreal. All <s>dharmas</s> are like the moon's reflection in water — they arise through the conceptualization of the mind. Those who understand thus are called 'bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline).' Those who are thus disciplined are well-disciplined."'

body.text: Vkn 3.36 atha tau bhikṣu etad avocatām: prajñādharo vinayadharo 'yam upāsakaḥ / na tv ayaṃ bhadantopālir yo bhagavatā vinayadharāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.36 'Then those two <s>bhikṣus</s> said: "This layman is a bearer of wisdom and a bearer of the <s>Vinaya</s>. Not even the venerable <s>Upāli</s>, whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> declared foremost among bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s>, [can match him]."'

body.text: tāv aham evaṃ vadāmi: mā bhikṣū atra gṛhapatisaṃjñām utpādayatām / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / tathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā nāsti kaścic chrāvako vā bodhisatvo vā, ya etasya pratibhānam ācchindyāt / tādṛśa etasya prajñālokaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'I said to them: "O <s>bhikṣus</s>, do not generate the perception of a householder regarding him. For what reason? Setting aside the <s>Tathāgata</s>, there is no <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) or <s>bodhisattva</s> who could cut short his eloquence. Such is his light of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)."'

body.text: Vkn 3.37 atha tau bhikṣū vinītakaukṛtyāv adhyāśayena tatraivānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpāditavantau, taṃ ca satpuruṣam abhivandyaivam āhatuḥ: sarvasatvā īdṛśasya pratibhānasya lābhino bhavantu / tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.37 'Then those two <s>bhikṣus</s>, their remorse removed, generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) with deep resolve, and having paid homage to that good man, said: "May all beings obtain such eloquence as this!" Therefore I am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: Vkn 3.38 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ rāhulam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ rāhula vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.38 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>: 'Go, <s>Rāhula</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: rāhulo 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye saṃbahulā licchavikumārakā yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mām etad avocan: tvaṃ rāhula tasya bhagavataḥ putraś cakravartirājyam utsṛjya pravrajitaḥ, tatra ke te pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Rāhula</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>: at one time, several <s>Licchavi</s> youths approached me and said: "You, <s>Rāhula</s>, are the son of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who renounced the kingship of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) and went forth. What are the benefits and advantages of going forth?"'

body.text: teṣām ahaṃ yathārūpaṃ pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsā nirdiśāmi, vimalakīrtir licchavir yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām abhivandyaitad avocat:
body.translated_text: 'As I was explaining to them the benefits and advantages of going forth in their proper form, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> approached me. Having paid homage, he said:'

body.text: Vkn 3.39 na bhadantarāhula evaṃ pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsā nirdeṣṭavyā yathā tvaṃ nirdiśasi / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / nirguṇā niranuśaṃsā hi pravrajyā / yatra bhadantarāhula saṃskṛtapravṛttis tatra guṇānuśaṃsā / pravrajyā cāsaṃskṛtā, asaṃskṛte ca na guṇā nānuśāṃsā / pravrajyā bhadantarāhula arūpiṇi rūpavigatā, panthā nirvāṇasya, praśaṃsitā paṇḍitaiḥ, parigṛhītāryaiḥ, parājayaḥ sarvamārāṇām, pañcagatyuttāraṇī, pañcacakṣuviśodhanī, pañcabalapratilambhā, pañcendriyapratiṣṭhā, pareṣām anupaghātaḥ, pāpadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭā, paratīrthyapramardanī, prajñaptisamatikrāntā, paṅke saṃkramaḥ, amamā mamakāravigatā, aparigrahā, anupādānā, anākulā, ākulaprahīṇā, svacittadarśanī paracittasaṃrakṣaṇī, śamathānukūlā, sarvato 'navadyā / iyam ucyate pravrajyā / ya evaṃ pravrajitās te supravrajitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.39 '"Venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, the benefits and advantages of going forth should not be explained in the way you explain them. For what reason? Going forth is without qualities and without advantages. Where, venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, there is conditioned activity, there are qualities and advantages. But going forth is unconditioned, and in the unconditioned there are no qualities or advantages. Going forth, venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, is formless, free from form; it is the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, praised by the wise, embraced by the noble ones; it is the defeat of all <s>Māras</s>; it is the crossing over of the five destinies; it is the purification of the five eyes; it is the attainment of the five powers; it is the establishment of the five faculties; it is the non-harming of others; it is unassociated with evil <s>dharmas</s>; it is the crushing of rival doctrines; it transcends conventional designation; it is a bridge across the mire; it is free from 'mine' and possessiveness; it is without attachment, without clinging, without entanglement, with entanglement abandoned; it manifests one's own mind and protects others' minds; it is favorable to <s>śamatha</s> (calm); it is faultless in every way. This is called 'going forth.' Those who have thus gone forth are well-gone-forth."'

body.text: Vkn 3.40 pravrajata yūyaṃ kumārakāḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye / durlabho hi buddhotpādaḥ, durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpat, durlabho manuṣyapratilambhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.40 '"Go forth, O youths, into the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>! For the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is rare, the conjunction of favorable conditions is rare, and the attainment of human birth is rare."'

body.text: te kumārakā evam āhuḥ: śrutam asmābhir gṛhapate, na tathāgato 'navasṛṣṭaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ pravrājayatīti /
body.translated_text: 'Those youths said: "We have heard, O householder, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not ordain one who has not been released by their parents."'

body.text: sa tān āha: utpādayata yūyaṃ kumārakāḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam / pratipattyā ca saṃpādayata, saiva yuṣmākaṃ bhaviṣyati pravrajyā sopasaṃpat /
body.translated_text: 'He said to them: "Generate, O youths, the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and accomplish it through practice — that itself will be your going forth with full ordination."'

body.text: Vkn 3.41 tatra dvātriṃśatā licchavikumārair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpāditāni / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.41 'Thereupon thirty-two <s>Licchavi</s> youths generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: Vkn 3.42 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvam ānanda vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 3.42 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: ānanda āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye bhagavataḥ kāyasya kaścid evābādhaḥ / tatra ca kṣīreṇa kṛtyam āsīt / so 'ham anyatamasmin brāhmaṇamahāśālasya gṛhamūle pātraṃ gṛhītvā sthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that at one time the body of the <s>Bhagavān</s> had some ailment, and milk was needed for treatment. So I stood holding my bowl at the entrance of the house of a certain great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder.'

body.text: vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ / sa māṃ vanditvaivam āha:
body.translated_text: The <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> arrived at that place. Having saluted me, he said:

body.text: Vkn 3.43 kiṃ bhadantānanda kālyam eva pātram ādāyāsmin gṛhadvārasamīpe tiṣṭhasi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.43) 'Why, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, do you stand early in the morning at this doorstep holding your bowl?'

body.text: tam enam aham etad avocam: bhagavato gṛhapate kāyasya kaścid evābādhaḥ / tatra ca kṣīreṇa kṛtyam, tat paryeṣāmi /
body.translated_text: I said to him: 'Householder, the body of the <s>Bhagavān</s> has some ailment, and milk is needed for treatment. That is what I am seeking.'

body.text: sa mām evam āha: alaṃ bhadantānanda mā evaṃ vocaḥ / vajrasaṃhatano hi bhadantānanda tathāgatakāyaḥ sarvākuśalavāsanāprahīṇaḥ sarvamahaujaskakuśaladharmasamanvāgataḥ / kutas tasya vyādhiḥ kuta upadravaḥ /
body.translated_text: He said to me: 'Enough, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>! Do not speak thus! For the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, is diamond-compact, with all impressions of unwholesome [deeds] abandoned, endowed with all supremely powerful wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Whence could there be illness for him? Whence affliction?'

body.text: Vkn 3.44 tūṣṇīṃbhūto bhadantānanda gaccha / mā bhagavantam abhyācakṣva / mā kasyacid bhūya evaṃ vocaḥ / mā mahaujaskā devaputrā anyabuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitāś ca bodhisatvāḥ śroṣyanti / rājñas tāvad bhadantānanda cakravartina itvarakuśalamūlasamanvāgatasya vyādhir na saṃvidyate / kutas tasya bhagavato 'pramāṇakuśalasamanvāgatasya vyādhir bhaviṣyati / nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate / gaccha gaccha bhadantānanda / mā mām adhyapatrāpaya, mā anyatīrthikacarakaparivrājakanigranthājīvāḥ śroṣyanti, mā teṣām evaṃ bhaviṣyati / kīdṛśo bata ayam eṣāṃ śāstā yaḥ svayam eva tāvad ātmānaṃ glānaṃ na śaknoti paritrātum, kutaḥ punar glānānāṃ satvānāṃ trāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati / tataḥ pracchannaṃ bhadantānanda gaccha śīghram / mā kaścic chṛṇuyāt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.44) 'Go silently, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Do not slander the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Do not ever speak thus again to anyone. Let not the mighty <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) and the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have assembled from other <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) hear this. Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, even a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), endowed with only limited roots of merit, has no illness — how much less will the <s>Bhagavān</s>, endowed with immeasurable merit, have illness? This situation does not exist. Go, go, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>! Do not bring shame upon me. Let not the wanderers of other sects (<s>tīrthikacarakas</s>), <s>parivrājakas</s>, <s>nirgranthas</s>, and <s>ājīvakas</s> hear this. Let them not think: "What kind of teacher is this, who cannot even save himself from illness — how then will he be a refuge for ailing beings?" Therefore, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, go secretly and quickly. Let no one hear.'

body.text: Vkn 3.45 api tu bhadantānanda dharmakāyās tathāgatā nāmiṣakāyāḥ / lokottarakāyās tathāgatāḥ sarvalokadharmasamatikrāntāḥ / anābādhas tathāgatasya kāyaḥ sarvāsravavinivṛtaḥ / asaṃskṛtas tathāgatasya kāyaḥ sarvasaṃkhyāvigataḥ / tasya bhadanto vyādhim icchatīty ayuktam asadṛśam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.45) 'But, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have <s>Dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body), not a material body. The <s>Tathāgatas</s> have a supramundane body, having transcended all worldly <s>dharmas</s>. The body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is without ailment, free from all <s>āsravas</s> (defilements). The body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), free from all enumeration. To wish illness upon such [a body], venerable sir, is improper and unfitting.'

body.text: Vkn 3.46 tasya me bhagavan mahadapatrāpyaṃ jātam / mā me bhagavato 'ntikād duḥśrutaṃ durgṛhītaṃ vā kṛtam iti / so 'ham antarīkṣāc chabdam aśrauṣam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.46) 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, was filled with great shame. [I thought:] "Perhaps I have misheard or poorly understood from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." Then I heard a voice from the sky:'

body.text: evam etad ānanda yathā gṛhapatir nirdiśati / atha ca punaḥ pañcakaṣāye bhagavān utpannaḥ, tenānarthalūhadaridracaryayā satvā vinetavyāḥ / tad gaccha tvam ānanda kṣīraṃ gṛhītvā, mā paryapatrapaś ceti /
body.translated_text: 'It is just as the householder describes, <s>Ānanda</s>. Nevertheless, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has appeared in the age of the five corruptions, and therefore beings must be disciplined through the conduct of poverty and wretchedness. So go, <s>Ānanda</s>, take the milk, and do not be ashamed.'

body.text: Vkn 3.47 īdṛśā bhagavan vimalakīrter licchaveḥ praśnavyākaraṇanirdeśāḥ / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya kulaputrasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.47) 'Such, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are the question-and-answer teachings of the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>. Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that son of good family to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: Vkn 3.48 evaṃ tāni pañcamātrāṇi śrāvakaśatāny anutsahamānāni bhagavate nivedayanti / ye ca tair vimalakīrtinā licchavinā sārdhaṃ kathāsaṃlāpāḥ kṛtās tān sarvān bhagavate nivedayanti sma /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.48) Thus did those approximately five hundred <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), declaring their inability, report to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And all the conversations they had had with the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, they reported to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: Vkn 3.49 tatra bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisatvam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ maitreya vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.49) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'Go, <s>Maitreya</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: maitreyo 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye saṃtuṣitena devaputreṇa sārdhaṃ tuṣitakāyikaiś ca devaputraiḥ sārdhaṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayāmi yad idaṃ bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānām avivartyāṃ bhūmim ārabhya / tatra ca vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ pradeśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām etad avocata:
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that at one time I was engaged in a conversation on the <s>Dharma</s> with the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> and the <s>devaputras</s> of the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven concerning the irreversible stage (<s>avivartyā bhūmi</s>) of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> came to that place and said to me:'

body.text: Vkn 3.50 tvaṃ maitreya ekajātipratibaddho bhagavatā vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tat katamayāsi maitreya jātyāu vyākṛtaḥ, kim atītayā vānāgatayota pratyutpannayā / tatra yātītā jātiḥ sā kṣīṇā, yāpy anāgatā sāpy asaṃprāptā, pratyutpannāyāḥ sthitir nāsti jāteḥ / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā: tathā hi tvaṃ bhikṣaḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe jāyase jīryasi mriyase cyavase upapadyase ceti / ajātitaś ca niyāmāvakrāntiḥ / na cājātir vyākriyate / nāpy ajātir abhisaṃbudhyate /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.50) 'You, <s>Maitreya</s>, have been predicted by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) as one birth away. Now in which birth have you been predicted, <s>Maitreya</s> — past, future, or present? If it is the past birth, that has ceased. If it is the future, that has not yet arrived. The present birth has no abiding. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: "Indeed, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, moment by moment you are born, you age, you die, you decease, and you are reborn." And from the perspective of being unborn, there is entry into the fixed course (<s>niyāmāvakrānti</s>). But what is unborn is not predicted. Nor does what is unborn attain awakening.'

body.text: Vkn 3.51 tat kathaṃ tvaṃ maitreya vyākṛtas tathatotpādena tathatānirodhena vā / na ca tathatotpadyate na nirudhyate, na nirotsyate / yā ca sarvasatvānāṃ tathatā, yā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ tathatā, saiva maitreyasyāpi tathatā / evaṃ yadi tvaṃ vyākṛtaḥ sarvasatvā api vyākṛtā bhavanti / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na hi tathatā dvayaprabhāvitā nānātvaprabhāvitā / tad yadā maitreyo bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate, sarvasatvā api tasmin samaye tādṛśīm eva bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / sarvasatvānubodho hi bodhiḥ / yadā ca maitreyaḥ parinirvāsyati, sarvasatvā api tadā parinirvāsyanti / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na hy aparinirvṛtānāṃ sarvasatvānāṃ tathāgatāḥ parinirvānti / parinirvṛtāni te satvāni paśyanti nirvāṇaprakṛtikāni / tasmād iha maitreya mā etān devaputrān ullāpaya mā visaṃvādaya /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.51) 'In what way, then, have you been predicted, <s>Maitreya</s> — through the arising of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) or through the cessation of <s>tathatā</s>? But <s>tathatā</s> neither arises nor ceases, nor will it cease. And the <s>tathatā</s> of all beings and the <s>tathatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s> is itself the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>Maitreya</s> as well. If you have been so predicted, then all beings too have been predicted. For what reason? Because <s>tathatā</s> is not produced by duality or plurality. When <s>Maitreya</s> will attain awakening, at that same time all beings too will attain such awakening. For what reason? Because awakening is the awakening of all beings. And when <s>Maitreya</s> will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, all beings too will then attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Because <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without all beings having attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. They see those beings as having the nature of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore, <s>Maitreya</s>, do not beguile and mislead these <s>devaputras</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 3.52 na bodhau kaścit pratiṣṭhate, na nivartate / api tu khalu punar maitreya yaiṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ bodhiparikalpanadṛṣṭis tām etām utsarjaya /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.52) 'No one is established in <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), nor does anyone turn back from it. But rather, <s>Maitreya</s>, you should help these <s>devaputras</s> abandon their view of conceptualizing awakening.'

body.text: na hi bodhiḥ kāyenābhisaṃbudhyate, na cittena / vyupaśamo bodhiḥ sarvanimittānām, asamāropo bodhiḥ sarvārambaṇānām, apracāro bodhiḥ sarvamanaskārāṇām, paricchedo bodhiḥ sarvadṛṣṭigatānām, vigamo bodhiḥ sarvaparikalpānām, visaṃyogo bodhiḥ sarveñjitamanyasyanditānām, anadhiṣṭhānaṃ bodhiḥ sarvapraṇidhānānām, asaṅgapraveśo bodhiḥ sarvodgrahavigatā, sthitā bodhir dharmadhātusthāne, anugatā bodhis tathatāyām, pratiṣṭhitā bodhir bhūtakoṭyām, advayā bodhir manodharmavigatā / samā bodhir ākāśasamatayā, asaṃskṛtā bodhir utpādabhaṅgasthityanyathātvavigatā, parijñā bodhiḥ sarvasatvacittacaritāśayānām, advārā bodhir āyatanānām, asaṃsṛṣṭā bodhiḥ sarvavāsanānusaṃdhikleśavigatā, na deśasthā na pradeśasthā bodhiḥ sthānāsthānavigatā, tathatāpratiṣṭhitā bodhiḥ sarvato 'dṛśyā / nāmadheyamātraṃ bodhis tac ca nāma nirīhakam, nirātmikā bodhir āyūhaniryūhavigatā, anākulā bodhiḥ prakṛtipariśuddhā, prakāśā bodhiḥ svabhāvapariśuddhā, anudgrahā bodhir adhyālambanavigatā, nirnānātvā bodhiḥ sarvadharmasamatāvabodhatvāt, anupamā bodhir upamopanyāsavigatāḥ, sūkṣmā bodhir duranubodhatvāt, sarvatrānugatā bodhir ākāśasvabhāvatvāt / sā na śakyā kāyena vācā cittenābhisaṃboddhum /
body.translated_text: 'For <s>bodhi</s> is not attained through the body nor through the mind. <s>Bodhi</s> is the quiescence of all signs. <s>Bodhi</s> is the non-superimposition of all supports. <s>Bodhi</s> is the non-activity of all mental engagements. <s>Bodhi</s> is the severance of all views. <s>Bodhi</s> is the departure from all conceptual constructions. <s>Bodhi</s> is the disjunction from all agitation, conceit, and outflows. <s>Bodhi</s> is the non-establishment of all aspirations. <s>Bodhi</s> is the entry into non-attachment, free from all grasping. <s>Bodhi</s> is established, established in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas). <s>Bodhi</s> follows <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). <s>Bodhi</s> is established at <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality). <s>Bodhi</s> is non-dual, free from mind and dharmas. <s>Bodhi</s> is equal, through equality with space. <s>Bodhi</s> is unconditioned, free from arising, destruction, abiding, and alteration. <s>Bodhi</s> is perfect knowledge of the mind-activities and dispositions of all beings. <s>Bodhi</s> is doorless, free from the sense-bases. <s>Bodhi</s> is unmixed, free from all impressions and defilement-continuities. <s>Bodhi</s> is not in any location or region, free from all spatial determination. <s>Bodhi</s> is established in <s>tathatā</s>, invisible everywhere. <s>Bodhi</s> is a mere name, and that name is without activity. <s>Bodhi</s> is without self, free from accumulation and dispersion. <s>Bodhi</s> is unconfused, pure by nature. <s>Bodhi</s> is luminous, pure in its own nature. <s>Bodhi</s> is without grasping, free from superimposition. <s>Bodhi</s> is without diversity, because it is the awakening to the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Bodhi</s> is without comparison, free from all analogies. <s>Bodhi</s> is subtle, because it is difficult to comprehend. <s>Bodhi</s> pervades everything, because it has the nature of space. It cannot be awakened to through body, speech, or mind.'

body.text: Vkn 3.53 iha bhagavan nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne tataḥ pariṣado dvayor devaputraśatayor anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt / ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.53) 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when this teaching was being proclaimed, two hundred <s>devaputras</s> in that assembly obtained the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). And I was struck speechless. Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: Vkn 3.54 tatra bhagavān prabhāvyūhaṃ licchavikumāram āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ satpuruṣa vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.54) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>Licchavi</s> youth <s>Prabhāvyūha</s>: 'Go, virtuous one, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: prabhāvyūho 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye bhagavan vaiśālyā mahānagaryā niṣkramāmi / vimalakīrtiś ca licchaviḥ praviśati / so 'haṃ tam abhivādyaivam avocam: kutas tvaṃ gṛhapate āgacchasīti /
body.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvyūha</s> also said: I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>: at one time, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I was going out of the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> while <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> was entering. I greeted him and asked: 'From where do you come, householder?'

body.text: sa mām evam āha: āgacchāmi bodhimaṇḍād iti /
body.translated_text: He said to me thus: 'I come from the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of enlightenment).'

body.text: tam aham etad avocam: bodhimaṇḍa iti kasyaitan nāma /
body.translated_text: I said to him: '<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> — what is this name for?'

body.text: sa mām etad avocat:
body.translated_text: He said to me:

body.text: Vkn 3.55 bodhimaṇḍa iti kulaputra āśayamaṇḍa eṣo 'kṛtrimatayā, prayogamaṇḍa eṣa ārambhottāraṇatayā, adhyāśayamaṇḍa eṣa viśeṣādhigamatayā, bodhicittamaṇḍa eṣo 'saṃpramoṣanatayā,
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.55) '<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, O son of good family: It is the seat of intention (<s>āśaya</s>) through its sincerity; the seat of application (<s>prayoga</s>) through its lifting one up from exertion; the seat of higher intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) through its attaining distinction; the seat of the mind of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>) through its non-forgetfulness;'

body.text: Vkn 3.56 dānamaṇḍa eṣa vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇatayā, śīlamaṇḍa eṣa praṇidhānaparipūraṇatayā, kṣāntimaṇḍa eṣa sarvasatvāpratihatacittatayā, vīryamaṇḍa eṣo 'vinivartanatayā, dhyānamaṇḍa eṣa cittakarmaṇyatayā, prajñāmaṇḍa eṣa pratyakṣadarśitayā,
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.56) 'the seat of generosity (<s>dāna</s>) through not expecting the fruit of ripening; the seat of morality (<s>śīla</s>) through the fulfillment of vows; the seat of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) through having an unobstructed mind toward all beings; the seat of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) through non-turning-back; the seat of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) through mental pliancy; the seat of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) through direct vision;'

body.text: Vkn 3.57 maitrīmaṇḍa eṣa sarvasatvasamacittatayā, karuṇāmaṇḍa eṣa khedasahiṣṇutayā, muditāmaṇḍa eṣa dharmārāmaratiratatayā, upekṣāmaṇḍa eṣo 'nunayapratighaprahāṇatayā,
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.57) 'the seat of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) through equanimous mind toward all beings; the seat of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) through endurance of hardship; the seat of sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) through delight in the garden of the <s>Dharma</s>; the seat of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) through the abandonment of attachment and aversion;'

body.text: Vkn 3.58 abhijñāmaṇḍa eṣa ṣaḍabhijñatayā, vimokṣamaṇḍa eṣo 'kalpanatayā, upāyamaṇḍa eṣa satvaparipācanatayā, saṃgrahavastumaṇḍa eṣa sarvasatvasaṃgrahanatayā, śrutamaṇḍa eṣa pratipattisārakatvāt, nidhyaptimaṇḍa eṣa yoniśaḥpratyavekṣaṇatayā, bodhipakṣyadharmamaṇḍa eṣa saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtotsarjanatayā, satyamaṇḍa eṣa sarvalokāvisaṃvādanatayā, pratītyasamutpādamaṇḍa eṣo 'vidyāsravakṣayatayā yāvaj jarāmaraṇāsravakṣayatayā, sarvakleśapraśamanamaṇḍa eṣa yathābhūtābhisaṃbodhanatayā,
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.58) 'the seat of superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>) through the six superknowledges; the seat of liberation (<s>vimokṣa</s>) through non-conceptualization; the seat of skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) through the ripening of beings; the seat of the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) through gathering all beings; the seat of learning (<s>śruta</s>) because practice is its essence; the seat of resolve (<s>nidhyapti</s>) through methodical investigation; the seat of the factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>) through the relinquishment of conditioned and unconditioned; the seat of truth (<s>satya</s>) through non-deception of the entire world; the seat of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) through the exhaustion of the defilements of ignorance down to the exhaustion of the defilements of old age and death; the seat of the pacification of all defilements through awakening to things as they really are;'

body.text: Vkn 3.59 sarvasatvamaṇḍa eṣa satvāsvabhāvatayā, sarvadharmamaṇḍa eṣa śūnyatābhisaṃbodhanatayā, sarvamāranirghātanamaṇḍa eso 'calanatayā, traidhātukamaṇḍa eṣa prasthānavigamanatayā, siṃhanādanadanavīryamaṇḍa eṣo 'bhītānutrāsanatayā, balavaiśāradyāveṇikasarvabuddhadharmamaṇḍa esa sarvato 'nupākruṣṭatvāt, traividyavidyāmaṇḍa esa niravaśeṣatvāt kleśānām, ekacittaniravaśeṣasarvadharmānubodhamaṇḍa eṣa sarvajñajñānasamudāgamatvāt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.59) 'the seat of all beings through the non-inherent-nature of beings; the seat of all <s>dharmas</s> through the awakening to emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>); the seat of the annihilation of all <s>Māras</s> through immovability; the seat of the three realms through departure from their course; the seat of the lion's roar through the vigor of fearlessness and courage; the seat of the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>) through being unassailable from all sides; the seat of the three knowledges (<s>traividyā</s>) through the complete exhaustion of defilements; the seat of the complete awakening to all <s>dharmas</s> in a single moment of mind through the attainment of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>).'

body.text: Vkn 3.60 iti hi kulaputra yāvanto bodhisatvāḥ pāramitāpratisaṃyuktaṃ satvaparipākapratisaṃyuktaṃ saddharmaparigrahapratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamūlapratisaṃyuktaṃ kramam utkṣipanti nikṣipanti ca / sarve te bodhimaṇḍād āgacchanti, buddhadharmebhya āgacchanti, buddhadharmeṣu ca pratiṣṭhante /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.60) 'Thus, O son of good family, as many <s>bodhisattvas</s> as there are who take up and set down the course connected with the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), connected with the ripening of beings, connected with the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s>, connected with the roots of merit — they all come from the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>, they come from the <s>Buddhadharmas</s>, and they stand established in the <s>Buddhadharmas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 3.61 iha bhagavan nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne pañcamātrair devamanuṣyaśatair bodhāya cittāny utpāditāni / ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.61) O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when this teaching was being taught, five hundred gods and humans generated the mind of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>). And I was struck speechless. Therefore I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: Vkn 3.62 tatra bhagavān jagatindharaṃ bodhisatvam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ jagatindhara vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.62) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Jagatindhara</s>: 'Go, <s>Jagatindhara</s>, to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> to inquire about his illness.'

body.text: jagatindharo 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: ekasmin samaye svake vihāre viharāmi / atha māraḥ pāpīyān dvādaśabhir apsaraḥsahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ śakraveṣeṇa tūryasaṃgītisaṃpravāditena yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasā vanditvā saparivāro māṃ puraskṛtyaikānte 'sthāt / tam enam ahaṃ jānāmi ḥ śakra eṣa devendra iti /
body.translated_text: <s>Jagatindhara</s> also said: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, am not able to go to that virtuous man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, O <s>Bhagavān</s>: at one time, I was dwelling in my monastery. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, accompanied by twelve thousand <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), in the guise of <s>Śakra</s>, with music and songs being played, approached me, bowed his head at my feet, and stood to one side together with his retinue, having placed me in front. I thought he was <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.'

body.text: tam aham etad avocam: svāgataṃ te kauśika, apramattena te bhavitavyaṃ sarvakāmaratiṣu, anityapratyavekṣanābahulenāttasāreṇa te bhavitavyaṃ kāyajīvitabhogebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: I said to him: 'Welcome, <s>Kauśika</s>. You should be heedful regarding all sensual pleasures. You should contemplate impermanence frequently and hold the essence from body, life, and possessions.'

body.text: sa mām evam āha: pratīccha tvaṃ satpuruṣa imāni dvādaśāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi mamāntikāt, etās te paricārikā bhavantām /
body.translated_text: He said to me thus: 'Accept, O virtuous man, these twelve thousand <s>apsaras</s> from me. Let them be your attendants.'

body.text: tam aham etad avocam: mā tvaṃ kauṣika akalpikena vastunā śramaṇān śākyaputrīyān nimantraya, yathā na hy etā asmākaṃ kalpyanta iti /
body.translated_text: I said to him: 'Do not, <s>Kauśika</s>, invite ascetics who are sons of the <s>Śākya</s> with what is inappropriate. These are not proper for us.'

body.text: Vkn 3.63 eṣā ca kathā pravṛttā, vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām evam āha: mā atra kulaputra śakrasaṃjñām utpādaya / māra eṣa pāpīyāṃs tava viheṭhanābhiprāya upasaṃkrāntaḥ, naiṣa śakra iti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.63) While this conversation was going on, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> approached. He said to me thus: 'O son of good family, do not produce the notion that this is <s>Śakra</s>. This is <s>Māra</s> the Evil One who has come with the intention of tormenting you; this is not <s>Śakra</s>.'

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ māraṃ pāpīyāṃsam etad avocat: asmabhyaṃ pāpīyan etā apsaraso niryātaya / asmākam etāḥ kalpyante, na śramaṇānāṃ śākyaputrīyāṇām iti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: 'Hand over these <s>apsaras</s> to us, Evil One. They are proper for us, not for ascetics who are sons of the <s>Śākya</s>.'

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīyān bhītas trastaḥ saṃvignaḥ / mā vimalakīrtinā licchavinā vipralapsya iti, icchati cāntardhātum, na ca śaknoti sarvarddhim api darśayitvāntardhātum / so 'ntarīkṣāc chabdam aśrauṣīt: niryātaya tvam etāḥ pāpīyan apsarasa etasmai satpuruṣāya, tataḥ śakṣyasi svabhavanaṃ gantum / atha māro bhītas trasto 'kāmako 'smai tā apsaraso niryātayati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One was frightened, terrified, and agitated. 'May I not be tricked by <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>,' he thought, and wished to vanish but could not, even after displaying all his supernatural power. He heard a voice from the sky: 'Hand over those <s>apsaras</s> to this virtuous man, Evil One, and then you will be able to go to your own abode.' Then <s>Māra</s>, frightened, terrified, and unwilling, handed over the <s>apsaras</s> to him.

body.text: Vkn 3.64 pratigṛhya ca vimalakīrtis tā apsarasa etad avocat: niryātitā yūyaṃ mahyaṃ māreṇa pāpīyasā, utpādayatedānīm anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam / sa tāsāṃ tadānulomikīṃ bodhiparipācanīṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā bodhau cittam utpādayati sma /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.64) Having received those <s>apsaras</s>, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to them: 'You have been given to me by <s>Māra</s> the Evil One. Now generate the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' Then he gave them a teaching suitable for ripening them toward enlightenment and aroused in them the mind of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>).

body.text: sa tā evam āha: utpāditam idānīṃ yuṣmābhir bodhicittam, dharmārāmaratiratābhir idānīṃ yuṣmābhir bhavitavyam, na kāmaratiratābhiḥ /
body.translated_text: He said to them: 'Now you have generated the mind of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>). From now on, you should delight in the pleasure of the <s>Dharma</s>, not in the pleasure of sensual desires.'

body.text: tāhuḥ: katamā ca punar dharmārāmaratiḥ /
body.translated_text: They asked: 'And what is the pleasure of the <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.text: sa āha: buddhe 'bhedyaprasādaratiḥ, dharme śuśrūṣaṇaratiḥ, saṃgha upasthānaratiḥ, guruṣu gauravopasthānaratiḥ, traidhātukān niḥsaraṇaratiḥ, viṣayeṣv aniśritaratiḥ, skandheṣu vadhakānityapratyavekṣaṇāratiḥ, dhātuṣv āśīviṣaparitulanāratiḥ, āyataneṣu śūnyagrāmavivekaratiḥ, bodhicittārakṣaṇaratiḥ, satveṣu hitavastutāratiḥ, dāne saṃvibhāgaratiḥ, śīleṣv aśaithilyaratiḥ, kṣāntyāṃ kṣamadamaratiḥ, vīrye kuśalasamudānayanaratiḥ, dhyāneṣu parikarmaratiḥ, prajñāyām apagatakleśāvabhāsaratiḥ, bodhau vistīrṇaratiḥ, mārasya nigraharatiḥ, kleśānāṃ praghātanāratiḥ, buddhakṣetrasya viśodhanāratiḥ, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanapariniṣpattyarthaṃ sarvakuśalamūlopacayaratiḥ, gambhīradharmaśravaṇānuttrāsaratiḥ, trivimokṣamukhaparijayaratiḥ, nirvāṇārambaṇaratiḥ, bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāraratiḥ, na cākālaprāptiratiḥ, sabhāgajanasevanāratiḥ, viṣabhāgeṣv adoṣāpratighātaratiḥ, kalyāṇamitreṣu sevāratiḥ, pāpamitreṣu visarjanāratiḥ, dharmaprītiprāmodyaratiḥ, upāye saṃgraharatiḥ, apramādabodhipakṣyadharmasevanāratiḥ / evaṃ hi bodhisatvo dharmārāmaratirato bhavati /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Pleasure in unbreakable faith in the <s>Buddha</s>; pleasure in listening to the <s>Dharma</s>; pleasure in attending upon the <s>Saṃgha</s>; pleasure in respectfully attending upon teachers; pleasure in departing from the three realms; pleasure in non-attachment to sense-objects; pleasure in contemplating the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as executioners and as impermanent; pleasure in regarding the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) as venomous serpents; pleasure in seclusion from the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) as from an empty village; pleasure in protecting the mind of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>); pleasure in the substance of benefit to beings; pleasure in sharing through generosity (<s>dāna</s>); pleasure in non-slackness in morality (<s>śīla</s>); pleasure in forbearance and restraint in patience (<s>kṣānti</s>); pleasure in accumulating wholesome qualities through vigor (<s>vīrya</s>); pleasure in mental cultivation through meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>); pleasure in the appearance of freedom from defilements through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); pleasure in the vast scope of enlightenment (<s>bodhi</s>); pleasure in subjugating <s>Māra</s>; pleasure in destroying defilements (<s>kleśa</s>); pleasure in purifying the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field); pleasure in accumulating all roots of merit for the sake of perfecting the marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>); pleasure in fearlessness upon hearing the profound <s>Dharma</s>; pleasure in mastery of the three gates of liberation (<s>trivimokṣamukha</s>); pleasure in the support of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; pleasure in adorning the seat of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>); and not pleasure attained at the wrong time; pleasure in associating with compatible people; pleasure in not being repelled by faults among incompatible people; pleasure in serving spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>); pleasure in abandoning evil friends; pleasure in the joy and delight of the <s>Dharma</s>; pleasure in gathering beings through skillful means (<s>upāya</s>); pleasure in diligently cultivating the factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>). Thus indeed does a <s>bodhisattva</s> delight in the pleasure of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 3.65 atha māraḥ pāpīyāṃs tā apsarasa etad avocat: āgacchata / idānīṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ svabhavanam iti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 3.65) Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One said to those <s>apsaras</s>: 'Come! Let us now go to our own abode.'

body.text: tā evam āhuḥ: niryātitā idānīṃ tvayā vayam asmai gṛhapataye / dharmārāmaratiratābhir asmābhir idānīṃ bhavitavyam, na kāmaratiratābhiḥ /
body.translated_text: They said: 'You have now given us to this householder. We must now delight in the pleasure of the <s>Dharma</s>, not in the pleasure of sensual desires.'

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīyān vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim evam āha: niḥsṛja tvaṃ gṛhapate imā apsarasaḥ / sarvasvaparityāgino bodhisatvā mahāsatvā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'Release these <s>apsaras</s>, householder! <s>Bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> give away all their possessions.'

body.text: vimalakīrtir āha: avasṛṣṭā bhavantu / gaccha pāpīyan / sarvasatvānāṃ dhārmikā abhiprāyāḥ paripūryantām /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'They are released. Go, Evil One! May the spiritual aspirations (<s>dhārmika abhiprāya</s>) of all beings be fulfilled.'

body.text: atha tā apsaraso vimalakīrtiṃ namaskṛtyaivam āhuḥ: kathaṃ vayaṃ gṛhapate mārabhavane 'vatiṣṭhema /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), having bowed to <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, spoke thus: How should we, householder, live in <s>Māra's</s> realm?

body.text: Vkn 3.66 āha: asti bhaginyaḥ akṣayapradīpaṃ nāma dharmamukham / tatra pratipadyadhvam / tat punaḥ katamat / tadyathā bhaginyaḥ ekasmāt tailapradīpād dīpaśatasahasrāṇy ādīpyante / na ca tasya dīpasya parihāṇir bhavati / evam eva bhaginyaḥ eko bodhisatvo bahūni satvaśatasahasrāṇi bodhau pratiṣṭhāpayati / na ca tasya bodhisatvasya cittasmṛtir hīyate, na parihīyate, uta ca vardhate / evaṃ sarvān kuśalān dharmān yathā yathā pareṣām ārocayati deśayati, tathā tathā vivardhate sarvaiḥ kuśalair dharmaiḥ / idaṃ tad akṣayapradīpaṃ nāma dharmamukham / tatra yuṣmābhir mārabhavane sthitābhir aparimāṇānāṃ devaputrāṇām apsarasāṃ ca bodhicittaṃ rocayitavyam / evaṃ yūyaṃ tathāgatasya kṛtajñā bhaviṣyatha / sarvasatvānāṃ copajīvyā bhaviṣyatha /
body.translated_text: He said: There is, sisters, a gateway to the <s>Dharma</s> called <s>Akṣayapradīpa</s> (the Inexhaustible Lamp). Practice in accordance with that. And what is it? Just as, sisters, from a single oil lamp, hundreds of thousands of lamps are kindled, and yet that lamp is not diminished — even so, sisters, a single <s>bodhisattva</s> establishes many hundreds of thousands of beings in <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), and yet that <s>bodhisattva's</s> mindfulness is not diminished, nor does it decline, but rather it increases. Likewise, the more one proclaims and teaches all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> to others, the more one grows in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. This is the gateway to the <s>Dharma</s> called <s>Akṣayapradīpa</s> (the Inexhaustible Lamp). While dwelling in <s>Māra's</s> realm, you should inspire <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) in immeasurable <s>devaputras</s> (sons of the gods) and <s>apsarases</s>. Thus you will be grateful to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and you will be a source of sustenance for all beings.

body.text: Vkn 3.67 atha tā apsaraso vimalakīrter licchaveḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā sārdhaṃ māreṇa prakrāntāḥ / ime bhagavan vimalakīrter licchaver vikurvaṇaviśeṣāḥ, yān ahaṃ nājñāsiṣam / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>apsarases</s>, having saluted with their heads the feet of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, departed together with <s>Māra</s>. These, Blessed One, are the extraordinary magical transformations of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, which I did not comprehend. Therefore I, Blessed One, am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: Vkn 3.68 tatra bhagavān sudattaṃ śreṣṭhiputram āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ kulaputra vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed <s>Sudatta</s>, the merchant's son: Go, son of good family, to inquire about the illness of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>.

body.text: sudatto 'py āha: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan: svake paitṛke niveśane mahāyajñaṃ yajāmi / sarvadaridraduḥkhitebhyaḥ sarvaśramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīyakayācanakebhyo dānaṃ dadāmi / saptadivasān mahāyajñaṃ yajāmi /
body.translated_text: <s>Sudatta</s> also said: I, Blessed One, am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness. For what reason? I recall, Blessed One: In my own paternal house I was performing a great sacrifice. I was giving gifts to all the poor and afflicted, to all <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics), <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, the destitute, and beggars. For seven days I was performing the great sacrifice.

body.text: tatra saptame divase vimalakīrtir licchavis tāṃ mahāyajñaśālāṃ praviśya mām etad avocat: na śreṣṭhiputra evaṃ yajño yaṣṭavyo yathā tvaṃ yajase / dharmayajñas te yaṣṭavyaḥ / kiṃ ta āmiṣayajñena /
body.translated_text: There, on the seventh day, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> entered that great sacrificial hall and said this to me: Son of the merchant, the sacrifice should not be performed in the way you are performing it. You should perform a <s>dharmayajña</s> (sacrifice of the Dharma). What use is a material sacrifice to you?

body.text: tam aham etad avocam: kathaṃ punar dharmayajño yaṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: I said this to him: How then should the <s>dharmayajña</s> (sacrifice of the Dharma) be performed?

body.text: sa mām evam āha:
body.translated_text: He spoke to me thus:

body.text: Vkn 3.69 yena dharmayajñenāpūrvācaramaṃ sarvasatvāḥ paripācyante, ayaṃ dharmayajñaḥ / sa punaḥ katamaḥ / yad idaṃ bodhyākārābhinirhṛtā mahāmaitrī, saddharmasaṃgrahābhinirhṛtā mahākaruṇā, sarvasatvaprāmodyārambanābhinirhṛtā mahāmuditā, jñānasaṃgrahābhinirhṛtā mahopekṣā,
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmayajña</s> (sacrifice of the Dharma) is that by which all beings are ripened without beginning or end. And what is it? It is: great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) brought forth from the qualities of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) brought forth from the gathering of the true <s>Dharma</s>, great <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) brought forth from having the delight of all beings as its object, and great <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) brought forth from the gathering of wisdom;

body.text: Vkn 3.70 śāntadāntābhinirhṛtā dānapāramitā, duḥśīlasatvaparipācanābhinirhṛtā śīlapāramitā, nairātmyadharmābhinirhṛtā kṣāntipāramitā, bodhyaṅgābhinirhṛtā vīryapāramitā, kāyacittavivekābhinirhṛtā dhyānapāramitā, sarvajñajñānābhinirhṛtā prajñāpāramitā,
body.translated_text: the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) brought forth from the peaceful and self-controlled, the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) brought forth from the ripening of immoral beings, the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) brought forth from the doctrine of non-self, the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) brought forth from the factors of awakening, the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) brought forth from the seclusion of body and mind, the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) brought forth from the knowledge of omniscience;

body.text: Vkn 3.71 sarvasatvaparipācanābhinirhṛtā śūnyatābhāvanā, saṃskṛtaparikarmābhinirhṛtānimittabhāvanā, saṃcintyopapattyabhinirhṛtāpraṇihitabhāvanā,
body.translated_text: the cultivation of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) brought forth from the ripening of all beings, the cultivation of the signless (<s>animitta</s>) brought forth from the preparation of the conditioned, the cultivation of the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>) brought forth from deliberate rebirth;

body.text: Vkn 3.72 saddharmaparigrahābhinirhṛto balaparākramaḥ, saṃgrahavastv abhinirhṛtaṃ jīvitendriyam, sarvasatvānāṃ dāsatvaśiṣyatvābhinirhṛtā nirmānatā, asārāt sārādānābhinirhṛtaḥ kāyajīvitabhogapratilambhaḥ, ṣaḍanusmṛtyabhinirhṛtā smṛtiḥ, saṃrañjaniyadharmābhinirhṛto 'dhyāśayaḥ, samyakpratipattyabhinirhṛtājīvapariśuddhiḥ, prasādaprāmodyasevanābhinirhṛtāryaparyupāsanā, anāryeṣv apratighātābhinirhṛtā cittanidhyaptiḥ, pravrajyābhinirhṛto 'dhyāśayaḥ, pratipattyabhinirhṛtaṃ śrutakauśalam, araṇādharmaprativedhābhinirhṛto 'raṇyavāsaḥ, buddhajñānasaṃprāpaṇābhinirhṛtaṃ saṃlayanam, sarvasatvakleśamocanayogābhinirhṛtā yogācārabhūmiḥ,
body.translated_text: the exertion of strength brought forth from the embrace of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the vital faculty brought forth from the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), humility brought forth from becoming the servant and disciple of all beings, the attainment of body, life, and possessions brought forth from extracting the essential from the inessential, mindfulness brought forth from the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections), right intention brought forth from qualities that inspire devotion, purity of livelihood brought forth from right practice, attendance upon the noble ones brought forth from the cultivation of faith and joy, patience toward the ignoble brought forth from freedom from aversion, right intention brought forth from renunciation, skill in learning brought forth from practice, forest-dwelling brought forth from penetrating the <s>Dharma</s> of non-conflict, meditative attainment brought forth from reaching the knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>, the stages of <s>yogācāra</s> (yogic practice) brought forth from the endeavor to liberate all beings from their <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

body.text: Vkn 3.73 lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasaṃbhārābhinirhṛtaḥ satvaparipākaḥ, buddhakṣetrālaṃkārābhinirhṛtaḥ puṇyasaṃbhāraḥ, sarvasatvacittacaritayathāśayadharmadeśanābhinirhṛto jñānasaṃbhāraḥ, sarvadharmānāyūhāniryūhaikanayajñanābhinirhṛtaḥ prajñāsaṃbhāraḥ, sarvakleśasarvāvaraṇasarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇābhinirhṛtaḥ sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhāraḥ,
body.translated_text: the ripening of beings brought forth from the accumulation of the marks and secondary characteristics, the accumulation of merit brought forth from the adornment of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the accumulation of knowledge brought forth from teaching the <s>Dharma</s> according to the minds, conduct, and dispositions of all beings, the accumulation of wisdom brought forth from knowing the single path of non-elaboration and non-exclusion of all <s>dharmas</s>, the accumulation of all roots of virtue brought forth from the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), all obstructions, and all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>;

body.text: Vkn 3.74 sarvajñajñānānubodhanasarvakuśaladharmābhinirhṛtaḥ sarvabodhipakṣyadharmasamudgamaḥ /
body.translated_text: the arising of all factors conducive to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) brought forth from the realization of omniscient knowledge and all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: ayaṃ sa kulaputra dharmayajñaḥ, yatra dharmayajñe pratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā iṣṭayajñayājūkā dakṣiṇīyā bhavanti sadevakasya lokasya / evaṃ hi bhagavan tasya gṛhapater nirdiśatas tasyā brāhmaṇaparṣado dvayor brāhmaṇaśatayor anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni /
body.translated_text: This, son of good family, is the <s>dharmayajña</s> (sacrifice of the Dharma). <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are established in this sacrifice of the <s>Dharma</s> become worthy recipients of offerings, worthy of veneration by the world including its gods. Thus indeed, Blessed One, as that householder was teaching, in that assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, two hundred <s>brāhmaṇas</s> generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).

body.text: Vkn 3.75 ahaṃ cāścaryaprasādapratilabdhas tasya satpuruṣasya caraṇau praṇamya śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ kaṇṭhād avatārya dadāmi / sa taiḥ muktāhāraṃ na pratigṛhṇāti sma / tam aham etad avocam: pratigṛhyemam, yatra te prasādo bhavati tasmai prayaccheti /
body.translated_text: And I, having obtained wondrous faith, bowed at the feet of that good man and, removing from my neck a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, I offered it to him. But he would not accept the pearl necklace. I said this to him: Please accept it and give it to whomever you are pleased to give it.

body.text: tena sa muktāhāro gṛhītvā dvidhākṛtaḥ / eko bhāgo yas tatra yajñaśālāyāṃ sarvalokajugupsito nagaradaridras tasmai dattaḥ / dvitīyaś ca bhāgo duṣprasahāya tathāgatāya dattaḥ / yathā ca sarvā parṣat paśyati taṃ ca marīciṃ lokadhātuṃ taṃ ca duṣprasahaṃ tathāgataṃ taṃ ca muktāhāraṃ duṣprasahasya mūrdhasaṃdhau muktāhārakūṭāgāraṃ prādurbhūtaṃ citraṃ darśanīyaṃ caturasraṃ catuḥsthūṇaṃ samaṃbhāgaśaḥ suvibhaktam /
body.translated_text: He then took the pearl necklace and divided it in two. One half he gave to the poorest beggar in that city, who was despised by all people in the sacrificial hall. The second half he offered to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Duṣprasaha</s> (Hard to Withstand). And the entire assembly saw that world-realm called <s>Marīci</s> (Mirage), and that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Duṣprasaha</s>, and that pearl necklace which appeared on the crown of <s>Duṣprasaha's</s> head as a jeweled pavilion, splendid, beautiful to behold, four-sided, with four pillars, well-proportioned on every side.

body.text: Vkn 3.76 sa idaṃ prātihāryaṃ saṃdarśyemāṃ vācam abhāṣata: yasya dāyakasya dānapater yādṛśī tathāgate dakṣiṇīyasaṃjñā tādṛśī nagaradaridre nirnānātvena samā, mahākaruṇācittena vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇatayā parityāgaḥ / iyaṃ dharmayajñasya paripūriḥ /
body.translated_text: Having displayed this miracle, he spoke these words: When the perception of a donor and lord of giving toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> as worthy of offerings is the same, without differentiation, toward the poorest beggar of the city — when the giving is done with a mind of great compassion, without expectation of karmic result — this is the fulfillment of the sacrifice of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: Vkn 3.77 tatrāsau nagaradaridra idaṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā, imaṃ ca dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayati sma / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
body.translated_text: Then that city beggar, having seen this miracle and having heard this teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). Therefore I, Blessed One, am not able to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

body.text: Vkn 3.78 iti hi sarve te bodhisatvā mahāsatvāḥ svakasvakān nirdeśān nirdiśanti sma, ye caiṣāṃ tena satpuruṣeṇa sārdham antarākathāsamudāhārā abhūvan, na cotsahante gantum // //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed all those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s> (great beings) described their respective encounters and the conversations they had had with that good man, and none were able to go.
