body.text: śrāvakabodhisatvavisarjanapraśno nāma tṛtīyaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, called "The Dismissal of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (Disciples) and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>."

body.text: Vkn 4.1 tatra bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam āmantrayate sma: gaccha tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful: Go, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, to inquire about the illness of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>.

body.text: mañjuśrīr apy āha: kiṃ cāpi durāsado 'sau bhagavan vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ, gambhīranayapratibhānapraviṣṭaḥ, vyastasamastavacananirhārakuśalaḥ, aviṣṭhitapratibhānaḥ, apratimabuddhiḥ sarvasatveṣu, sarvabodhisatvakriyāsu niryātaḥ, sarvabodhisatvasarvabuddhaguhyasthāneṣu supraviṣṭaḥ, sarvamārasthānavivartanakuśalamahābhijñāvikrīḍitaḥ, advayāsaṃbhedadharmadhātugocaraparamapāramiprāptaḥ, ekavyūhadharmadhātvanantākāravyūhadharmanirdeśakaḥ, sarvasatvendriyavyūhasaṃprāpaṇajñānakuśalaḥ, upāyakauśalyagatiṃgataḥ, prāptapraśnaviniścayaḥ / sa na śakyo 'lpakena saṃnāhenābhirādhayitum / atha ca punar gamiṣyāmi buddhādhiṣṭhānena, tatra yathāśakti yathābalaṃ nirdekṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> also said: Although, Blessed One, that <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> is difficult to approach — he has entered into the eloquence of profound method, is skilled in presenting arguments both separately and collectively, possesses inexhaustible eloquence, has incomparable intelligence toward all beings, has mastered all the activities of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, has fully penetrated all the secret places of all <s>bodhisattvas</s> and all <s>Buddhas</s>, is skilled in overturning all the abodes of <s>Māra</s> through his sport of great supernatural powers, has reached the highest perfection in the domain of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) which is non-dual and undivided, is one who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in infinite arrangements from the single array of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, is skilled in the knowledge of reaching the faculties of all beings in their various arrangements, has gone to the depth of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), and has attained the resolution of all questions — yet he cannot be satisfied with but a small effort. Nevertheless, I shall go, sustained by the <s>Buddha's</s> power, and there, to the best of my ability and strength, I shall engage in discourse.

body.text: Vkn 4.2 atha tataḥ parṣadas teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ teṣāṃ ca śrāvakāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca śakrabrahmalokapālānāṃ teṣāṃ ca devaputrāṇām etad abhavat: niścayena tatra mahādharmaśravaṇasāṃkathyaṃ bhaviṣyati, yatra mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sa ca satpuruṣa ubhau saṃlapiṣyataḥ / tatrāṣṭau ca bodhisatvasahasrāṇi pañcamātrāṇi ca śrāvakaśatāni saṃbahulāś ca śakrabrahmalokapālāḥ saṃbahulāni ca devaputraśatasahasrāṇi mañjuśriyam anubaddhāni dharmaśravaṇāya / atha mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtas tair bodhisatvair mahāsatvais taiś ca śrāvakais taiś ca śakrabrahmalokapālair devaputraiś ca parivṛto vaiśālīṃ mahānagarīṃ praviśati sma /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.2 Then this thought occurred to those in the assembly — to those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, those <s>śrāvakas</s>, those <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and <s>Lokapālas</s>, and those <s>devaputras</s>: 'Certainly, wherever <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful, and that good man meet, there will be a great hearing and discussion of the <s>Dharma</s>.' Thereupon eight thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, about five hundred <s>śrāvakas</s>, numerous <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and <s>Lokapālas</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of <s>devaputras</s> followed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful, surrounded by those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, those <s>śrāvakas</s>, those <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s>, and <s>devaputras</s>, entered the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text:
Vkn 4.3 atha vimalakīrter etad abhavat: ayaṃ mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūta āgacchati mahatā parivāreṇa / yan nv ahaṃ śūnyaṃ gṛham adhitiṣṭheyam / tena taṃ gṛhaṃ śūnyam adhiṣṭhitam apagatadvārapālam / na tatra mañcā vā pīṭhā vāsanāni vā saṃdṛśyante 'nyatraikasmān mañcāt, yatrātmanā glānaḥ samārūḍhaḥ śayitaḥ /
Vkn 4.4 atha mañjuśrīḥ saparivāro yena vimalakīrter niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya praviśati sma / sa taṃ gṛhaṃ śūnyam apaśyad vigatadvārapālam / na cātra mañcān vā pīṭhān vāpaśyad anyatraikamañcāt, yatra vimalakīrtiḥ śayitaḥ / atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam adrākṣīt / dṛṣṭvā ca punar evam āha: svāgataṃ mañjuśriyo 'svāgataṃ mañjuśriyo 'nāgatasyādṛṣṭaśrutapūrvasya darśanam /
body.translated_text:
Vkn 4.3 Then this thought occurred to <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'This <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful, is coming with a great retinue. Let me make my house empty by supernatural power.' By that power, his house was made empty, the doorkeeper was removed. No beds, seats, or chairs were visible there, except for a single bed on which he himself lay ill.
Vkn 4.4 Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, together with his retinue, approached <s>Vimalakīrti</s>'s dwelling. Having approached, he entered. He saw that house empty, without a doorkeeper. He saw no beds or chairs there except for the single bed on which <s>Vimalakīrti</s> lay. Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> saw <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful. Having seen him, he spoke thus: 'Welcome, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! Welcome, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! This is the appearance of one who has not come, who was never before seen or heard.'

body.text: mañjuśrir āha: evam etad gṛhapate yathā vadasi / ya āgato na sa bhūya āgamiṣyati / yaś ca gato na sa bhūyo gamiṣyati / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na cāgatasyāgamanaṃ prajñāyate, na ca gatasya gamanam, yaś ca dṛṣṭo na bhūyo draṣṭavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'It is so, householder, as you say. One who has come will not come again. One who has gone will not go again. For what reason? The coming of one who has come is not discerned, nor the going of one who has gone; and one who has been seen is not to be seen again.'

body.text: Vkn 4.5 api tu kaccit te satpuruṣa kṣapaṇīyam, kaccid yāpanīyam, kaccid vātena pratikupyanti dhātavaḥ, kaccid apagacchati vyādhir na vivardhate / bhagavāṃs te 'lpābādhatāṃ paripṛcchati, alpātaṅkatāṃ cālpaglānyatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yatrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.5 'But, good sir, are you bearing up? Are you getting along? Are the elements not aggravated by wind? Is your illness decreasing and not increasing? The <s>Bhagavān</s> inquires after your freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, freedom from sickness, lightness of rising, as well as your comfort, strength, ease, blamelessness, and easeful dwelling.'

body.text: Vkn 4.6 kutra te gṛhapate idaṃ vyādhisamutthānam / kiyacciram upādāya te vyādhiḥ / kadā copaśamiṣyati /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.6 'Where, householder, was the origin of this illness of yours? How long have you had it? And when will it subside?'

body.text: vimalakirtir āha: yāvacciram upādāya mañjuśrīḥ avidyā bhavatṛṣṇā ca tāvacciram upādāya mamaiṣa vyādhiḥ / yadā ca sarvasatvā vigatavyādhayo bhaviṣyanti tadā mama vyādhiḥ praśrabdho bhaviṣyati / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / satvādhiṣṭhāno hi mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvasya saṃsāraḥ / saṃsāraniśritaś ca vyādhiḥ / yadā sarvasatvā vigatavyādhayo bhaviṣyanti tadā bodhisatvo 'rogo bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> replied: 'As long, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the craving for becoming (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) have existed, so long have I had this illness. When all beings become free from illness, then my illness will be pacified. For what reason? The <s>bodhisattva</s>'s course in <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is grounded in beings. And illness is dependent upon <s>saṃsāra</s>. When all beings are free from illness, then the <s>bodhisattva</s> too will be free from illness.'

body.text: Vkn 4.7 tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ śreṣṭhina ekaputrako glāno bhavet / tasya mātāpitarāv api glānau syātām / tāvac ca duḥkhitau bhavetāṃ yāvan nāsāv ekaputrakas tayor vigatavyādhiḥ syāt / evaṃ mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvasya sarvasatveṣv ekaputrakaprema / sa satvaglānyena glāno bhavati, satvārogyāt tv arogaḥ / yat punar mañjuśriḥ evaṃ vadasi ḥ kutaḥ samutthito vyādhir iti, mahākaruṇāsamutthito bodhisatvānāṃ vyādhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.7 'For example, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, if the only son of a merchant were to fall ill, both his parents too would become ill; and they would remain distressed as long as that only son were not free from illness. Just so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> has the love of an only child for all beings. He falls ill when beings are ill, and he is well when beings are well. You further ask, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, "Where does this illness originate?" — the illness of <s>bodhisattvas</s> originates from <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion).'

body.text: Vkn 4.8 mañjuśrīr āha: śūnyaṃ te gṛhapate gṛham / na ca te kaścid upasthāyakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.8 <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Your house is empty, householder, and you have no attendant.'

body.text: āha: sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇy api mañjuśriḥ śūnyāni /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'All <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) too, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, are empty.'

body.text: āha: kena śūnyāni /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'By what are they empty?'

body.text: āha: śūnyatayā śūnyāni /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'They are empty by <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness).'

body.text: āha: śūnyatāyāḥ kā śūnyatā /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'What is the emptiness of emptiness?'

body.text: āha: aparikalpanāś ca śūnyatāyāḥ śūnyatāḥ /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Non-conceptualization is the emptiness of emptiness.'

body.text: āha: śakyā punaḥ śūnyatā parikalpayitum /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Can emptiness then be conceptualized?'

body.text: āha: yenāpi parikalpyeta tad api śūnyam / na ca śūnyatā śūnyatāṃ parikalpayati /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Even that by which one would conceptualize is also empty. And emptiness does not conceptualize emptiness.'

body.text: āha: śūnyatā gṛhapate kuto mārgitavyā /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Where, householder, should emptiness be sought?'

body.text: āha: śūnyatā mañjuśrīḥ dvāṣaṣṭibhyo dṛṣṭigatebhyo mārgitavyā /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Emptiness, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should be sought in the sixty-two wrong views.'

body.text: āha: dvāṣaṣṭiḥ punar dṛṣṭigatāni kuto mārgitavyāni /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Where again should the sixty-two wrong views be sought?'

body.text: āha: tathāgatavimuktito mārgitavyāni /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'They should be sought in the liberation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: āha: tathāgatavimuktiḥ punaḥ kuto mārgitavyā /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Where again should the liberation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> be sought?'

body.text: āha: sarvasatvacittacaritebhyo mārgitavyā / yat punar mañjuśrīḥ evaṃ vadasi ḥ kas ta upasthāyaka iti / sarvamārāḥ sarvaparapravādinaś ca mamopasthāyakāḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / mārā hi saṃsārasya varṇavādinaḥ / saṃsāraś ca bodhisatvasyopasthāyakaḥ / parapravādino dṛṣṭigatānāṃ varṇavādinaḥ / bodhisatvaś ca sarvadṛṣṭigatebhyo na calati / tasmāt sarvamārāḥ sarvaparapravādinaś ca mamopasthāyakāḥ /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'It should be sought in the mind-conduct of all beings. As for your further question, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, "Who is your attendant?" — all <s>Māras</s> and all heterodox teachers are my attendants. For what reason? <s>Māras</s> are those who praise <s>saṃsāra</s>, and <s>saṃsāra</s> is the attendant of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Heterodox teachers are those who praise wrong views, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not waver from any wrong view. Therefore all <s>Māras</s> and all heterodox teachers are my attendants.'

body.text: Vkn 4.9 mañjuśrīr āha: kidṛśo 'yaṃ te gṛhapate vyādhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.9 <s>Mañjuśrī</s> asked: 'What is the nature of this illness of yours, householder?'

body.text: āha: adṛśyo 'nidarśanaḥ /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'It is invisible and without indication.'

body.text: āha: kim eṣa vyādhiḥ kāyasaṃprayukta uta cittasaṃprayuktaḥ /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Is this illness associated with the body or associated with the mind?'

body.text: āha: na kāyasaṃprayuktaḥ kāyaviviktatayā / na cittasaṃprayukto māyādharmatayā cittasya /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'It is not associated with the body, because the body is devoid [of self]. Nor is it associated with the mind, because the mind has the nature of illusion.'

body.text: āha: catvāra ime gṛhapate dhātavaḥ / katame catvāraḥ, yad uta pṛthivīdhātur abdhātus tejodhātur vāyudhātur iti / tat katamas tatra dhātur bādhate /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Householder, there are these four elements (<s>dhātus</s>). Which are the four? Namely, the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the wind element. Which of these elements is afflicted?'

body.text: āha: ya evaṃ dhātuko mañjuśrīḥ sarvasatvānāṃ vyādhis tenāhaṃ vyādhitaḥ /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Whatever, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the elemental constitution of the illness of all beings — by that I am ill.'

body.text: Vkn 4.10 api tu khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ kathaṃ bodhisatvena glānako bodhisatvaḥ pratisaṃmoditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.10 'But further, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> comfort an ailing <s>bodhisattva</s>?'

body.text: mañjuśrīr āha: kāyānityatayā na ca nirvidvirāgatayā, kāyaduḥkhatayā na ca nirvāṇābhinandanatayā, kāyānātmatayā satvaparipācanatayā ca, kāyaśāntatayā na cātyantaśamatayā, sarvaduścaritadeśanatayā na ca saṃkrāntitaḥ, svaglānyena parasatvaglānakaruṇatayā, pūrvāntakoṭīduḥkhānusmaraṇatayā, satvārthakriyānusmaraṇatayā, kuśalamūlābhimukhīkaraṇatayā, ādiviśuddhatayā, aparitarṣaṇatayā, sadāvīryāraṃbhāc ca, vaidyarājo bhaviṣyasi sarvavyādhīnāṃ śamayiteti / evaṃ bodhisatvena bodhisatvo glānaḥ pratisaṃmoditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'By [reflecting on] the impermanence of the body, but not with disenchantment and dispassion; by [reflecting on] the suffering of the body, but not with delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>; by [reflecting on] the selflessness of the body, yet with the ripening of beings; by [reflecting on] the quiescence of the body, but not with ultimate cessation; by confessing all past misdeeds, but not as a transference [of fault]; by compassion for other beings' illness through one's own illness; by recollecting the suffering of the infinite past; by recollecting the welfare of all beings; by turning toward the roots of merit; by [reflecting on] original purity; by freedom from craving; and by the constant undertaking of vigor — [saying:] "You shall become a king of physicians, the pacifier of all diseases." Thus should a <s>bodhisattva</s> comfort an ailing <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 4.11 mañjuśrīr āha: kathaṃ kulaputra bodhisatvena glānena svacittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam /
body.translated_text: Vkn 4.11 <s>Mañjuśrī</s> asked: 'How, O son of good family, should an ailing <s>bodhisattva</s> control his own mind?'

body.text: vimalakīrtir āha: iha mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvena glānenaivaṃ svacittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam / pūrvāntāsadviparyāsakarmasamutthānasamutthito 'yaṃ vyādhir abhūtaparikalpakleśasamutthitaḥ / na punar atra kaścit paramārthato dharma upalabhyate yasyaiṣa vyādhiḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / cāturmahābhautiko 'yaṃ samucchrayaḥ / na caiṣāṃ dhātūnāṃ kaścit svāmī na samutthāpayitā / anātmā hy ayaṃ samucchrayaḥ / yo 'yaṃ vyādhir nāma nāyaṃ paramārthata upalabhyate, anyatrātmābhiniveśāt / uta nātmany abhiviniṣṭā vihariṣyāmo vyādhimūlaparijñātāvinaḥ / tenātmasaṃjñāṃ viṣṭhāpya dharmasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / dharmasaṃghāto 'yaṃ kāyaḥ / dharmā evotpadyamānā utpadyante / dharmā eva nirudhyamānā nirudhyante / te ca dharmāḥ parasparaṃ na cetayanti na jānanti / na ca teṣām utpadyamānānām evaṃ bhavaty utpadyāmaha iti / na nirudhyamānānām evaṃ bhavati nirudhyāmaha iti /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> replied: 'Here, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, an ailing <s>bodhisattva</s> should control his own mind thus: "This illness has arisen from the false delusion of <s>karma</s> of the beginningless past; it has arisen from the defilements of unreal conceptualization. But in ultimate reality, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is apprehended to which this illness belongs." For what reason? This physical frame is [merely] of the four great elements. And none of these elements has an owner or a producer. This physical frame is without self. This thing called illness is not ultimately apprehended, except through clinging to a self. Therefore we shall not dwell clinging to a self, having fully understood the root of illness. Thereby one should displace the notion of self and generate the notion of <s>dharma</s>: "This body is an aggregate of <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Dharmas</s> that arise simply arise; <s>dharmas</s> that cease simply cease. Those <s>dharmas</s> do not think about each other, do not know each other. When they arise, they do not think 'we arise,' and when they cease, they do not think 'we cease.'"'

body.text: Vkn 4.12 tena dharmasaṃjñāyā evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyam / yāpy eṣā dharmasaṃjñā so 'pi viparyāsaḥ / viparyāsaś ca mahāvyādhiḥ / vigatavyādhikena ca mayā bhavitavyam / vyādhiprahāṇāya ca yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tatra katamad vyādhiprahāṇam, yad idam ahaṃkāramamakāraprahāṇam / tac ca katamad ahaṃkāramamakāraprahāṇam, yad idaṃ dvayavigamaḥ / tatra katamo dvayavigamaḥ, yad idam adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā ca samudācāraḥ / tatra katamo 'dhyātmaṃ bahirdhā samudācāraḥ, yad uta samatayācalanatāpracalanatā / katamā ca samatā / ātmasamatayā ca nirvāṇasamatā / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / ubhe 'py ete śūnye, yad utātmā nirvāṇaṃ ca / kenaite śūnye / nāmodāhāreṇaite śūnye / ubhāv apy etāv apariniṣpannau, yad utātmā nirvāṇaṃ ca / tena samadarśinā nānyo vyādhir nānyā śūnyatā kartavyā / vyādhir eva śūnyatā /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.12) 'Regarding the perception of <s>Dharma</s>, one should generate this thought: "Even this perception of <s>Dharma</s> is a <s>viparyāsa</s> (delusion). And delusion is a great illness. I must become free from illness, and effort must be made for the abandonment of illness." And what is the abandonment of illness? It is the abandonment of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense) and <s>mamakāra</s> (possessiveness). And what is the abandonment of ego-sense and possessiveness? It is the departure from duality. And what is the departure from duality? It is the equal conduct regarding the internal and the external. And what is the equal conduct regarding the internal and external? It is non-movement, non-agitation through equanimity. And what is equanimity? The equanimity of the self and the equanimity of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Because both of these are empty — namely, the self and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. How are they empty? They are empty by mere verbal designation. Both are without ultimate reality — namely, the self and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For one who sees with such equanimity, illness is not to be made into something other than emptiness. Illness itself is emptiness.'

body.text: Vkn 4.13 aviditā ca sā vedanā veditavyā / na cānena vedanānirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ / aparipūrṇeṣu buddhadharmeṣūbhe vedane notsraṣṭavye / na ca durgatyupapannānāṃ satvānām antike mahākaruṇā notpādayitavyā / tathā kariṣyāmo yathaiṣāṃ satvānām evam ayoniśonidhyaptyā vyādhim apaneṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.13) 'And that sensation (<s>vedanā</s>) which is unknown should be known. Yet one should not realize the cessation of sensation directly. When the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> are not yet fulfilled, one should not abandon both [pleasant and painful] sensations. Nor should one fail to generate great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward beings who have been reborn in miserable destinies. We shall act in such a way as to remove the illness of these beings that arises from such unwholesome mental attention.'

body.text: Vkn 4.14 na caiṣāṃ kaṃcid dharmam upaneṣyāmo nāpaneṣyāmaḥ / yato nidānāc ca punar vyādhir utpadyate tasya parijñāyai tebhyo dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmaḥ / katamac ca punar nidānam, yad idam adhyālambananidānam / yāvatādhyālambananidānam adhyālambate, tāvad vyādhinidānam / kiṃ cādhyālambate, traidhātukam adhyālambate / tasyādhyālambanatayā kā parijñā, yad idam ālambanānupalambhaḥ / yaṃ hi nopalabhyate taṃ nālambate / kiṃ ca nopalabhate, ubhe dṛṣṭī nopalabhate, yad idam ātmadṛṣṭiṃ paradṛṣṭiṃ ca / tad ucyate 'nupalambha iti / evaṃ hi mañjuśrīḥ glānena bodhisatvena svacittaṃ nidhyapayitavyaṃ jarāvyādhimaraṇopapattiprahāṇāya / evaṃ ca mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvānāṃ bodhir yadi na bhavet, nirarthako nanu vyāyāmo bhavet / yathā pratyarthikanirghātāc churā ity ucyante, evam eva jarāvyādhimaraṇaduḥkhopaśamanād bodhisatvā ity ucyante /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.14) 'And we shall neither bring any <s>dharma</s> to them nor take any away. And to bring them to the thorough understanding of the source from which illness arises, we shall teach them the <s>Dharma</s>. And what is that source? It is the source of superimposition (<s>adhyālambana</s>). As long as one superimposes the source of superimposition, so long does the source of illness persist. And what does one superimpose? One superimposes the three realms. And what is the thorough understanding of that superimposition? It is the non-apprehension of any support. What one does not apprehend, one does not superimpose upon. And what does one not apprehend? One does not apprehend both views — namely, the view of self and the view of other. This is called non-apprehension. Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should the ailing <s>bodhisattva</s> attend to his own mind, for the abandonment of old age, illness, death, and rebirth. This, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the awakening of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. If it did not exist, the effort would be purposeless. Just as [warriors] are called "heroes" (<s>śūra</s>) because they vanquish the adversary, so too are they called <s>bodhisattvas</s> because they alleviate the suffering of old age, illness, and death.'

body.text: Vkn 4.15 tena bodhisatvena vyādhitenaivaṃ pratyavekṣitavyam / yathā mama vyādhir abhūto 'sann evaṃ sarvasatvānām api vyādhir abhūto 'sann iti / tasyaivaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇasya nānuśaṃsādṛṣṭipatitā satveṣu mahākaruṇotpadyate, anyatrāgantukakleśaprahāṇābhiyuktyā satveṣu mahākaruṇotpadyate / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / anuśaṃsadṛṣṭipatitayaiva hi mahākaruṇayā bodhisatvasya khedo bhavaty upapattiṣu / anuśaṃsadṛṣṭiparyutthānavigatayā punar mahākaruṇayā bodhisatvasya khedo na bhavaty upapattiṣu / so 'yam upapadyate, na ca dṛṣṭiparyutthānaparyutthita upapadyate / so 'paryutthitacitta upapadyamāno mukta evotpadyate mukta eva jāyate / sa mukta evotpadyamāno mukta eva jāyamāno baddhānāṃ satvānāṃ śaktaḥ pratibalo bandhamokṣāya dharmaṃ deśayitum / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā sa tāvad ātmanā baddhaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti nādaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate / yas tv ātmanā muktaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti sthānam etad vidyate tasmān muktena bodhisatvena bhavitavyam, na baddhena /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.15) 'The ailing <s>bodhisattva</s> should reflect thus: "Just as my illness is unreal and non-existent, so too the illness of all beings is unreal and non-existent." While reflecting thus, there should not arise in him toward beings a great compassion that has fallen into the view of [seeking] benefit — rather, great compassion should arise toward beings that is directed to the abandonment of adventitious defilements. For what reason? Because it is precisely great compassion that has fallen into the view of benefit that causes weariness for the <s>bodhisattva</s> in his rebirths. But great compassion that is free from the secondary defilement of the view of benefit does not cause weariness for the <s>bodhisattva</s> in his rebirths. He is reborn, but is not reborn overwhelmed by the secondary defilement of views. Being reborn with an unobstructed mind, he arises as one who is liberated, is born as one who is liberated. And being born as one who is liberated, he has the power and ability to teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the release from bondage of bound beings. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: "That one who is himself bound will free another from bondage — this situation does not exist. But one who is himself free will free another from bondage — this situation does exist." Therefore the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be liberated, not bound.'

body.text: Vkn 4.16 tatra katamo bandhaḥ, katamo mokṣaḥ / anupāyād bhavagatiparigraho bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ, upāyād bhavagatigamanaṃ mokṣaḥ / anupāyād dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ, upāyena dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā mokṣaḥ / anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ, upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ / prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhanam, prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.16) 'And what is bondage, what is liberation? Grasping at the realms of existence without <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) is bondage for the <s>bodhisattva</s>; going to the realms of existence with <s>upāya</s> is liberation. Relishing <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) without <s>upāya</s> is bondage for the <s>bodhisattva</s>; relishing <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s> with <s>upāya</s> is liberation. <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) not embraced by <s>upāya</s> is bondage; <s>prajñā</s> embraced by <s>upāya</s> is liberation. <s>Upāya</s> not embraced by <s>prajñā</s> is bondage; <s>upāya</s> embraced by <s>prajñā</s> is liberation.'

body.text: Vkn 4.17 tatra katamo 'nupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ, yad idaṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitanidhyaptiḥ, na ca lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyaptiḥ / iyam anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ / tatra katamopāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ, yad idaṃ lakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyapticittaṃ ca śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitaparijayaś ca / iyam upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ / tatra katamaḥ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ, yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighapratiṣṭhitasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau cāpariṇāmanā / ayaṃ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ / tatra katamaḥ prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ, yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighaprahīṇasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau pariṇāmitas tasya cāparāmarśaḥ / ayaṃ bodhisatvasya prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.17) 'And what is <s>prajñā</s> not embraced by <s>upāya</s> that is bondage? It is the contemplation of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), and wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), but not the contemplation of the marks, secondary characteristics, <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) adornment, and the ripening of beings. This is <s>prajñā</s> not embraced by <s>upāya</s> — it is bondage. And what is <s>prajñā</s> embraced by <s>upāya</s> that is liberation? It is the contemplation of the marks, secondary characteristics, <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> adornment, and the ripening of beings, along with mastery of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. This is <s>prajñā</s> embraced by <s>upāya</s> — it is liberation. And what is <s>upāya</s> not embraced by <s>prajñā</s> that is bondage? It is the undertaking of all roots of merit while being established in all views, defilements, secondary defilements, latent dispositions, attachment, and aversion, without dedication to awakening. This is <s>upāya</s> not embraced by <s>prajñā</s> — it is bondage. And what is <s>upāya</s> embraced by <s>prajñā</s> that is liberation? It is the undertaking of all roots of merit, having abandoned all views, defilements, secondary defilements, latent dispositions, attachment, and aversion, dedicated to awakening, without clinging to that [dedication]. This is <s>upāya</s> embraced by <s>prajñā</s> for the <s>bodhisattva</s> — it is liberation.'

body.text: Vkn 4.18 tatra mañjuśrīḥ glānena bodhisatvenaivam ime dharmā nidhyapayitavyāḥ / yatl kāyasya cittasya ca vyādheś cānityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmapratyavekṣaṇā, iyam asya prajñā / yat punaḥ kāyavyādhipariharaṇatayā na khidyate, na pratibadhnāti saṃsāram, satvārthayogam anuyuktaḥ, ayam asyopāyaḥ / punar aparaṃ yat kāyasya vyādheś cittasya cānyonyaparāparatāṃ na nirnavatāniḥpurāṇatāṃ pratyavekṣate, iyam asya prajñā / yat punaḥ kāyasya vyādheś cittasya ca nātyantopaśamaṃ nirodham atyayati, ayam asyopāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.18) 'Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should the ailing <s>bodhisattva</s> attend to these <s>dharmas</s>. The reflection on the impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self of the illness of body and mind — this is his <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Not becoming weary or despairing over the illness of body, not binding oneself to <s>saṃsāra</s>, and being engaged in the welfare of beings — this is his <s>upāya</s> (skillful means). Furthermore, reflecting on the illness of body and mind without investigating their mutual succession, their novelty or antiquity — this is his <s>prajñā</s>. Not seeking the ultimate cessation and extinction of the illness of body and mind — this is his <s>upāya</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 4.19 evaṃ hi mañjuśriḥ glānena bodhisatvena cittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam / na ca tena nidhyaptau vānidhyaptau vā sthātavyam / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / yadi hy anidhyaptau tiṣṭhed bāladharma eṣaḥ / atha nidhyaptau tiṣṭhec chrāvakadharma eṣaḥ / tasmād bodhisatvena na nidhyaptau sthātavyam / yad atrāsthānam ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 4.19) 'Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should the ailing <s>bodhisattva</s> attend to the mind. And one should abide neither in contemplation nor in non-contemplation. For what reason? If one abides in non-contemplation, that is the way of the foolish. If one abides in contemplation, that is the way of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers). Therefore the <s>bodhisattva</s> should not abide in contemplation [alone]. That which is neither abiding [in contemplation] nor [non-contemplation] — this is the domain of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text:
Vkn 4.20 yan na pṛthagjanagocaro nāryagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat saṃsāragocaraś ca na ca kleśagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yan nirvāṇapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na cātyantaparinirvāṇagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac caturmārasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca sarvamāraviṣayātikrāntagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat sarvajñajñānaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cākāle jñānaprāptigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac catuḥsatyajñānagocaraś ca na cākāle satyaprativedhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad adhyātmapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavopapattiparigrahagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad ajātipratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na ca niyāmāvakrāntigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat pratītyasamutpādagocaraś ca sarvadṛṣṭivigatagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat sarvasatvasaṃgaṇikāgocaraś ca na ca kleśānuśayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad vivekagocaraś ca na ca kāyacittakṣayaniśrayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat traidhātukagocaraś ca na ca dharmadhātusaṃbhedagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac chūnyatāgocaraś ca sarvākāraguṇaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad ānimittagocaraś ca satvapramocanārambaṇavitarkagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad apraṇihitagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavagatisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad anabhisaṃskāragocaraś ca sarvakuśalamūlābhisaṃskārāpratiprasrabdhigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat ṣaṭpāramitāgocaraś ca sarvasatvacittacaritapāragamanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat ṣaḍanusmṛtigocaraś ca na ca sarvāsravakṣayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat saddharmapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca na ca kumārgādhyālambanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat ṣaḍabhijñāgocaraś ca na cāsravakṣayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac caturapramāṇagocaraś ca na ca brahmalokopapattisparśanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad dhyānasamādhisamāpattigocaraś ca na ca samādhisamāpattivaśenopapattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat smṛtyupasthānagocaraś ca na ca kāyavedanācittadharmātyarthagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat samyakprahāṇagocaraś ca na ca kuśalākuśaladvayopalambhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad ṛddhipādābhinirhāragocaraś cānābhogarddhipādavaśavartigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat pañcendriyagocaraś ca sarvasatvendriyaparāparajñānagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat pañcabalapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca daśatathāgatabalābhisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat saptabodhyaṅgapariniṣpattigocaraś ca buddhiprabhedajñānakauśalyagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yan mārgapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca kumārgānadhyālambanagocaraś ca,
ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac chamathavidarśanāsaṃbhāraparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cātyantaśāntipatanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad anutpādalakṣaṇasarvadharmamīmāṃsanagocaraś ca rūpalakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakāyālaṃkārapariniṣpattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac chrāvakapratyekabuddhākalpasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca buddhadharmātyajanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad atyantaviśuddhiprakṛtisamāpannasarvadharmānugamanagocaraś ca yathādhimuktisarvasatveryāpathasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad atyantāsaṃvartavivartākāśasvabhāvasarvabuddhakṣetrapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca nānāvyūhānekavyūhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad dharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca bodhisatvacaryātyajanagocaraś ca, ayam api bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
body.translated_text:
(Vkn 4.20) That which is neither the domain of ordinary persons nor the domain of noble ones — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of <s>saṃsāra</s> yet not the domain of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of contemplating <s>nirvāṇa</s> yet not the domain of final <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of seeing the four <s>Māras</s> yet the domain of having transcended the sphere of all <s>Māras</s> — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of seeking omniscient knowledge yet not the domain of attaining knowledge at the wrong time — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of knowledge of the four noble truths yet not the domain of penetrating the truths at the wrong time — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of inner contemplation yet also the domain of intentionally taking birth in existence — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of contemplating non-arising yet not the domain of entering the fixed course (<s>niyāmāvakrānti</s>) — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) yet also the domain free from all views — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of association with all beings yet not the domain of latent defilements (<s>kleśānuśaya</s>) — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of solitude yet not the domain of relying on the destruction of body and mind — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of the three realms yet not the domain of breaking apart the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas) — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) yet also the domain of seeking all forms and qualities — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>) yet also the domain of deliberation aimed at liberating beings — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>) yet also the domain of intentionally displaying the courses of existence — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of non-conditioning yet also the domain of not relaxing the conditioning of all wholesome roots — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) yet also the domain of crossing to the far shore of all beings' mental activities and dispositions — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections) yet not the domain of the destruction of all <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of establishing the true <s>Dharma</s> yet not the domain of relying on false paths — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) yet not the domain of the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) yet not the domain of touching rebirth in the <s>Brahmaloka</s> — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) yet not the domain of rebirth through the power of concentration and attainment — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) yet not the domain of excessive focus on body, feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) yet not the domain of apprehending the duality of wholesome and unwholesome — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of accomplishing the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) yet also the domain of mastering supernatural power effortlessly — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>) yet also the domain of knowing the superiority and inferiority of all beings' faculties — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of establishing the five powers (<s>bala</s>) yet also the domain of displaying the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of perfecting the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) yet also the domain of skill in the discernment of wisdom — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of establishing the path yet also the domain of not relying on false paths —
that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of seeking the provisions of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vidarśanā</s> (insight) yet not the domain of falling into utter quiescence — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of investigating all <s>dharmas</s> as having the characteristic of non-arising yet also the domain of perfecting the adornment of the <s>Buddha</s>-body with marks and secondary characteristics — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of displaying the manner of the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> yet also the domain of not abandoning the <s>Buddhadharmas</s> — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of following all <s>dharmas</s> as endowed with utterly pure inherent nature yet also the domain of displaying the conduct of all beings according to their aspirations — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of contemplating all <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) as having the nature of space, utterly beyond formation and destruction, yet also the domain of displaying the adornment of <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> qualities with diverse and manifold arrays — that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain. That which is the domain of displaying the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Dharma-wheel) and <s>mahāparinirvāṇa</s> (great final nirvāṇa) yet also the domain of not abandoning the <s>bodhisattva</s>-practice — that too is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s domain.

body.text: iha nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne ye mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena sārdham āgatā devaputrās tato 'ṣṭānāṃ devaputrasahasrāṇām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni // //
body.translated_text: When this teaching was being expounded, eight thousand <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) who had come with <s>Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta</s> generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). //

body.text: glānapratisaṃmodanāparivartaś caturthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, called <s>Glānapratisaṃmodanā</s> (Inquiring After the Illness). //

body.text: Vkn 5.1 athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat: kutreme bodhisatvā niṣatsyanti, ime ca mahāśrāvakāḥ / neha gṛha āsanāni saṃvidyante /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.1) Then this thought occurred to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Where will these <s>bodhisattvas</s> sit, and these great <s>śrāvakas</s>? There are no seats to be found in this house.'

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetovitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram etad avocat: kiṃ bhadantaśāriputro dharmārthika āgata utāsanārthikaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, knowing the thought of the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>'s mind, said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Have you come seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, or seeking a seat?'

body.text: āha: dharmārthikā vayam āgatā nāsanārthikāḥ /
body.translated_text: He said: 'We have come seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, not seeking seats.'

body.text: Vkn 5.2 āha: tena hi bhadantaśāriputra yo dharmarthiko bhavati, nāsau svakāyārthiko bhavati / kiṃ punar āsanārthiko bhaviṣyati / yo bhadantaśāriputra dharmārthiko bhavati, na sa rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānārthiko bhavati, na skandhadhātvāyatanārthikaḥ / yo dharmārthikaḥ, na sa kāmadhāturupadhātvārūpyadhātvarthiko bhavati, nāsau buddhābhiniveśārthiko bhavati, na dharmasaṃghābhiniveśārthikaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.2) He said: 'In that case, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, one who seeks the <s>Dharma</s> does not seek even his own body. How much less will he seek a seat? One who seeks the <s>Dharma</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, does not seek form, feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; he does not seek the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), or <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). One who seeks the <s>Dharma</s> does not seek the desire-realm, the form-realm, or the formless realm. He does not seek attachment to the <s>Buddha</s>, nor attachment to the <s>Dharma</s> or the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 5.3 punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra yo dharmārthikaḥ, nāsau duḥkhaparijñānārthiko na samudayaprahāṇārthiko na nirodhasākṣātkriyārthiko na mārgabhāvanārthiko bhavati / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / aprapañco hi dharmo nirakṣaraḥ / tatra yaḥ prapañcayati ḥ duḥkhaṃ parijñāsyāmi samudayaṃ prahāsyāmi nirodhaṃ sākṣātkariṣyāmi mārgaṃ bhāvayiṣyāmīti, nasau dharmārthikaḥ, prapañcārthiko 'sau / dharmo hi bhadantaśāriputra upaśāntaḥ / tatra ya utpādavyaye caranti, na te dharmārthikā na vivekārthikāḥ, utpādavyayārthikās te / dharmo hy arajo rajo'pagataḥ / tatra ye kvacid dharme rakṣante 'ntaśo nirvāṇe 'pi, na te dharmārthikāḥ, rajo'rthikās te / dharmo hy aviṣayaḥ / ye viṣayasaṃkhyātāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, viṣayārthikās te / dharmo nāyūho niryūhaḥ / ye kecid dharmaṃ gṛhṇanti vā muñcanti vā, na te dharmārthikāḥ, udgrahaniḥsargārthikās te /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.3) 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, one who seeks the <s>Dharma</s> does not seek the full understanding of suffering, nor the abandonment of the origin, nor the realization of cessation, nor the cultivation of the path. For what reason? The <s>Dharma</s> is free from conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>), beyond syllables. One who engages in conceptual elaboration, thinking "I shall fully understand suffering, abandon the origin, realize cessation, and cultivate the path" — he is not a seeker of the <s>Dharma</s> but a seeker of conceptual elaboration. The <s>Dharma</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is quiescent. Those who pursue arising and perishing are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s>, nor seekers of solitude — they are seekers of arising and perishing. The <s>Dharma</s> is dustless, free from dust. Those who are attached to any <s>dharma</s>, even to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> — they are seekers of dust. The <s>Dharma</s> is not an object of perception. Those who are enumerated by objects of perception are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> — they are seekers of objects. The <s>Dharma</s> is not to be taken up or set down. Those who grasp or release any <s>dharma</s> are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> — they are seekers of grasping and releasing.'

body.text: Vkn 5.4 dharmo 'nālayaḥ / ya ālayārāmāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, ālayārthikās te / dharmo nirnimittaḥ / yeṣāṃ nimittānusārivijñānam, na te dharmārthikāḥ, nimittārthikās te / dharmo 'saṃvāsaḥ / ye kecid dharmeṇa sārdhaṃ saṃvasanti, na te dharmārthikāḥ, saṃvāsārthikās te / dharmo 'dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātaḥ / ye dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāteṣu caranti, na te dharmārthikāḥ, dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātārthikās te /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.4) 'The <s>Dharma</s> is without abode. Those who delight in abodes are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> — they are seekers of abodes. The <s>Dharma</s> is without signs. Those whose consciousness follows signs are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> — they are seekers of signs. The <s>Dharma</s> cannot be dwelt in. Those who dwell together with the <s>Dharma</s> are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> — they are seekers of dwelling. The <s>Dharma</s> is not seen, heard, thought, or cognized. Those who pursue what is seen, heard, thought, or cognized are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> — they are seekers of the seen, heard, thought, and cognized.'

body.text: Vkn 5.5 dharmo bhadantaśāriputra asaṃskṛtaḥ saṃskṛtāpagataḥ / ye saṃskṛtagocarāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, saṃskṛtodgrahaṇārthikās te / tasmād iha bhadantaśāriputra dharmārthikena te bhavitukāmena sarvadharmānarthikena bhavitavyam / iha dharmanirdeśe nirdiśyamāne pañcānāṃ devaputraśatānāṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur viśuddham /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.5) The <s>Dharma</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), free from conditioned things. Those whose domain is conditioned things are not seekers of the <s>Dharma</s> but seekers of grasping conditioned things. Therefore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, one who wishes to be a seeker of the <s>Dharma</s> should not seek anything in any <s>dharma</s>. When this teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> was being proclaimed, the <s>Dharmacakṣus</s> (Dharma-eye) was purified for five hundred <s>devaputras</s> regarding <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: Vkn 5.6 atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam āmantrayate sma: tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ daśasu dikṣv asaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakṣetraśatasahasreṣu buddhakṣetracārikāṃ carasi / tat katarasmin buddhakṣetre tvayā sarvaviśiṣṭāni sarvaguṇopetāni siṃhāsanāni dṛṣṭāni / evam ukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat: asti kulaputra pūrve digbhāge ṣaṭtriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya merudhvajā nāma lokadhātuḥ / tatra merupradīparājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati / tasya tathāgatasya caturaśītiyojanaśatasahasra ātmabhāvaḥ / aṣṭaṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasraṃ tasya bhagavataḥ siṃhāsanam / teṣāṃ ca bodhisatvānāṃ catvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasra ātmabhāvaḥ / catustriṃśadyojanaśatasahāsrāni teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ siṃhāsanāni / merudhvajāyāṃ lokadhātau tasya bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetre sarvaviśiṣṭāni sarvagunopetāni siṃhāsanāni /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.6) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful: 'You, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, wander through innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions. In which <s>buddhakṣetra</s> have you seen the most excellent lion-thrones (<s>siṃhāsana</s>) endowed with all qualities?' When this was said, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'There is, O son of good family, in the eastern direction, passing through as many <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as there are grains of sand in thirty-six Ganges rivers, a world-system called <s>Merudhvajā</s>. There the <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Merupradīparāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, abides, endures, and lives. That <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body measures eighty-four hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. That <s>Bhagavān</s>'s lion-throne measures sixty-eight hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s>' bodies measure forty hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>' lion-thrones are thirty-four hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. In the world-system <s>Merudhvajā</s>, in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s>, the lion-thrones are the most excellent and endowed with all qualities.'

body.text: Vkn 5.7 atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samanvāhāraṃ samanvāharati sma / tādṛśaṃ carddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskṛtavān, yat tato merudhvajālokadhātor dvātriṃśatsiṃhāsanaśatasahasrāṇi tena bhagavatā merupradīparājena tathāgatena preṣitāni / tāvad udviddhāni tāvad vistīrṇāni tāvad darśanīyāni yad apūrvāṇi tair bodhisatvais taiś ca mahāśrāvakais taiś ca śakrabrahmalokapālair devaputraiś ca / tāny upary antarīkṣeṇāgatya vimalakirter licchaver niveśane pratyatiṣṭhan / tac ca gṛhaṃ tāvad vistīrṇaṃ saṃdṛśyate, yatra tāni dvātriṃśatsiṃhāsanaśatasahasrāṇi vicitrāṇy anutpīḍanatayā / na ca vaiśālyā mahānagaryā āvaraṇaṃ kṛtam, na jambūdvīpasya, na cāturdvīpikasyāvaraṇam / sarve te tathaiva saṃdṛśyante yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.7) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> at that moment directed his mental determination and performed such a supernatural feat that from the world-system <s>Merudhvajā</s>, thirty-two hundred thousand lion-thrones were sent by that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s> — so tall, so wide, so magnificent, as had never been seen before by those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, those <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s>, and <s>devaputras</s>. Those thrones, coming through the air from above, stood within the dwelling of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>. And that house appeared so spacious that those thirty-two hundred thousand magnificent lion-thrones were accommodated without crowding. And no obstruction was made to the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, nor to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, nor to the four-continent world. Everything appeared just as it had been before.

body.text: Vkn 5.8 atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam etad avocat: niṣida tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ siṃhāsane sārdham etair bodhisatvaiḥ / tādṛśāṃś cātmabhāvān adhitiṣṭhata yat siṃhāsaneṣv anurūpāḥ syuḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.8) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful: 'Sit, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, upon a lion-throne together with these <s>bodhisattvas</s>! Transform your bodies to such a size as would be appropriate for the lion-thrones.'

body.text: atha ye 'bhijñāpratilabdhā bodhisatvās te dvācatvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasram ātmabhāvam adhiṣṭhāya teṣu siṃhāsaneṣu nisīdanti sma / ye cādikarmikā bodhisatvās te na śaknuvanti sma teṣu siṃhāsaneṣu niṣattum /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had attained the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), having transformed their bodies to forty-two hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, sat upon those lion-thrones. But the beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> were unable to sit upon those lion-thrones.

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma: niṣīda bhadantaśāriputra siṃhāsane /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Sit, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, upon a lion-throne.'

body.text: āha: na śaknomi satpuruṣa niṣattum uccāni pragṛhitāni cemāni siṃhāsanāni /
body.translated_text: He said: 'I am unable, O virtuous man, to sit upon them — these lion-thrones are so tall and elevated.'

body.text: āha: tena hi bhadantaśāriputra tasyaiva bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya namaskāraṃ kuru / tataḥ śakṣyasi niṣattum /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Then, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, pay homage to that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s>. Then you will be able to sit.'

body.text: atha te mahāśrāvakās tasya bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya namaskāraṃ kurvanti sma / te tatra paścāt teṣu siṃhāsaneṣu nyaṣīdan /
body.translated_text: Then those great <s>śrāvakas</s> paid homage to that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Merupradīparāja</s>. Thereafter they sat upon those lion-thrones.

body.text: Vkn 5.9 athāyuṣmāñ śāriputro vimalakirtiṃ licchavim evam āha: āścaryaṃ kulaputra yad ihaivaṃ parītte gṛha imānīyanti siṃhāsanasahasrāṇy evam uccāny evaṃ pragṛhītāni vicitrāṇi / na ca vaiśālyā mahānagaryā āvaraṇaṃ kṛtam, na jambūdvīpasya, na grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīnām, na cāturmahādvīpikasya kiṃcid āvaraṇam, na devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāṇām āvaraṇaṃ kṛtam / tathaiva saṃdṛśyante yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.9) Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'It is wonderful, O son of good family, that in this very small house, so many thousands of lion-thrones, so tall, so elevated, so magnificent, are brought in! And no obstruction is made to the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, nor to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, nor to the villages, cities, market-towns, settlements, kingdoms, and capitals, nor to the four-continent world — no obstruction at all; nor to the gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>. Everything appears just as it was before.'

body.text: Vkn 5.10 vimalakīrtir āha: asti bhadantaśāriputra tathāgatānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ cācintyo nāma vimokṣaḥ, yatrācintyavimokṣe pratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ tāvad uccaṃ tāvat pragṛhītaṃ tāvad udviddhaṃ tāvad vistīrṇaṃ sarṣapaphalakośe praveśayet / na ca sarṣapaphalakośaṃ vivardhayet / na ca sumeruṃ hāpayet / tāṃ ca kriyām ādarśayet / na cāturmahārājakāyikā devās trayastriṃśato vā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ / anye ca satvā ṛddhivineyā jānīyuḥ paśyeyus taṃ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ sarśapaphalakośapraviṣṭam / ayaṃ bhadantaśāriputra bodhisatvānām acintyasya vimokṣasya viṣayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.10) <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'There is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a liberation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> called "Inconceivable" (<s>acintya</s>). A <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the Inconceivable Liberation could insert Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, so tall, so elevated, so vast, so wide, into a mustard seed. The mustard seed would not expand, nor would <s>Sumeru</s> diminish. And he could display this deed. The <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods would not know: "Where have we been placed?" But other beings who are to be disciplined through supernatural power would know and see that Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, had entered the mustard seed. This, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the entry into the domain of the Inconceivable Liberation (<s>acintyavimokṣa</s>) of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 5.11 punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo yaś caturṣu mahāsamudreṣv apskandhas tam ekasmin romakūpe prakṣipet / na ca matsyakacchapaśiśumāramaṇḍūkānām anyeṣāṃ vaudakānāṃ prāṇināṃ pīḍā bhavet / na ca nāgayakṣagandharvāsurāṇām evaṃ bhavet ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ / sā ca kriyā prajñāyeta / na ca kaścit satvo vihiṃsito viheṭhito vā bhavet /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.11) 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the Inconceivable Liberation could place the water-mass of the four great oceans in a single hair-pore. There would be no distress to the fish, turtles, crocodiles, frogs, or other aquatic beings. Nor would the <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Asuras</s> think: "Where have we been placed?" And this deed would be evident. Nor would any being be harmed or tormented.'

body.text: Vkn 5.12 imaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ bhārgavacakram iva parigṛhya dakṣiṇe pāṇāv avabhrāmya gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān lokadhātūn kṣipet / na ca satvā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ nītāḥ, kuto vāgatā iti / punar api cānāyya yathāsthānaṃ sthāpayet / na ca gamanāgamanaṃ saṃjānīran / sā ca kriyā saṃdṛśyeta /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.12) 'And taking this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world system) like a potter's wheel in the right palm and spinning it, he could cast it beyond world-systems equal to the sands of the Ganges. And beings would not know: "Where have we been taken? Or where did we come from?" And he could bring it back and set it in its original place, and they would not perceive any going or coming. And this deed would be evident.'

body.text: Vkn 5.13 punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra santi satvā apramāṇasaṃsāravainayikāḥ / santi saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravainayikāḥ / tatrācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo 'pramāṇasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya saptarātraṃ kalpam atikrāntam ādarśayet / saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya kalpaṃ saptarātram atikrāntam ādarśayet / tatrāpramāṇasaṃsāravineyāḥ satvāḥ saptarātraṃ kalpam atikrāntaṃ saṃjānīran I saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravineyāḥ satvāḥ kalpaṃ saptarātram atikrāntaṃ saṃjānīran /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.13) 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there are beings who can be disciplined through an immeasurable duration of <s>saṃsāra</s>. There are beings who can be disciplined through a shortened duration of <s>saṃsāra</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the Inconceivable Liberation, in order to discipline those beings who need an immeasurable <s>saṃsāra</s>, could show seven nights as having passed as a <s>kalpa</s> (eon). For those beings who need a shortened <s>saṃsāra</s>, he could show a <s>kalpa</s> as having passed as seven nights. Those beings needing an immeasurable <s>saṃsāra</s> would perceive seven nights as having passed as a <s>kalpa</s>. Those beings needing a shortened <s>saṃsāra</s> would perceive a <s>kalpa</s> as having passed as seven nights.'

body.text: Vkn 5.14 iti hy acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān ekasmin buddhakṣetre saṃdarśayati / sarvasatvān api dakṣiṇe karatale pratiṣṭhāpya cittajāyikayarddhyā kramet / sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu ca saṃdarśanaṃ dadyāt / na caikato 'pi kṣetrāc calet / yāvatyaś ca daśasu dikṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā vartante, tāḥ sarvā ekaromakūpa ādarśayet / yāvantaś ca daśasu dikṣu candrasūryās tārārūpāni ca, tāny api sarvāṇy ekaromakūpa ādarśayet / yāvatyaś ca daśasu dikṣu vātamaṇḍalyaḥ pravānti, tā api sarvā mukhadvāre praveśayet / na cāsya kāyo vikīryeta / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre tṛṇavanaspatayo nameyuḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.14) 'Thus a <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the Inconceivable Liberation can display all the arrays of the qualities of all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. He can also place all beings in the right palm of his hand and, through mind-born supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), travel and display himself in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> without moving from any single field. He can reveal in a single hair-pore all the offerings being made to the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions. He can also reveal in a single hair-pore all the suns and moons and constellations in the ten directions. He can also draw into his mouth all the wind-circles that blow in the ten directions, without his body being scattered and without the trees and forests in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> bending.'

body.text: Vkn 5.15 yāni ca daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrāṇy uddahyante kalpoddāhena, tad api sarvam agniskandhaṃ svamukhe prakṣipet / yac ca tena karma kartavyaṃ bhavet, tac ca kuryāt / yac cāvastād gaṅgānadīvālikākoṭīsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣv atikramya buddhakṣetram, tad abhyutkṣipyordhaṃ digbhāgaṃ gaṅgānadīvālikākoṭīsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet / tadyathāpi nāma balavān puruṣaḥ sūcyagreṇa badarīpatram utkṣipet /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.15) 'And whatever <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) in the ten directions are consumed by the <s>kalpa</s>-fire (eon-conflagration), all that mass of fire he would take into his own mouth, and it would perform whatever function it was to perform. And whatever <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> lies below, having passed beyond <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> equal to the sands of the Ganges River multiplied by tens of millions, he would lift it up and place it in the upper region of space upon <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> equal to the sands of the Ganges River multiplied by tens of millions. Just as a strong man would lift up a <s>badarī</s> (jujube) leaf on the tip of a needle.'

body.text: Vkn 5.16 evam acṃtyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sarvasatvāni cakravartyādirūpāṇy adhitiṣṭhet /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.16) 'Thus a <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the <s>acintyavimokṣa</s> (inconceivable liberation) can manifest all beings in the form of <s>cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs) and the like through supernatural transformation.'

body.text: Vkn 5.17 yāvantaś ca daśasu dikṣu śabdāvabhāsāḥ śabdaprajñāptayaḥ, tāḥ sarvā hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭānāṃ satvānāṃ sarvabuddhaghoṣarutaracitāny adhitiṣṭhan, tataś ca rutaghoṣād anityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmaśabdarutāni niścārayet / yāvadbhiś cākāranirdeśair daśasu dikṣu buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayanti, tāṃs tato rutanirghoṣān niścārayet /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.17) 'And whatever sound-manifestations and verbal designations exist in the ten directions — all those he would transform for beings of lesser, middling, and superior [capacity] into sounds and utterances composed of all <s>Buddha</s>-voices, and from those sounds and utterances he would cause to issue forth the sounds of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. And whatever modes of expression by which the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, in the ten directions teach the <s>Dharma</s>, he would cause all those sounds and resonances to issue forth.'

body.text: Vkn 5.18 ayaṃ bhadantaśāriputra acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ yatkiṃcinmātro viṣayāvatāranirdeśaḥ / api tu kalpam ahaṃ bhadantaśāriputra kalpāvaśesaṃ vācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ viṣayānāṃ viṣayāvatāranirdeśaṃ nirdiśeyam, ato vottari /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.18) 'This, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is but a brief indication of the domain-entry of <s>bodhisattvas</s> established in the <s>acintyavimokṣa</s> (inconceivable liberation). But I, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, could describe the domain-entry of the domains of <s>bodhisattvas</s> established in the inconceivable liberation for a <s>kalpa</s> (eon) or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>, and even more than that.'

body.text: Vkn 5.19 atha khalu sthaviro mahākāśyapa imaṃ bodhisatvānām acintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptaḥ sthaviraṃ śāriputram etad avocat: tadyathāpi nāma āyuṣmañ śāriputra jātyandhasya puruṣasya purastāt kaścid eva sarvarūpagatāny upadarśayet / na ca tatra sa jātyandha ekarūpam api paśyet / evam eva āyuṣmañ śāriputra ihācintyavimokṣe nirdiśyamāne sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā iha jātyandhā iva cakṣurvihīnā ekasminn apy acintyakāraṇe na pratyakṣāḥ / ko nāma vidvān imam acintyaṃ vimokṣaṃ śrutvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpādayet / tat kiṃ nu bhūyaḥ kariṣyāmo 'tyantopahatendriyā dagdhavinaṣṭānīva bījāny abhājanībhūtā iha mahāyāne / sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhair imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā rudadbhis trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur vijñāpayitavyaḥ / sarvabodhisatvaiś ca pramuditair imam acintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvā mūrdhnā saṃpratyetavyaḥ, adhimuktibalaṃ ca saṃjanayitavyam / yasyaiṣācintyavimokṣādhimuktiḥ sarvamārās tasya kiṃ kariṣyanti / imaṃ nirdeśaṃ nirdiśataḥ sthavirasya mahākāśyapasya dvātriṃśatā devaputrasahasrair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.19) Then the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, upon hearing this inconceivable liberation of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, was filled with wonder and said to the elder <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Just as, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, if someone were to display all manner of forms before a man born blind, that blind man would not see even a single form — just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, when this inconceivable liberation is being taught, all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas) are like those born blind, devoid of eyes, unable to perceive even a single inconceivable aspect. What learned person, having heard this inconceivable liberation, would not generate the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)? What more shall we do, we whose faculties are utterly damaged, like seeds that are burnt and destroyed, having become unfit vessels for this <s>Mahāyāna</s>? All <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, should weep loudly enough to fill this billion-world system! And all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having heard this inconceivable liberation with joy, should accept it upon the crown of their heads and generate the power of firm resolve (<s>adhimukti</s>). Whoever has firm resolve in this inconceivable liberation — what can all <s>Māras</s> do to him?' When the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> was delivering this teaching, thirty-two thousand <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) generated the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening).

body.text: Vkn 5.20 atha vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ sthaviraṃ mahākāśyapam evam āha: yāvanto bhadantamahākāśyapa daśasu dikṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu mārā māratvaṃ kārayanti, sarve te yadbhūyasācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā upāyakauśalyena satvaparipācanāya māratvaṃ kārayanti / yāvadbhir bhadantamahākāśyapa daśasu dikṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu bodhisatvā yācanakair yācyante hastapādān vā karṇanāsaṃ vā śoṇitaṃ snāyuṃ vāsthimajjānaṃ vā netrāṇi vottamāṅgāni śirāṃsi vāṅgapratyaṅgāni vā rājyarāṣṭrajanapadān vā bhāryāputraduhitṝr vā dāsadāsīr vā hayagajarathavāhanāni vā suvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍamaṇiratnajātaṃ vānnapānāni rasān vā, vastrāṇi cotpīḍya yācyante, sarve te yācanakā yadbhūyasācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā upāyakauśalyenemāṃ dṛḍhādhyāśayatāṃ darśayanti / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / ugratapaso hi bhadantamahākāśyapa bodhisatvās ta evaṃ darśayanti / nāsti hi prākṛtajanasyāsthānānavakāśakṛtasya bodhisatvam utpīḍayitum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 5.20) Then the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said to the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: 'All the <s>Māras</s> who exercise the power of <s>Māra</s> in the immeasurable world-systems of the ten directions, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> — all of them, for the most part, are <s>bodhisattvas</s> established in the inconceivable liberation who, through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), exercise the power of <s>Māra</s> for the ripening of beings. And all those who ask <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the immeasurable world-systems of the ten directions for gifts — their hands and feet, ears and nose, blood, sinews, bones, marrow, eyes, heads, limbs and appendages, kingdoms, countries, provinces, wives, sons, daughters, male and female servants, horses, elephants, chariots, vehicles, gold, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystal, coral, gem-treasures, food, drink, flavors, and garments, pressing and importuning them — all those beggars, for the most part, are <s>bodhisattvas</s> established in the inconceivable liberation who, through <s>upāyakauśalya</s>, display this firm resolve. For what reason? Because, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> practice fierce <s>tapas</s> (austerities) and display [these situations] in this way. For an ordinary person has no power or opportunity to oppress a <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhadantamahākāśyapa na śaktir asti khadyotakasya sūryamaṇḍalaprabhām abhibhavitum / evam eva bhadantamahākāśyapa na śaktir asti prākṛtasya janasya bodhisatvenānavakāśakṛtasyopasaṃkramituṃ yācituṃ vā / tadyathā bhadantamahākāśyapa yo hastināgasya prahāro na sa śakyo gardabhena soḍhum / evam eva bhadantamahākāśyapa na śakyam abodhisatvena bodhisatvasyotpīḍanaṃ soḍhum / bodhisatva eva bodhisatvotpīḍāṃ sahate / ayaṃ bhadantamahākāśyapa acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānām upāyajñānabalapraveśaḥ // //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, a firefly has no power to overpower the light of the sun's disk, just so, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, an ordinary person has no power to approach or solicit a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has given him no opportunity. Just as, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the blow of a mighty elephant cannot be endured by a donkey, just so, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the oppression of a <s>bodhisattva</s> cannot be endured by one who is not a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Only a <s>bodhisattva</s> can endure the oppression of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. This, venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, is the entry into the power of the knowledge of skillful means of <s>bodhisattvas</s> established in the inconceivable liberation.'

body.text: acintyavimokṣasaṃdarśanaparivartaḥ pañcamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, called <s>Acintyavimokṣasaṃdarśana</s> (The Demonstration of the Inconceivable Liberation).

body.text: Vkn 6.1 atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat: kathaṃ satpuruṣa bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.1) Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful, said to the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>: 'How, O virtuous one, should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings?'

body.text:
āha: tadyathāpi nāma mañjuśrīḥ vijñapuruṣa udakacandram avekṣeta, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma mañjuśrīḥ ādarśamaṇḍale mukhamaṇḍalam ālokayet, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ marīcikāyām udakam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ māyākāro māyākāranirmitaṃ puruṣam avekṣeta, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ pratiśrutkāyā rutaghoṣaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ gagane 'bhrakūṭam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ phenapiṇḍasya pūrvāntaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśriḥ udakabudbudānām utpādavyayaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ kadalyāḥ sāradarśanam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ vidyutaḥ saṃkrāntiḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ pañcamo dhātuḥ / evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ saptamam āyatanam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ ārūpyeṣu rūpāvabhāsaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ paritaptānāṃ bījānām aṅkurapariniṣpattiḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ maṇḍūkaromapravāraḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ mṛtasya kāmakrīḍāratiḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ srotaāpannasya satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśriḥ sakṛdāgāminas tṛtīyo bhavaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ anāgāmino garbhāvakrāntiḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśriḥ arhataḥ rāgadoṣamohāḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ kṣāntipratilabdhasya bodhisatvasya mātsaryadauḥśīlyavyāpādavihiṃsācittāni, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ tathāgatasya kleśavāsanā, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ jātyandhasya puruṣasya rūpadarśanam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ nirodhasamāpannasyāśvāsāḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ ākāśe śakunipadam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ paṇḍakasyendriyasya prādurbhāvaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ bandhyāyāḥ putrapratilambhaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ tathāgatanirmitasyānutpannāḥ kleśāḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena
sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ svapnadarśanapratibuddhasya darśanam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśriḥ aparikalpayataḥ kleśāḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ anupādānasyāgneḥ saṃbhavaḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ parinirvṛtasya pratisaṃdhiḥ, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ / evaṃ hi mañjuśrīr bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a wise person would regard the moon reflected in water — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, one would see one's own face in a mirror — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, water [appears] in a mirage — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a magician would regard a person created by magic — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the sound of an echo — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a mass of clouds in the sky — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prior end of a mass of foam — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the arising and destruction of water bubbles — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, one would look for the core of a plantain trunk — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the passing of lightning — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a fifth element — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a seventh sense-base — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the appearance of form in the formless realms — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the sprouting of scorched seeds — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a garment made of frog's hair — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the enjoyment of sensual pleasure by a dead person — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the view of the composite self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) in a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a third existence for a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the descent into the womb for a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>) — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, desire, hatred, and delusion in an <s>arhat</s> — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, thoughts of avarice, immorality, malice, and harmfulness in a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance) — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the residual impressions of defilements in a <s>Tathāgata</s> — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the seeing of forms by one born blind — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the breathing of one who has entered the cessation-attainment — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a bird's track in the sky — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the appearance of the sexual faculty in a eunuch — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the obtaining of a son by a barren woman — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the unarisen defilements of a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s magical creation — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the seeing of one awakened from a dream [sees the dream] — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the defilements of one who does not conceptualize — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the arising of a fire without fuel — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the rebirth-connection of one who has attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings. Thus indeed, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should a <s>bodhisattva</s> regard all beings.'

body.text: Vkn 6.2 āha: yadi kulaputraivaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ, kathaṃ punar asya mahāmaitrī bhavati sarvasatveṣu /
body.translated_text: Vkn 6.2 He asked: 'If, O son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> should thus regard all beings, how then does his great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward all beings arise?'

body.text: āha: yadā mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatva evaṃ pratyavekṣate, mayā hy eṣāṃ satvānām evaṃ dharmaparijñāyai dharmo deśayitavya iti, ato 'sya bhūtā satvatrāṇamaitrī sarvasatveṣūtpadyate 'nārambaṇatayā, upaśamamaitry anutpādanatayā, niṣparidāhamaitrī niḥkleśatayā, yathāvadmaitrī tryadhvasamatayā, avirodhamaitry aparyupasthānatayā, advayamaitry adhyātmabahirdhāsaṃsṛṣṭatayā, akopyamaitry atyantaniṣṭhatayā, dṛḍhamaitrī vajradṛḍhābhedyāśayatayā, śuddhamaitrī prakṛtiśuddhatayā, samamaitry ākāśasamatayā, arhanmaitry arinirghātanatayā, bodhisatvamaitrī satvaparipākāsraṃsanatayā, tathāgatamaitrī tathatānubodhanatayā, buddhamaitrī suptasatvaprabodhanatayā, svayambhumaitrī svayamabhisaṃbodhanatayā bodhimaitri samarasatayā, asamāropamaitry anunayapratighaprahāṇatayā, mahākaruṇāmaitrī mahāyānaparidīpanatayā, aparikhedamaitrī śūnyanairātmyapratyavekṣaṇatayā, dharmadānamaitry anācāryamuṣṭitayā, śīlamaitrī duḥśīlasatvāvekṣaṇatayā, kṣāntimaitry ātmaparākṣaṇyanatayā, vīryamaitrī sarvasatvabhāravahanatayā, dhyānamaitry anāsvādanatayā, prajñāmaitrī kālasaṃprāpaṇatayā, upāyamaitrī sarvatramukhoddarśanatayā, akuhanamaitry āśayapariśuddhitayā, aśāṭhyamaitry āśayatayā, adhyāśayamaitrī niraṅgaṇatayā, amāyāmaitry akṛtrimatayā, saukhyamaitrī buddhasaukhyapratiṣṭhāpanatayā / iyaṃ mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvasya mahāmaitrī /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'When, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> thus reflects: "I should teach the <s>Dharma</s> to these beings for the thorough understanding of <s>dharmas</s>" — then there arises in him genuine loving-kindness that protects beings, being without an object; calming loving-kindness, because it does not produce; non-burning loving-kindness, because it is free from defilements; loving-kindness in accord with reality, because of the equality of the three times; non-conflicting loving-kindness, because it does not take a stand; non-dual loving-kindness, because it is not entangled with either the internal or the external; unshakeable loving-kindness, because of its ultimate finality;
