firm loving-kindness, because of its diamond-firm unbreakable resolve; pure loving-kindness, because of its original purity; equal loving-kindness, because of its equality with space; <s>arhat</s>-loving-kindness, because it destroys enemies [i.e. defilements]; <s>bodhisattva</s>-loving-kindness, because it never abandons the ripening of beings; <s>Tathāgata</s>-loving-kindness, because it awakens to <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); <s>Buddha</s>-loving-kindness, because it awakens sleeping beings; spontaneous loving-kindness, because of its self-awakening; <s>bodhi</s>-loving-kindness, because of its single taste; loving-kindness free from superimposition, because it abandons attraction and aversion; <s>mahākaruṇā</s>-loving-kindness, because it illuminates the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle); tireless loving-kindness, because it contemplates emptiness and selflessness; <s>Dharma</s>-gift loving-kindness, because it holds nothing back; <s>śīla</s>-loving-kindness, because it watches over beings of bad morality; <s>kṣānti</s>-loving-kindness, because it protects both self and others; <s>vīrya</s>-loving-kindness, because it bears the burden of all beings; <s>dhyāna</s>-loving-kindness, because it does not savor [meditative bliss]; <s>prajñā</s>-loving-kindness, because it arrives at the right time; <s>upāya</s>-loving-kindness, because it shows the entrance everywhere; non-deceptive loving-kindness, because of the purity of intention; non-hypocritical loving-kindness, because of the sincerity of intention; deeply resolved loving-kindness, because it is free from blemish; non-deceitful loving-kindness, because it is genuine; blissful loving-kindness, because it establishes beings in the bliss of a <s>Buddha</s>. This, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the great loving-kindness of a <s>bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 6.3 āha: katarā punar asya mahākaruṇā /
body.translated_text: Vkn 6.3 He asked: 'And what is his great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>)?'

body.text: āha: yat kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ sarvasatvebhya utsṛjati /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'He dedicates to all beings whatever roots of merit he has accumulated.'

body.text: āha: katarā punar asya mahāmuditā /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'And what is his great joy (<s>mahāmuditā</s>)?'

body.text: āha: yad datvāttamanā bhavati, na vipratisārī /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Having given, he is contented and does not regret.'

body.text: āha: katarā punar asya mahopekṣā /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'And what is his great equanimity (<s>mahopekṣā</s>)?'

body.text: āha: yobhayato 'rthatā /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'It is benefitting both [self and others].'

body.text: Vkn 6.4 āha: saṃsārabhayabhītena kiṃ pratipattavyam /
body.translated_text: Vkn 6.4 He asked: 'What should be practiced by one who is afraid of the terror of <s>saṃsāra</s>?'

body.text: āha: saṃsārabhayabhītena mañjuśriḥ bodhisatvena buddhamāhātmyaṃ pratipattavyam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'One who is afraid of the terror of <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should take refuge in the magnificence of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: āha: buddhamāhātmye sthātukāmena kutra sthātavyam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Where should one who wishes to stand in the magnificence of the <s>Buddha</s> stand?'

body.text: āha: buddhamāhātmye sthātukāmena sarvasatvasamatāyāṃ sthātavyam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'One who wishes to stand in the magnificence of the <s>Buddha</s> should stand in the equality of all beings.'

body.text: āha: sarvasatvasamatāyāṃ sthātukāmena kutra sthātavyam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Where should one who wishes to stand in the equality of all beings stand?'

body.text: āha: sarvasatvasamatāyāṃ sthātukāmena sarvasatvapramokṣāya sthātavyam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'One who wishes to stand in the equality of all beings should stand in the complete liberation of all beings.'

body.text: Vkn 6.5 āha: sarvasatvapramokṣaṃ kartukāmena kiṃ kartavyam /
body.translated_text: Vkn 6.5 He asked: 'What should be done by one who wishes to achieve the complete liberation of all beings?'

body.text: āha: sarvasatvapramokṣaṃ kartukāmena kleśapramokṣaḥ kartavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'One who wishes to achieve the complete liberation of all beings should accomplish the liberation from defilements.'

body.text: āha: kleśān utsraṣṭukāmena kathaṃ prayuktena bhavitavyam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'How should one who wishes to abandon defilements be engaged?'

body.text: āha: kleśān utsraṣṭukāmena yoniśaḥ prayuktena bhavitavyam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'One who wishes to abandon defilements should be engaged in right method (<s>yoniśas</s>).'

body.text: āha: kathaṃ prayuktaḥ punar yoniśaḥ prayukto bhavati /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'How is one who is engaged [said to be] rightly engaged?'

body.text: āha: anutpādānirodhaprayukto yoniśaḥ prayukto bhavati /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'One who is engaged in non-arising and non-ceasing is rightly engaged.'

body.text: āha: kiṃ notpādayati, kiṃ na nirodhayati /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'What does one not cause to arise? What does one not cause to cease?'

body.text: āha: akuśalaṃ notpādayati, kuśalaṃ na nirodhayati /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'One does not cause the unwholesome to arise, and one does not cause the wholesome to cease.'

body.text: āha: kuśalasyākuśalasya ca kiṃ mūlam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'What is the root of the wholesome and the unwholesome?'

body.text: āha: satkāyo mūlam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'The composite self (<s>satkāya</s>) is their root.'

body.text: āha: satkāyasya ca punaḥ kiṃ mūlam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'And what again is the root of the composite self?'

body.text: āha: satkāyasyecchālobhau mūlam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Desire and attachment are the root of the composite self.'

body.text: āha: icchālobhayoḥ kiṃ mūlam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'What is the root of desire and attachment?'

body.text: āha: icchālobhayor abhūtaparikalpo mūlam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is the root of desire and attachment.'

body.text: Vkn 6.6 āha: abhūtaparikalpasya kiṃ mūlam /
body.translated_text: Vkn 6.6 He asked: 'What is the root of unreal conceptualization?'

body.text: āha: abhūtaparikalpasya viparyastā saṃjñā mūlam /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'A distorted perception (<s>viparyastā saṃjñā</s>) is the root of unreal conceptualization.'

body.text: āha: viparyastāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ kiṃ mūlam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'What is the root of perverted perception?'

body.text: āha: viparyastāyāḥ saṃjñāyā apratiṣṭhā mūlam /
body.translated_text: He answered: 'The root of perverted perception is non-establishment (<s>apratiṣṭhā</s>).'

body.text: āha: apratiṣṭhāyāḥ kiṃ mūlam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'What is the root of non-establishment?'

body.text: āha: yan mañjuśrīḥ apratiṣṭhānaṃ tasya kiṃ mūlaṃ bhaviṣyati / iti hy apratiṣṭhānamūlapratiṣṭhitāḥ sarvadharmāḥ /
body.translated_text: He answered: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what root could that which is non-established have? Thus all <s>dharmas</s> are established on the root of non-establishment.'

body.text: Vkn 6.7 atha yā tatra gṛhe devatā prativasati, sā teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānām imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭodagrāttamanā, audārikam ātmabhāvaṃ saṃdarśya divyaiḥ puṣpais tān mahāsatvāṃs tāṃś ca mahāśrāvakān abhyavakirati sma / abhyavakīrṇānāṃ ca tatra yāni bodhisatvānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi patitāni, tāni dharaṇitale pratiṣṭhitāni / yāni punar mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi patitāni, tāni tatraiva sthitāni na bhūmau patitāni / tatas te mahāśrāvakā ṛddhiprātihāryaiḥ tāni puṣpāṇy utsṛjanti, na ca patanti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.7) Then the goddess (<s>devatā</s>) who dwelt in that house, having heard this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, was delighted, elated, and uplifted in mind. Displaying a magnificent form, she scattered divine flowers upon those <s>mahāsattvas</s> and those great <s>śrāvakas</s>. The flowers that fell upon the bodies of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> fell to the ground. But the flowers that fell upon the bodies of the great <s>śrāvakas</s> stuck to them and did not fall to the ground. Then those great <s>śrāvakas</s> attempted to shake off the flowers through supernatural displays, but the flowers did not fall.

body.text: Vkn 6.8 atha sā devatāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha: kiṃ bhadantaśāriputra, etāni puṣpāṇy utsṛjasi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.8) Then that goddess said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Why, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, do you try to shake off these flowers?'

body.text: āha: akalpikāni devate etāni puṣpāṇi / tasmād aham etāni puṣpāṇy apanayāmi /
body.translated_text: He said: 'These flowers are not proper for ascetics, goddess. That is why I am removing them.'

body.text: devatāha: mā bhadantaśāriputra evaṃ vocaḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / etāni hi puṣpāṇi kalpikāni / kiṃ kāraṇam / tathā hy etāni puṣpāṇi na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti / sthaviraḥ punaḥ śāriputraḥ kalpayati vikalpayati ca / ye bhadantaśāriputra svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāṃ kalpayanti vikalpayanti ca, te 'kalpikāḥ / sthaviras tu kalpayati vikalpayati ca / ye punar na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti, te kalpikāḥ / paśya bhadantaśāriputra eṣāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi na śliṣyanti / yathāpi nāma sarvakalpavikalpaprahīṇatvāt / tadyathāpi nāma bhīrukajātīyasya puruṣasyāmanuṣyā avatāraṃ Iabhante / evam eva saṃsārabhayabhītānāṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāny avatāraṃ labhante / ye punaḥ sarvasaṃsārakleśabhayavigatāḥ, kiṃ teṣāṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni kariṣyanti / yeṣāṃ vāsanāprahīṇā, teṣāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi śliṣyanti / tasmāt sarvavāsanāprahīṇānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi na śliṣyanti /
body.translated_text: The goddess said: 'Do not say that, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. For what reason? These flowers are indeed proper. Why? Because these flowers neither conceptualize (<s>kalpayanti</s>) nor discriminate (<s>vikalpayanti</s>). It is the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> who conceptualizes and discriminates. Those, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, who have gone forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-discipline and who conceptualize and discriminate — they are the improper ones. The elder conceptualizes and discriminates. But those who do not conceptualize or discriminate — they are the proper ones. See, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the flowers do not stick to the bodies of these <s>mahāsattvas</s> — precisely because they have abandoned all conceptualization and discrimination. Just as non-human beings gain entry over a person of timid nature, so too forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles gain entry over those who are afraid of the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>. But those who are free from the fear of all defilements of <s>saṃsāra</s> — what can forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles do to them? The flowers stick to the bodies of those whose latent dispositions (<s>vāsanā</s>) have not been abandoned. Therefore the flowers do not stick to the bodies of those whose latent dispositions have been completely abandoned.'

body.text: Vkn 6.9 atha khalv āyuṣmāñ śāriputras tāṃ devatām etad avocat: kiyacciraniviṣṭā punas tvaṃ devate iha gṛhe /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.9) Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to that goddess: 'How long have you been dwelling in this house, goddess?'

body.text: āha: yāvacciraniviṣṭā sthavirasyāryā vimuktiḥ /
body.translated_text: She said: 'As long as the noble liberation (<s>āryā vimukti</s>) of the elder has been established.'

body.text: āha: na cirasthitā tvaṃ devate iha gṛhe /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Have you been dwelling in this house for a long time, goddess?'

body.text: āha: kiyacciraniviṣṭā punaḥ sthavirasyāryā vimuktiḥ /
body.translated_text: She said: 'And how long has the noble liberation of the elder been established?'

body.text: tataḥ sthaviras tūṣṇīm abhūt /
body.translated_text: At that the elder fell silent.

body.text: āha: kim idānīṃ mahāprajñānām agryaḥ sthaviras tūṣṇīm abhūt / prāptakālaṃ praśnaṃ na visarjayati /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Why does the elder, foremost among those of great wisdom, now remain silent? He does not answer a question when the time has come.'

body.text: āha: apravyāhārā hi devate vimuktiḥ / tan na jāne kiṃ vyāharāmīti /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Liberation, goddess, is beyond expression. Therefore I do not know what to say.'

body.text: āha: yad yad eva sthaviro 'kṣaram udāharati, sarvāṇy etāny akṣarāṇi vimuktilakṣaṇāni / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / yā hi sā vimuktiḥ, sā nādhyātmaṃ na bahir nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate / evam akṣarāṇy api / tasmāt tarhi bhadantaśāriputra mā akṣarāpanayena vimuktiṃ nirdiśa / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / sarvadharmasamatā hi vimuktiḥ /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Whatever syllable the elder utters, all those syllables have the characteristic of liberation. For what reason? Liberation is not found internally, externally, or in between. Likewise syllables. Therefore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, do not indicate liberation through the removal of syllables. For what reason? The equality of all <s>dharmas</s> is liberation.'

body.text: āha: nanu devate rāgadoṣamohavigamād vimuktiḥ /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Is it not, goddess, that liberation comes from the removal of passion, hatred, and delusion?'

body.text: devatāha: abhimānikānām eṣa nirdeṣo rāgadoṣamohavigamād vimuktir iti / ye nirabhimānikāḥ, teṣāṃ rāgadoṣamohaprakṛtir eva vimuktiḥ /
body.translated_text: The goddess said: 'The statement that liberation is from the removal of passion, hatred, and delusion is for those with conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>). For those without conceit, the very nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of passion, hatred, and delusion is itself liberation.'

body.text: Vkn 6.10 atha khalv āyuṣmāñ śāriputras tāṃ devatām etad avocat: sādhu sādhu devate kiṃ tvayā prāptaṃ kiṃ vā sākṣātkṛtam, yasyās ta īdṛśaṃ pratibhānam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.10) Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to that goddess: 'Well done, well done, goddess! What have you attained? What have you realized, that you have such eloquence?'

body.text: āha: na mayā bhadantaśāriputra kiṃcit prāptaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ vā / tena ma īdṛśaṃ pratibhānam / yeṣām evaṃ bhavaty asmābhiḥ prāptaṃ vā sākṣātkṛtaṃ ceti, te svākhyāte dharmavinaya ābhimānikā ity ucyante /
body.translated_text: She said: 'I, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, have neither attained nor realized anything. Therefore I have such eloquence. Those who think "we have attained" or "we have realized" — they are said to be conceited in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-discipline.'

body.text: Vkn 6.11 āha: kiṃ tvaṃ devate śrāvakayānikā pratyekabuddhayānikā mahāyānikā vā /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.11) He asked: 'Are you, goddess, of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>, or the <s>Mahāyāna</s>?'

body.text: āha: śrāvakāyānikāsmi śrāvakayānasūcanatayā, pratyekabuddhayānikāsmi pratītyadharmāvatāreṇa, mahāyānikāsmi mahākaruṇānutsṛjanatayā /
body.translated_text: She said: 'I am of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> insofar as I indicate the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> to others; I am of the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> insofar as I enter the <s>dharma</s> of dependent origination; I am of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> insofar as I never abandon great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).'

body.text: Vkn 6.12 api tu khalu punar bhadantaśāriputra na campakavanaṃ praviṣṭā eraṇḍagandhaṃ jighranti / campakavanaṃ tu praviṣṭāś campakagandham eva jighranti / evam eva bhadantaśāriputra neha gṛhe buddhadharmaguṇagandhike vasantaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhagandhaiḥ jighranti / ye 'pi bhadantaśāriputra śakrabrahmalokapālā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā idaṃ gṛhaṃ praviśanti, te 'py asya satpuruṣasya dharmaśravaṇena buddhadharmaguṇagandhenotpāditabodhicittā niṣkrāmanti / dvādaśavarṣāṇy upādāya bhadantaśāriputra prativasantyā me na jātu śrāvakapratyekabuddhasaṃprayuktā kathā śrutapūrvā, nānyatra mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāpratisaṃyuktaivācintyadharmapratisaṃyuktaiva /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.12) 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those who enter a <s>campaka</s> grove do not smell the scent of castor bean (<s>eraṇḍa</s>) but smell only the <s>campaka</s> fragrance. Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those who dwell in this house, fragrant with the qualities of the <s>Buddhadharma</s>, do not smell the scents of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. And those <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s>, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> who enter this house — even they, upon hearing the <s>Dharma</s> from this virtuous man, leave with the mind of enlightenment aroused by the fragrance of the qualities of the <s>Buddhadharma</s>. For twelve years that I have dwelt here, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I have never heard any discourse connected with <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, but only that connected with the great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), the great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and the inconceivable <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 6.13 iha bhadantaśāriputra gṛhe 'ṣṭāv āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ satatasamitaṃ saṃdṛśyante / katame 'ṣṭau /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.13) 'In this house, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, eight wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharmas</s> are constantly seen. What are these eight?'

body.text: neha rātrir vā divaso vā prajñāyate sadāvabhāsitam idaṃ gṛhaṃ suvarṇavarṇayā prabhayā / neha sūryācandramasau prajñāyete, na bhrājete / ayaṃ prathama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Night and day are not perceived here; this house is always illuminated by a golden-colored radiance. Neither sun nor moon are perceived here, nor do they shine. This is the first wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra ye praviśantīdaṃ gṛham, teṣāṃ samanantarapraviṣṭānāṃ sarvakleśā na bādhante / ayaṃ dvitīya āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those who enter this house find that all their defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) do not afflict them immediately upon entry. This is the second wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra idaṃ gṛham avirahitaṃ śakrabrahmalokapālair anyabuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitaiś ca bodhisatvaiḥ / ayaṃ tṛtīya āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, this house is never without <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s>, and <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have assembled from other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. This is the third wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text:
punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra idaṃ gṛhaṃ satatasamitam avirahitaṃ dharmaśravaṇena ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktayā kathayāvivartyadharmakathayā ca / ayaṃ caturtha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe yās tūryasaṃgītayo divyamānuṣyakāṇi vā vādyāni vādyante, tebhyas tūryebhyo 'pramāṇo dharmaśabdanirhāro niścarati sārvakālikaḥ / ayaṃ pañcama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, this house is constantly and continuously never without the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, with discourse connected to the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>) and discourse on the irreversible <s>Dharma</s>. This is the fourth wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>. Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, divine and human music and songs are played, and from those instruments issues forth an immeasurable sound of the <s>Dharma</s>, constantly. This is the fifth wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe catvāri mahānidhānāni sarvaratnaparipūrṇāny akṣayāṇi yato niṣyandaṃ sarvadaridrakṛpaṇā ādāya prakrāmanti, na ca kṣīyante / ayaṃ ṣaṣṭha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house there are four great treasuries full of all jewels, inexhaustible, from which all the poor and wretched may take and depart, yet they are not depleted. This is the sixth wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe śākyamunis tathāgato 'mitābho 'kṣobhyo ratnaśrī ratnārcī ratnacandro ratnavyūho duḥprasahaḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ prabhūtaratnaḥ siṃhanādanādī siṃhaghoṣas tathāgata evaṃ pramukhā daśasu dikṣv apramāṇās tathāgatā ye 'sya satpuruṣasya cintitamātreṇāgacchanti / āgatya ca tathāgataguhyaṃ nāma dharmamukhapraveśaṃ deśayitvā prakrāmanti / ayaṃ saptama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Akṣobhya</s>, <s>Ratnaśrī</s>, <s>Ratnārcis</s>, <s>Ratnacandra</s>, <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, <s>Duḥprasaha</s>, <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Siṃhanādanāda</s>, <s>Siṃhaghoṣa</s> — headed by these, immeasurable <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions come by merely being thought of by this virtuous man. Having come and taught the <s>Dharma</s>-gateway called "The Secret of the <s>Tathāgata</s>" (<s>Tathāgataguhya</s>), they depart. This is the seventh wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe sarvadevabhavanavyūhāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāś ca saṃdṛśyante / ayam aṣṭama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in this house, all the palace-arrays of the gods and all the arrays of the qualities of the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> are seen. This is the eighth wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: ime bhadantaśāriputra aṣṭāv āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ satatasamitam iha gṛhe saṃdṛśyante / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / ka imām acintyadharmatāṃ paśyañ śrāvakadharmatāyai spṛhayet /
body.translated_text: 'These, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are the eight wonderful and extraordinary <s>dharmas</s> constantly seen in this house. For what reason? Who, seeing this inconceivable <s>dharma</s>-nature, would aspire to the nature of a <s>śrāvaka</s>?'

body.text: Vkn 6.14 āha: kiṃ tvaṃ devate strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.14) He said: 'Why do you not transform yourself from your female state, goddess?'

body.text: āha: paripūrṇāni me dvādaśavarṣāṇy upādāya strībhāvaṃ paryeṣamāṇāyā na cainaṃ labhe / api ca bhadantaśāriputra yā māyākāreṇa strīnirmitā yas tām evaṃ vadet: kiṃ tvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasīti, sa kiṃ vadet /
body.translated_text: She said: 'For fully twelve years I have been searching for the female state, and yet I have not found it. Moreover, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, if a woman were created by a magician and someone said to her: "Why do you not transform your female state?" — what would she say?'

body.text: āha: na tasyāḥ kācit bhūtā pariniṣpattiḥ /
body.translated_text: He said: 'She has no real fixed nature.'

body.text: āha: evam eva bhadantaśāriputra apariniṣpanneṣu sarvadharmeṣu māyānirmitasvabhāveṣu kutas tavaivaṃ bhavati: kiṃ tvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasīti /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, since all <s>dharmas</s> are without fixed nature and have the nature of magical creations, why do you think: "Why do you not transform your female state?"'

body.text: Vkn 6.15 atha sā devatā tādṛśam adhiṣṭhānam adhitiṣṭhati sma / yathā sthaviraḥ śāriputro yādṛśī sā devatā tādṛśaḥ saṃdṛśyate, sā devatā yādṛśaḥ sthaviras tādṛśī saṃdṛśyate / atha sā devatā śāriputrarūpā śāriputraṃ devatārūpadhāriṇam apṛcchat: kiṃ bhadantaśāriputra strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.15) Then that goddess exercised such a supernatural transformation that the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> appeared in the form of the goddess, and the goddess appeared in the form of the elder. Then the goddess, in the form of <s>Śāriputra</s>, asked <s>Śāriputra</s>, who bore the form of the goddess: 'Why do you not transform your female state, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>?'

body.text: śāriputro devatārūpy āha: na jāne kiṃ vinivartayāmīti / puruṣarūpam antarhitaṃ strīrūpaṃ me nirvṛttam /
body.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the form of the goddess, said: 'I do not know what to transform. My male form has disappeared, and a female form has arisen for me.'

body.text: āha: yadi sthaviraḥ śakṣyati strībhāvaṃ vinivartayitum, tataḥ sarvāḥ striyo 'pi strībhāvaṃ vinivartayiṣyanti / yathā sthaviro na strī strīva saṃdṛśyate, evaṃ sarvastrīṇām api strīrūpaṃ na ca striyaḥ strīrūpāś ca saṃdṛśyante / idaṃ saṃdhāya bhagavān āha: ḥsarvadharmā na strī na puruṣaḥ iti /
body.translated_text: She said: 'If the elder were able to transform the female state, then all women too would transform their female state. Just as the elder is not a woman yet appears as a woman, so too all women — their female form [is not their true form], and they are not women though they appear in female form. It is with this in mind that the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "All <s>dharmas</s> are neither female nor male."'

body.text: atha sā devatā tad adhiṣṭhānam avāsṛjat / athāyuṣmāñ śāriputraḥ punar eva svarūpasamanvāgato babhūva / atha sā devatāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha: kva nu te bhadantaśāriputra strīrūpaṃ kṛtaṃ gatam /
body.translated_text: Then that goddess released the supernatural transformation. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> was once again endowed with his own form. Then the goddess said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Where has your female form gone, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>?'

body.text: āha: na tat kṛtaṃ na vikṛtam /
body.translated_text: He said: 'It was neither made nor unmade.'

body.text: āha: evam eva sarvadharmā na kṛtā na vikṛtāḥ / yatra ca na kṛtir na vikṛtis tad buddhavacanam /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Just so, all <s>dharmas</s> are neither made nor unmade. That which is neither made nor unmade — that is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 6.16 āha: itas tvaṃ devate cyutā kutropapatsyase /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.16) He asked: 'When you decease from here, O goddess, where will you be reborn?'

body.text: āha: yatraiva tathāgatanirmita upapatsyate, tatraivāham upapatsye /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Wherever a <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanation would be reborn, there I too shall be reborn.'

body.text: āha: tathāgatanirmitasya na cyutir nopapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: He said: 'A <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanation has neither decease nor rebirth.'

body.text: āha: evam eva sarvadharmāṇāṃ na cyutir nopapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Just so, all <s>dharmas</s> have neither decease nor rebirth.'

body.text: āha: kiyaccireṇa punar devate bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'How long before you, O goddess, will attain awakening?'

body.text: āha: yadā sthaviraḥ pṛthagjanadharmasamanvāgato bhaviṣyati, tadāhaṃ bodhim abhisaṃbhotsye /
body.translated_text: She said: 'When the elder becomes endowed with the qualities of an ordinary person, then I shall attain awakening.'

body.text: āha: asthānam etad devate yad ahaṃ pṛthagjanadharmasamanvāgataḥ syām /
body.translated_text: He said: 'It is impossible, O goddess, that I should become endowed with the qualities of an ordinary person.'

body.text: āha: evam eva bhadantaśāriputra asthānam etad yad ahaṃ bodhim abhisaṃbhotsye / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / asthānasthitaiva hi bodhiḥ / tasmād asthānaṃ na kaścid abhisaṃbhotsyate /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is impossible that I should attain awakening. For what reason? Because <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is established in the impossible. Therefore, no one will attain awakening from the impossible.',

body.text: sthavira āha: uktaṃ devate tathāgatena ḥgaṅgānadīvālikāsamās tathāgatā abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante 'bhisaṃbhotsyante caḥ /
body.translated_text: The elder said: 'It has been said by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O goddess: "<s>Tathāgatas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river have attained, are attaining, and will attain awakening."'

body.text: devatāha: akṣaragaṇanāsaṃketādhivacanam etad bhadantaśāriputra atītānāgatapratyutpannā buddhā iti / na punar buddhā atītā vānāgatā vā vartamānā vā / tryadhvasamatikrāntā hi bodhiḥ / api ca prāptaṃ sthavireṇārhatvam /
body.translated_text: The goddess said: 'This is merely a conventional designation through the enumeration of syllables, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> — "past, future, and present <s>Buddhas</s>." But <s>Buddhas</s> are neither past, nor future, nor present. For <s>bodhi</s> transcends the three times. Moreover, has the elder attained <s>arhatship</s>?'

body.text: āha: prāptam asaṃprāptikāraṇena /
body.translated_text: He said: 'It is attained, through the absence of any attainment.'

body.text: āha: evam evābhisaṃbodhir anabhisaṃbodhikāraṇena /
body.translated_text: She said: 'Just so, awakening is [attained] through the absence of any awakening.'

body.text: Vkn 6.17 atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha: dvānavatibuddhakoṭīparyupāsitā bhadantaśāriputra eṣā devatābhijñājñānavikrīḍitā praṇidhānasamucchritā kṣāntipratilabdhāvaivartikasamavasaraṇā praṇidhānavaśena yathecchati tathā tiṣṭhati satvaparipākāya // //
body.translated_text: (Vkn 6.17) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'This goddess, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, has attended upon ninety-two <s>koṭis</s> (billions) of <s>Buddhas</s>. She sports with the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) and <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom). Her vows are fulfilled. She has attained <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and has reached the irreversible stage (<s>avaivartika</s>). By the power of her vow, she abides wherever she wishes for the ripening of beings.' //

body.text: devatāparivartaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, the <s>Devatāparivarta</s> (Chapter of the Goddess). //

body.text: Vkn 7.1 atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim evam āha: kathaṃ kulaputra bodhisatvo gatiṃgato bhavati buddhadharmeṣu /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 7.1) Then <s>Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta</s> said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'How, O son of good family, does a <s>bodhisattva</s> become one who has gone to the course of the <s>Buddhadharmas</s>?'

body.text: āha: yadā mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvo 'gatigamanaṃ gacchati, tadā bodhisatvo gatiṃgato bhavati buddhadharmeṣu /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'When, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> goes the going of the non-course (<s>agatigamana</s>), then the <s>bodhisattva</s> has gone to the course of the <s>Buddhadharmas</s>.'

body.text: āha: katamac ca bodhisatvasyāgatigamanam /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'And what is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s going of the non-course?'

body.text:
āha: yadā pañcānantaryagatiṃ ca gacchati, na ca vyāpādavihiṃsāpraduṣṭo bhavati / nirayagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvarajaḥkleśavigataś ca bhavati / tiryagyonigatiṃ ca gacchati, vigatatamo'ndhakāraś ca bhavati / asuragatiṃ ca gacchati, mānamadadarpavigataś ca bhavati / yamalokagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropāttaś ca bhavati / aneñjyarūpagatiṃ ca gacchati, na ca tadgatisamavasaraṇo bhavati / rāgagatiṃ ca gacchati, vigatarāgaś ca bhavati sarvakāmabhogeṣu / doṣagatiṃ ca gacchati, apratihataś ca bhavati sarvasatveṣu / mohagatiṃ ca gacchati, prajñānidhyapticittaś ca bhavati sarvadharmeṣu / mātsaryagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvādhyātmabāhyavastuparityāgī ca bhavati kāyajīvitānapekṣaḥ / duḥśīlagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvaśīlaśikṣādhutaguṇasaṃlekhapratiṣṭhitaś ca bhavaty anumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśī / vyāpādakhilakrodhagatiṃ ca gacchati, maitrīvihāri ca bhavaty atyantāvyāpannacittaḥ / kausīdyagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvakuśalamūlaparyeṣṭyabhiyuktaś ca bhavaty apratiprasrabdhavīryārambhaḥ / vibhrāntendriyagatiṃ ca gacchati, ariktadhyānaś ca bhavati prakṛtisamāpannaḥ / dauḥprajñagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvalokikalokottaraśāstrakuśalaś ca bhavati prajñāpāramitāgatiṃgataḥ / kuhanalapanacaryāgatiṃ gacchati, upāyakauśalacaryāniryātaś ca bhavati saṃdhābhāṣyakuśalaḥ / mānagatiṃ ca darśayati, setusaṃkrāmabhṛtaś ca bhavati sarvalokasya / kleśagatiṃ ca gacchati, prakṛtipariśuddhaś ca bhavaty atyantāsaṃkliṣṭaḥ / māragatiṃ ca gacchati, aparapratyayaś ca bhavati sarvabuddhadharmeṣu / śrāvakagatiṃ ca gacchati, aśrutadharmaśrāvayitā ca bhavati satvānām / pratyekabuddhagatiṃ ca gacchati, mahākaruṇāniryātaś ca bhavati satvaparipākāya / daridragatiṃ ca gacchati, ratnapāṇitāpratilabdhaś
ca bhavaty akṣayabhogaḥ / vikalendriyagatiṃ ca gacchati, lakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaś ca bhavaty abhirūpaḥ / hīnakulopapattigatiṃ ca gacchati, tathāgatakulagotrasaṃbhṛtaś ca bhavati puṇyajñānopacitasaṃbhāraḥ / durbaladurvarṇāvahoṭimakagatiṃ ca gacchati, nārāyaṇātmabhāvapratilabdhaś ca bhavati priyadarśanaḥ sarvasatvānām / jīrṇavyādhitoglānacaryāṃ ca darśayati, atyantavyādhisamudghātitaś ca bhavati maraṇabhayasamatikrāntaḥ / bhogagatiṃ ca darśayati, anityasaṃjñāpratyavekṣaṇābahulaś ca bhavati sarvaiṣaṇāpratiprasrabdhaḥ / antaḥpuranāṭakavyūhāś ca bodhisatvo darśayati, uttīrṇakāmapaṅkaś ca bhavaty aniketacārī / dhandhāyatanagatiṃ ca gacchati, vicitrapratibhānālaṃkāraś ca bhavati dhāraṇīpratilabdhaḥ / tīrthikagatiṃ ca gacchati, tīrthabhūtaś ca bhavati / sarvalokagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvagatinivṛttaś ca bhavati / nirvāṇagatiṃ ca gacchati, saṃsāraprabandhaṃ ca na jahāti / evaṃ mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvo 'gatigamanaṃ gacchati, gatiṃgataś ca bhavati sarvabuddhadharmeṣu /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'When he goes to the course of the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous deeds) yet is free from malice, injury, and corruption. When he goes to the course of the hells yet is free from all dust and defilement. When he goes to the course of animal births yet is free from the darkness of ignorance. When he goes to the course of the <s>asuras</s> (jealous gods) yet is free from pride, intoxication, and arrogance. When he goes to the course of <s>Yama</s>'s realm yet has accumulated all provisions of merit and knowledge. When he goes to the course of the immovable form-realm yet does not arrive at that destination. When he goes to the course of passion yet is free from passion in all sensual pleasures. When he goes to the course of hatred yet is unobstructed toward all beings. When he goes to the course of delusion yet his mind is established in discernment and investigation of all <s>dharmas</s> through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). When he goes to the course of miserliness yet gives away all inner and outer possessions without regard for body or life. When he goes to the course of immorality yet is established in all moral precepts, training rules, and ascetic qualities, fearful of even the slightest fault. When he goes to the course of malice, spite, and anger yet abides in loving-kindness, with an utterly benevolent mind. When he goes to the course of laziness yet is devoted to seeking all roots of merit with unrelaxed vigor. When he goes to the course of distracted faculties yet is undiminished in meditation, naturally established in <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment). When he goes to the course of poor wisdom yet is skilled in all mundane and supramundane treatises, having gone to the course of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). When he goes to the course of flattery, deceit, and hypocrisy yet has emerged in the practice of skillful means, skilled in intentional discourse. When he displays the course of pride yet serves as a bridge and crossing for all worldly beings. When he goes to the course of defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) yet is inherently pure, utterly undefiled. When he goes to the course of <s>Māra</s> yet does not depend on others for all <s>Buddhadharmas</s>. When he goes to the course of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) yet teaches beings <s>dharmas</s> unheard before. When he goes to the course of the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas) yet has emerged in great compassion for the ripening of beings. When he goes to the course of poverty yet has obtained a jewel-hand with inexhaustible wealth. When he goes to the course of defective faculties yet is adorned with the major marks and is handsome. When he goes to the course of birth in a low family yet is endowed with the lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s family, having accumulated provisions of merit and knowledge. When he goes to the course of the weak, ugly, and dwarfish yet has obtained the body of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, pleasing to behold by all beings. When he displays the conduct of the old, sick, and ailing yet has utterly eradicated illness and transcended the fear of death. When he displays the course of possessions yet his mind is abundant with the contemplation of impermanence, with all cravings relaxed. The <s>bodhisattva</s> displays the arrays of the inner palace and dancing — yet has crossed beyond the mire of sensual desire, wandering without a home. When he goes to the course of the dull and slow yet is adorned with varied eloquence and has obtained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (perfect retention). When he goes to the course of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) yet has become a true ford for all beings. When he goes to the course of all worlds yet has ceased all courses. When he goes to the course of <s>nirvāṇa</s> yet does not abandon the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> goes the going of the non-course and has gone to the course of all <s>Buddhadharmas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 7.2 atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam evam āha: kataman mañjuśrīḥ tathāgatānāṃ gotram /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 7.2) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta</s>: 'What, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>?'

body.text: āha: satkāyaḥ kulaputra tathāgatānāṃ gotram, avidyā bhavatṛṣṇā ca gotram, rāgadoṣamohā gotram, catvāro viparyāsā gotram, pañca nivaraṇāni gotram, ṣaḍ āyatanaṃ gotram, sapta vijñānasthitayo gotram, aṣṭau mithyātvāni gotram, navāghātavastūni gotram, daśākuśalāḥ karmapathā gotram / idaṃ kulaputra tathāgatānāṃ gotram / saṃkṣepeṇa kulaputra dvāṣaṣṭir dṛṣṭigatāni tathāgatānāṃ gotram /
body.translated_text: He said: 'The embodied self (<s>satkāya</s>), O son of good family, is the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) are the lineage. Passion, hatred, and delusion are the lineage. The four delusions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) are the lineage. The five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) are the lineage. The six sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) are the lineage. The seven stations of consciousness (<s>vijñānasthiti</s>) are the lineage. The eight wrong states (<s>mithyātva</s>) are the lineage. The nine grounds of ill-will (<s>āghātavastu</s>) are the lineage. The ten unwholesome courses of action (<s>akuśala karmapatha</s>) are the lineage. This, O son of good family, is the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. In brief, O son of good family, the sixty-two wrong views are the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 7.3 āha: kiṃ saṃdhāya mañjuśrīḥ evaṃ vadasi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 7.3) He asked: 'With what intention, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do you speak thus?'

body.text: āha: na śakyaṃ kulaputra asaṃskṛtadarśinā niyāmāvakrāntisthitenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayitum / kleśāgārasaṃskṛtasthitenādṛṣṭisatyena śakyam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayitum / tadyathā kulaputra nojjaṅgaleṣu pṛthivīpraveśeṣūtpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaugandhikāni virohanti / kardamapulinaprakṣiptāny utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaugandhikāni virohanti / evam eva kulaputra nāsaṃskṛtaniyāmaprāpteṣu satveṣu buddhadharmā virohanti / kleśapulinakardamaprāpteṣu satveṣu buddhadharmā virohanti / tadyathāpi nāma nākāśe bījāni virohanti / dharaṇitalapratiṣṭhitāni virohanti / evam eva nāsaṃskṛtaniyāmaprāpteṣu buddhadharmā virohanti / sumerusamāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭim utpādya bodhicittam utpadyate / tataś ca buddhadharmā virohanti / tad anenāpi te kulaputra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam / yathā sarvakleśās tathā tathāgatānāṃ gotram / tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra nānavatīrya mahāsamudraṃ śakyam anarghaṃ ratnam utkṣeptum / evam eva nānavatīrṇena kleśasāgaraṃ śakyaṃ sarvajñatācittaratnam utpādayitum /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'It is not possible, O son of good family, for one who sees the unconditioned and who stands in the fixed course of certainty to generate the mind of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). But one who stands in the house of defilements, in the conditioned, without having seen the truth — for such a one it is possible to generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening. Just as, O son of good family, blue lotuses, lotuses, night-lotuses, white lotuses, and fragrant lotuses do not grow on dry highland ground — but blue lotuses, lotuses, night-lotuses, white lotuses, and fragrant lotuses do grow when planted in the mud of a marshy bank. Just so, O son of good family, <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> do not grow in beings who have attained the fixed course of the unconditioned. <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> grow in beings who have entered the mud-bank of defilements. Just as seeds do not grow in the sky but grow when established on the ground — just so, <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> do not grow in those who have attained the fixed course of the unconditioned. It is by generating a view of the embodied self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> that the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) arises, and from that <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> grow. By this further teaching too, O son of good family, you should understand: just as all defilements are such, so is the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Just as, O son of good family, one cannot retrieve a priceless jewel without diving into the great ocean — just so, without diving into the ocean of defilements, one cannot generate the jewel of the mind of omniscience.'

body.text: Vkn 7.4 atha sthaviro mahākāśyapo mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya sādhukāram adāt: sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ subhāṣitā ta iyaṃ vāg bhūtam / etat kleśā gotraṃ tathāgatānām / kuto hy asmadvidhānāṃ śaktir asti bodhicittam idānīm utpādayitum / pañcānantaryaprāptaḥ śakto bodhicittam utpādayitum, śakto buddhadharmān abhisaṃboddhum, na punar aham /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 7.4) Then the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> applauded <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eternally youthful: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! Well-spoken is this word, and true! Indeed, the defilements are the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. How indeed could people like us have the power now to generate the mind of awakening? Even one who has committed the five heinous offenses (<s>pañcānantarya</s>) can generate the mind of awakening and can attain the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — but not I!'

body.text: Vkn 7.5 tadyathā vikalendriyasya puruṣasya pañcakāmaguṇā nirguṇā niḥsamarthāḥ / evam eva sarvasaṃyojanaprahīṇasya śrāvakasya sarvabuddhadharmā nirguṇā niḥsamarthāḥ / na tasya bhūyaḥ śaktir asti tān adhyālambitum* / tasmān mañjuśrīḥ pṛthagjanās tathāgatasya kṛtajñāḥ, na śrāvakāḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / pṛthagjanā hi buddhaguṇāñ śrutvā triratnavaṃśānupacchedāyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayanti / śrāvakāḥ punar yāvajjīvam api buddhadharmabalavaiśāradyāni śrutvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau na śaktāś cittam utpādayitum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 7.5) 'Just as a man with damaged faculties finds the five strands of sensual pleasure without quality and without power — just so, for a <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) who has abandoned all fetters, all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> are without quality and without power. He no longer has the power to engage with them. Therefore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, it is ordinary people (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who are grateful to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, not the <s>śrāvakas</s>. For what reason? Because ordinary people, upon hearing the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities, generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening for the unbroken continuity of the lineage of the Three Jewels. But <s>śrāvakas</s>, even if they hear throughout their lives about the powers and fearlessnesses of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, are unable to generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: Vkn 7.6 atha sarvarūpasaṃdarśano nāma bodhisatvas tasyām eva parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ / sa vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim evam āha: kasmin punas te gṛhapate mātāpitarau dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyam, kutra mitrajñātisālohitāḥ, kutra parivāro hayagajarathapativāhanaṃ vā / evam ukte vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ sarvarūpasaṃdarśanaṃ bodhisatvaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣat:
body.translated_text: (Vkn 7.6) Then a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Sarvarūpasaṃdarśana</s> (Revealer of All Forms), who had gathered and was seated in that very assembly, said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'Where, householder, are your parents, children, wife, male and female servants, workers, and attendants? Where are your friends, relatives, and kinsmen? Where is your retinue, your horses, elephants, chariots, and vehicles?' When this was said, the <s>Licchavi</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvarūpasaṃdarśana</s> in verses:

children.text: prajñāpāramitā mātā bodhisatvāna māriṣa /
children.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is the mother of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, O venerable one,

children.text: pitā copāyakauśalyaṃ yato jāyanti nāyakāḥ // (1)
children.translated_text: and <s>Upāyakauśalya</s> (Skillful Means) is the father — from these the guides [of beings] are born. (1)

children.text: bhāryā dharmaratis teṣāṃ maitri karuṇā ca duhitarau /
children.translated_text: Delight in the <s>Dharma</s> is their wife; <s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>Karuṇā</s> (compassion) are their daughters;

children.text: satyadharmāv ubhau putrau gṛhaṃ śūnyārthacintanā // (2)
children.translated_text: Truth and <s>Dharma</s> are both their sons; contemplation of the meaning of emptiness is their home. (2)

children.text: sarvakleśās tathā śiṣyā yatheṣṭavaśavartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: All the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>) are their disciples, subject to their will;

children.text: bodhyaṅgāś caiva mitrāṇi bodhiṃ budhyanti yair varām // (3)
children.translated_text: and the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) are their friends, through whom they awaken to the supreme <s>bodhi</s>. (3)

children.text: sahāyāś cānubaddhā hi ṣaḍ imāḥ pāramitāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: The six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are their constant companions, always in attendance;

children.text: stryāgāraḥ saṃgrahas teṣāra dharmāḥ saṃgītivāditam // (4)
children.translated_text: the [four] means of gathering beings (<s>saṃgraha</s>) are their harem; the <s>dharmas</s> are singing and music. (4)

children.text: udyānaṃ dhāraṇī teṣāṃ bodhyaṅgakusumaiś citam /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇī</s> (retentive power) is their garden, adorned with the flowers of the factors of awakening;

children.text: phalaṃ vimuktijñānaṃ ca vṛkṣā dharmadhanaṃ mahat // (5)
children.translated_text: liberation-knowledge is the fruit, and the great wealth of the <s>Dharma</s> constitutes the trees. (5)

children.text: vimokṣāḥ puṣkiriṇyaś ca samādhijālapūritāḥ /
children.translated_text: The liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) are their bathing pools, filled with the waters of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),

children.text: viśuddhipadmasaṃchannā yatra snāyanti nirmalāḥ // (6)
children.translated_text: covered with the lotuses of purity — where the stainless ones bathe. (6)

children.text: abhijñā vāhanaṃ teṣāṃ mahāyānam anuttamam /
children.translated_text: The <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) are their vehicles, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the supreme [vehicle];

children.text: sārathir bodhicittaṃ tu sanmārgo 'ṣṭāṅgikaḥ śivaḥ // (7)
children.translated_text: the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) is their charioteer, and the noble Eightfold Path is the auspicious road. (7)

children.text: bhūṣanā lakṣaṇāny eṣām aśītiś cānuvyañjanāḥ /
children.translated_text: The [thirty-two] marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) are their ornaments, and the eighty secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>);

children.text: hrīrapatrāpyavastrās te kalyāṇādhyāśayāḥ śubhāḥ // (8)
children.translated_text: modesty (<s>hrī</s>) and moral shame (<s>apatrāpya</s>) are their garments; and wholesome intentions are their auspicious adornments. (8)

children.text: saddharmadhanavantas te prayogo dharmadeśanā /
children.translated_text: They possess the wealth of the true <s>Dharma</s>; their profession is the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: pratipattir mahālābhaḥ pariṇāmaś ca bodhaye // (9)
children.translated_text: practice is their great gain; and the dedication is toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). (9)

children.text: śayanaṃ caturo dhyānāḥ śuddhājīvena saṃstṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: The four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) are their bed, spread with pure livelihood;

children.text: prajñā vibodhanaṃ teṣāṃ nityaṃ śrutasamāhitā // (10)
children.translated_text: <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) is their awakening, always accompanied by learning. (10)

children.text: amṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ teṣāṃ vimuktirasapānakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Amṛta</s> (the deathless) is their food; the flavors of liberation are their drink;

children.text: viśuddhāśayatā snānaṃ śīlaṃ gandhānulepanam // (11)
children.translated_text: purity of intention is their bath; and <s>śīla</s> (morality) is their perfume and ointment. (11)

children.text: kleśaśatruvinirghātāc chūrās te hy aparājitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Through vanquishing the enemy of defilements, they are heroes, unconquered;

children.text: dharṣenti caturo mārān bodhimaṇḍadhvajāśritāḥ // (12)
children.translated_text: they overpower the four <s>Māras</s>, taking refuge in the banner of the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). (12)

children.text: saṃcintyajāti darśenti ajātāś ca asaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: By deliberate intention they display birth, though unborn and non-arising;

children.text: dṛśyante sarvakṣetreṣu raśmirājavad udgatāḥ // (13)
children.translated_text: they are seen in all <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields), risen like the king of rays. (13)

children.text: buddhakoṭyo hi pūjitvā sarvapūjāhi nāyakān /
children.translated_text: Having worshipped tens of millions of <s>Buddhas</s>, the guides, with all offerings,

children.text: na caivātmani buddhe vā jātu kurvanti niśrayam // (14)
children.translated_text: they never take refuge in either self or <s>Buddha</s>. (14)

children.text: buddhakṣetrāṇi śodhenti satvānāṃ caritaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: They purify <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> according to the conduct of beings,

children.text: ākāśakṣetrānuprāptā na satve satvasaṃjñinaḥ // (15)
children.translated_text: having attained the field of space, they are without the perception of a being regarding beings. (15)

children.text: sarvasatvāna ye rūpā rutaghoṣāś ca īritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever forms of all beings and whatever sounds and utterances are expressed —

children.text: ekakṣanena darśenti bodhisatvā viśāradāḥ // (16)
children.translated_text: the confident <s>bodhisattvas</s> display them all in a single moment. (16)

children.text: mārakarma ca budhyante mārāṇāṃ cānuvartakāḥ /
children.translated_text: They know the workings of <s>Māra</s> and act in conformity with <s>Māras</s>;

children.text: upāyapāramiprāptāḥ sarvāṃ darśenti te kriyām // (17)
children.translated_text: having reached the perfection of <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), they display all activities. (17)

children.text: te jīrṇavyādhitā bhonti mṛtam ātmānu darśayī /
children.translated_text: They show themselves as old, sick, and even dying,

children.text: satvānāṃ paripākāya māyādharmavihāriṇaḥ // (18)
children.translated_text: for the ripening of beings, dwelling in the <s>dharma</s> of illusion. (18)

children.text: kalpoddāhaṃ ca darśenti uddahya tāṃ vasundharām /
children.translated_text: They display the <s>kalpa</s>-conflagration burning this earth,

children.text: nityasaṃjñīna satvānām anityam iti darśayī // (19)
children.translated_text: showing impermanence to beings who have the perception of permanence. (19)

children.text: satvakoṭīsahasrebhir ekarāṣṭre nimantritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Invited by tens of millions of beings in a single kingdom,

children.text: sarveṣāṃ gṛhi bhuñjanti sarvān nāmenti bodhaye // (20)
children.translated_text: they eat in the homes of all and lead all to awakening. (20)

children.text: ye kecin mantravidyā vā śilpasthānā bahūvidhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever mantras, sciences, or crafts of many kinds there may be,

children.text: sarvatra pāramiprāptāḥ sarvasatvasukhāvahāḥ // (21)
children.translated_text: in all of them they have reached perfection, bringing happiness to all beings. (21)

children.text: yāvanto loki pāṣaṇḍāḥ sarvatra pravrajanti te /
children.translated_text: However many religious orders there are in the world, they go forth into all of them,

children.text: nānādṛṣṭigataprāptān satvān hi parimocayi // (22)
children.translated_text: liberating beings who have arrived at various views. (22)

children.text: candrā bhavanti sūryā vā śakrabrahmaprajeśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: They become the moon, the sun, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and lords of creatures;

children.text: bhavanti āpas tejaś ca pṛthivī mārutas tathā // (23)
children.translated_text: they become water, fire, earth, and wind as well. (23)

children.text: roga-antarakalpeṣu bhaiṣajyaṃ bhonti uttamam /
children.translated_text: In intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of disease, they become the supreme medicine,

children.text: yehi satvā vimucyanti sukhī bhonti anāmayāḥ // (24)
children.translated_text: by which beings are liberated and become happy and free from illness. (24)

children.text: durbhikṣāntarakalpeṣu bhavanti pānabhojanam /
children.translated_text: In intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of famine, they become food and drink;

children.text: kṣudhāpipāsām apanetvān dharmaṃ deśenti prāṇinām // (25)
children.translated_text: having removed hunger and thirst, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to living beings. (25)

children.text: śastra-antarakalpeṣu maitryādhyāyī bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: In intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of weapons, they become those who meditate on <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness);

children.text: avyāpāde niyojenti satvakoṭīśatān bahūn // (26)
children.translated_text: they engage many hundreds of millions of beings in non-hostility. (26)

children.text: mahāsaṃgrāmamadhye ca samapakṣā bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: In the midst of great battles, they are impartial to both sides;

children.text: saṃdhisāmagri rocenti bodhisatvā mahābalāḥ // (27)
children.translated_text: the mighty <s>bodhisattvas</s> promote reconciliation and concord. (27)

children.text: ye cāpi nirayāḥ kecid buddhakṣetreṣv acintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever hells there may be in the inconceivable <s>Buddhakṣetras</s>,

children.text: saṃcintya tatra gacchanti satvānāṃ hitakāraṇāt // (28)
children.translated_text: they deliberately go there for the benefit of beings. (28)

children.text: yāvantyo gatayaḥ kāścit tiryagyonau prakāśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever destinies are known in the realms of animal birth,

children.text: sarvatra dharmaṃ deśenti tena ucyanti nāyakāḥ // (29)
children.translated_text: everywhere they teach the <s>Dharma</s> — therefore they are called guides. (29)

children.text: kāmabhogāṃ pi darśenti dhyānaṃ darśenti dhyāyinām /
children.translated_text: They display sensual pleasures to those [who need them], and display <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) to meditators;

children.text: vihastaṃ māraṃ kurvanti avatāraṃ na denti te // (30)
children.translated_text: they confound <s>Māra</s> and give him no opportunity. (30)

children.text: agnimadhye yathā padmam adbhutaṃ pi vidarśayet /
children.translated_text: Just as a lotus in the midst of fire would display a wonder,

children.text: evaṃ kāmāṃś ca dhyānaṃ ca adbhutaṃ te vidarśayi // (31)
children.translated_text: so they display the wonder of both sensual pleasures and <s>dhyāna</s>. (31)

children.text: saṃcintya gaṇikā bhonti puṃsām ākarṣaṇāya te /
children.translated_text: They deliberately become courtesans for the attraction of men;

children.text: rāgāṅkuśena lobhetvā buddhajñāne sthapenti te // (32)
children.translated_text: having drawn them with the hook of passion, they establish them in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. (32)

children.text: grāmikāś ca sadā bhonti sārthavāhāḥ purohitāḥ /
children.translated_text: They always become village headmen, caravan leaders, royal chaplains,

children.text: agrāmātyo 'tha cāmātyāḥ satvānāṃ hitakāraṇāt // (33)
children.translated_text: chief ministers and ministers — for the benefit of beings. (33)

children.text: daridrāṇāṃ ca satvānāṃ nidhānaṃ bhonti akṣayam /
children.translated_text: For poor beings, they become an inexhaustible treasury;

children.text: yeṣāṃ dānāni datvā hi bodhicittaṃ janenti te // (34)
children.translated_text: having given gifts to them, they generate the mind of awakening. // (34)

children.text: mānastabdheṣu satveṣu mahānagnā bhavanti te /
children.translated_text: Among beings stiffened by pride, they become great naked ascetics,

children.text: sarvamānasamudghātāṃ bodhiṃ prārthenti uttamām // (35)
children.translated_text: and aspire to supreme awakening that uproots all pride. // (35)

children.text: bhayārditānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃtiṣṭhante 'grataḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: They always stand in front of beings oppressed by fear,

children.text: abhayaṃ teṣu datvā ca paripācenti bodhaye // (36)
children.translated_text: and having given them fearlessness, they ripen them toward awakening. // (36)

children.text: pañcābhijñā hi bhūtvā te ṛṣayo brahmacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having become <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) with the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) and celibate,

children.text: śīle satvān niyojenti kṣāntisauratyasaṃyame // (37)
children.translated_text: they establish beings in morality, patience, gentleness, and self-restraint. // (37)

children.text: upasthānagurūn satvān saṃpaśyeha vināyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing beings devoted to service of teachers, those guides

children.text: ceṭā bhavanti dāsā vā śiṣyatvam upayānti ca // (38)
children.translated_text: become servants, slaves, or take on the role of disciples. // (38)

children.text: yena yenaiva cāṅgena satvā dharmaratā bhave /
children.translated_text: By whatever means beings might find delight in the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: darśenti hi kriyāḥ sarvā mahopāyasuśikṣitāḥ // (39)
children.translated_text: they demonstrate all kinds of activities, being well-trained in great <s>upāya</s> (skillful means). // (39)

children.text: teṣām anantaśikṣā hi anantaś cāpi gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Their training is infinite, and infinite too is their range;

children.text: anantajñānasaṃpannā anantaprāṇimocakāḥ // (40)
children.translated_text: endowed with infinite knowledge, they are liberators of infinite beings. // (40)

children.text: na teṣāṃ kalpakoṭībhiḥ kalpakoṭīśatais tathā /
children.translated_text: Not even by hundreds of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (eons),

children.text: bhāṣadbhiḥ sarvabuddhais tu guṇāntaḥ suvaco bhavet // (41)
children.translated_text: with all the <s>Buddhas</s> speaking, could the limit of their virtues be easily told. // (41)

children.text: bodhiṃ na prārthayet ko 'gryāṃ śrutvā dharmān imān budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who, being wise, having heard these teachings, would not aspire to supreme awakening,

children.text: anyatra hīnasatvebhyo yeṣāṃ prajñā na vidyate // (42)
children.translated_text: except for inferior beings in whom <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) does not exist? // (42)

body.text: iti // //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: tathāgatagotraparivartaḥ saptamaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the seventh chapter, called <s>Tathāgatagotrapari varta</s> (The Chapter on the Family of the Tathāgata). //

body.text: Vkn 8.1 atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tān bodhisatvān āmantrayate sma: pratibhātu satpuruṣāḥ katamo bodhisatvānām advayadharmamukhapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.1 Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> addressed those <s>bodhisattvas</s>: 'Good sirs, please explain: What is the <s>bodhisattvas</s>' entry into the <s>Dharma</s>-gate of non-duality (<s>advayadharmamukhapraveśa</s>)?'

body.text: tatra dharmavikurvaṇo nāma bodhisatvaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ / sa evam āha: utpādabhaṅgau kulaputra dvayam / yan na jātaṃ notpannaṃ na tasya kaścid bhaṅgaḥ / anutpādadharmakṣāntipratilambho 'dvayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thereupon the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dharmavikurvaṇa</s> (Transformation of the Dharma), who was present in the assembly, spoke thus: 'Arising and destruction, O son of good family, are a duality. What is unborn and unarisen — of that there is no destruction. The attainment of the <s>anutpādadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas) — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.2 śrīgupto bodhisatva āha: ahaṃ mameti dvayam etat / ātmāsamāropān mameti na bhavati / yaś cāsamāropo 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.2 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Śrīgupta</s> said: '"I" and "mine" — this is a duality. Because there is no superimposition of a self, there is no "mine." The absence of superimposition — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.3 śrīkūṭo bodhisatva āha: saṃkleśo vyavadānam iti dvayam etat / saṃkleśaparijñānād vyavadānamananā na bhavati / sarvamananāsamudghātā sārūpyagāminī pratipad ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.3 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Śrīkūṭa</s> said: 'Defilement and purification — this is a duality. Through the thorough understanding of defilement, there is no mental engagement with purification. The path that leads to the uprooting of all mental engagement and to conformity — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.4 sunakṣatro bodhisatva āha: iñjanā mananeti dvayam etat / yat punar nāñjate na manasikaroty anadhikāraḥ, adhikāravirahito 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.4 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sunakṣatra</s> said: 'Agitation and mental engagement — this is a duality. What is not agitated and not mentally engaged is without a basis; that which is devoid of a basis — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.5 subāhur bodhisatva āha: bodhicittaṃ śrāvakacittam iti dvayam etat / yā punar māyācittasamadarśanatā tatra na bodhicittaṃ na śrāvakacittam / yā cittasamalakṣaṇatāyam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.5 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Subāhu</s> said: 'The <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) and the <s>śrāvaka</s>-mind (hearer's mind) — this is a duality. But when one sees the mind as equal to an illusion, there is neither <s>bodhicitta</s> nor <s>śrāvaka</s>-mind. The single characteristic of the mind — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.6 animiṣo bodhisatva āha: upādānam anupādānam iti dvayam etat / yan nopādadāti tan nopalabhate, tatrohāpohaṃ na karoti / akaraṇam avyāpattiḥ sarvadharmāṇām ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.6 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Animiṣa</s> said: 'Grasping and non-grasping — this is a duality. What is not grasped is not obtained; in regard to that, one does not affirm or deny. Non-action, the non-failure of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.7 sunetro bodhisatva āha: ekalakṣaṇam alakṣaṇam iti dvayam etat / yat punar na lakṣayati na vikalpayati, naikalakṣaṇaṃ karoti nālakṣaṇam / yal lakṣaṇavilakṣaṇasamalakṣaṇapraveśo 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.7 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sunetra</s> said: 'Single characteristic and characteristiclessness — this is a duality. But when one neither characterizes nor discriminates, neither imposes a single characteristic nor characteristiclessness — the entry into the equality of characteristic and non-characteristic — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.8 puṣyo bodhisatva āha: kuśalam akuśalam iti dvayam etat / yā kuśalākuśalasyānupasthānatā tad animittam / animittakoṭyāś cādvayatā / yatra nistīraṇatāyam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.8 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Puṣya</s> said: 'Wholesome and unwholesome — this is a duality. The non-occurrence of both the wholesome and the unwholesome is signlessness. The non-duality of the limit of signlessness, wherein there is transcendence — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.9 siṃho bodhisatva āha: avadyatānavadyateti dvayam etat / yat punar vajranibaddhajñānatayā na badhyate na mucyate 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.9 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Siṃha</s> said: 'Blame and blamelessness — this is a duality. When, through diamond-firm knowledge, one is neither bound nor freed — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.10 siṃhamatir bodhisatva āha: idaṃ sāsravam idam anāsravam iti dvayam etat / yat punaḥ samatādharmaprāptaḥ sāsravānāsravasaṃjñaṃ na karoti, na vāsaṃjñāprāptaḥ, na cāsaṃjñāsamatāyāṃ samatāprāptaḥ, na saṃjñāgrathitaḥ / ya evaṃ praveśo 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.10 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Siṃhamati</s> said: '"This has defilements" and "this is free from defilements" — this is a duality. When one has attained the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, one does not create the notion of defiled and undefiled; nor does one attain the state of non-perception; nor does one attain equality in the equality of non-perception; nor is one entangled in perception. Such entry — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.11 sukhādhimukto bodhisatva āha: idaṃ sukham idam asukham iti dvayam etat / yat punaḥ sarvasaukhyāpagato gaganasamabuddhiḥ suviśuddhajñānatayā na sañjaty ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.11 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sukhādhimukta</s> said: '"This is pleasure" and "this is non-pleasure" — this is a duality. When one is free from all pleasure and has a mind equal to space, with perfectly purified knowledge, one does not attach — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.12 nārāyaṇo bodhisatva āha: idaṃ laukikam idaṃ lokottaram iti dvayam etat / yā laukikasya prakṛtiśūnyatā, na tatra kiṃcid uttīryate nāvatīryate na sāryate na visāryate / yatra nottaraṇaṃ nāvataraṇaṃ na saraṇaṃ na visaraṇam ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.12 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> said: '"This is worldly" and "this is supramundane" — this is a duality. The worldly is by nature empty; in it nothing transcends, nothing descends, nothing flows in, nothing flows out. Where there is no transcending, no descending, no flowing in, no flowing out — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.13 dāntamatir bodhisatva āha: saṃsāro nirvāṇam iti dvayam etat / saṃsārasvabhāvadarśanān na saṃsarati na parinirvāti / yaivaṃ budhyanāyam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.13 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Dāntamati</s> said: '<s>Saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is a duality. Through seeing the own-nature of <s>saṃsāra</s>, one neither transmigrates nor attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Such understanding — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.14 pratyakṣadarśī bodhisatva āha: kṣayo 'kṣaya iti dvayam etat / kṣayo 'tyantakṣīṇaḥ / yaś cātyantakṣīṇaḥ sa na kṣapayitavyaḥ / tenocyate 'kṣaya iti / yaś cākṣayaḥ sa kṣaṇikaḥ / kṣanikasya nāsti kṣayaḥ / evaṃ praviṣṭo 'dvayadharmamukhapraviṣṭo vaktavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.14 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Pratyakṣadarśin</s> said: 'Destruction and non-destruction — this is a duality. Destruction is ultimately destroyed. What is ultimately destroyed need not be destroyed further — therefore it is called "non-destruction." And what is non-destructible is momentary. What is momentary has no destruction. One who has thus entered is to be called one who has entered the <s>Dharma</s>-gate of non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.15 samantagupto bodhisatva āha: ātmā nirātmeti dvayam etat / yas tām ātmatāṃ nopalabhate, sa kiṃ nirātmīkariṣyati / ātmasvabhāvadarśī dvayaṃ na karoty ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.15 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantagupta</s> said: 'Self and non-self — this is a duality. When one does not apprehend that selfhood, what will one make selfless? One who sees the own-nature of the self does not create a duality — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.16 vidyuddevo bodhisatva āha: vidyāvidyeti dvayam etat / avidyāprakṛtikaiva vidyā / yā cāvidyā sāprakṛtikāgaṇanā gaṇanāpathasamatikrāntā / yo 'trābhisamayo 'dvayābhisamayo 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.16 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vidyuddeva</s> said: 'Knowledge and ignorance — this is a duality. The nature of ignorance is itself knowledge. And that ignorance is without nature, beyond enumeration, transcending the path of counting. Realization here is non-dual realization — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.17 priyadarśano bodhisatva āha: rūpaṃ śūnyam iti dvayam etat / rupam eva hi śūnyatā / na rūpavināśāc chūnyatā, rūpaprakṛtir eva śūnyatā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānaṃ śūnyam iti dvayam etat / vijñānam eva hi śūnyatā / na vijñānavināśāc chūnyatā, vijñānaprakṛtir eva śūnyatā / yo 'tra pañcasūpādānaskandheṣv evaṃ jñānānubodho 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.17 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Priyadarśana</s> said: '"Form is empty" — this is a duality. Form itself is emptiness. It is not that emptiness arises from the destruction of form; the very nature of form is emptiness. So too with feeling, perception, formations — "consciousness is empty" — this is a duality. Consciousness itself is emptiness. It is not that emptiness arises from the destruction of consciousness; the very nature of consciousness is emptiness. Knowledge and realization of this regarding the five aggregates of clinging — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.18 prabhāketur bodhisatva āha: anye catvāro dhātavo 'nya ākāśadhātur iti dvayam etat / ākāśasvabhāvā eva catvāro dhātavaḥ / pūrvāntata ākāśasvabhāvā aparāntata ākāśasvabhāvās tathā pratyutpannato 'py ākāśasvabhāvāḥ / yac caivaṃ dhātupraveśajñānam ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.18 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Prabhāketu</s> said: '"The four elements are one thing and the space element is another" — this is a duality. The four elements are by nature space. Their prior limit is by nature space; their posterior limit is by nature space; likewise their present [nature] is also by nature space. Knowledge of the entry into the elements in this way — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.19 sumatir bodhisatva āha: cakṣū rūpaṃ ca dvayam etat / yat punaś cakṣuḥparijñātāvī rūpeṣu na rajyati na duṣyati na muhyati, sa ucyate śānta iti / śrotraṃ śabdāś ca ghrāṇaṃ gandhāś ca jihvā rasāś ca kāyaḥ spraṣṭavyāni ca mano dharmāś ca dvayam etat / yat punar manaḥparijñātāvī dharmeṣu na rajyate na duṣyati na muhyati, sa ucyate śānta iti / evaṃ śāntasthitasyādvayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.19 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sumati</s> said: 'The eye and forms — this is a duality. When one has fully understood the eye and does not become passionate, hostile, or deluded regarding forms — that one is called "peaceful." The ear and sounds, the nose and smells, the tongue and tastes, the body and tangible objects, the mind and <s>dharmas</s> — this is a duality. When one has fully understood the mind and does not become passionate, hostile, or deluded regarding <s>dharmas</s> — that one is called "peaceful." The entry into non-duality for one thus established in peace.'

body.text: Vkn 8.20 akṣayamatir bodhisatva āha: dānaṃ sarvajñatāyāṃ pariṇāmayatīti dvayam etat / dānasvabhāvaiva sarvajñatā, sarvajñatāsvabhāva eva pariṇāmaḥ / evaṃ śīlaṃ kṣāntiṃ vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñāṃ sarvajñatāyāṃ pariṇāmayatīti dvayam etat / prajñāsvabhāvaiva sarvajñatā, sarvajñatāsvabhāva eva pariṇāmaḥ / yo 'traikanayapraveśo 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.20 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> said: '"One dedicates generosity to omniscience" — this is a duality. The own-nature of generosity is itself omniscience; the own-nature of omniscience is itself dedication. So too: "One dedicates morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom to omniscience" — this is a duality. The own-nature of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is itself omniscience; the own-nature of omniscience is itself dedication. Entry into the single principle here — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.21 gambhīrabuddhir bodhisatva āha: anyā śūnyatānyad animittam anyad apraṇihitam iti dvayam etat / yad dhi śūnyaṃ tatra na kiṃcin nimittam / animitte 'praṇihitam / apraṇihite na cittaṃ na mano na manovijñānaṃ pracarati / yatraikaṃ vimokṣamukhaṃ tatra sarvāṇi vimokṣamukhāni draṣṭavyāny ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.21 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gambhīrabuddhi</s> said: '"Emptiness is one thing, signlessness another, and wishlessness another" — this is a duality. What is empty — in it there is no sign. Where there is no sign, there is no wish. Where there is no wish, neither mind, nor <s>manas</s>, nor <s>manovijñāna</s> operates. Where there is a single gate of liberation, there all gates of liberation are to be seen — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.22 śāntendriyo bodhisatva āha: buddho dharmaḥ saṃgha iti dvayam etat / buddhasya hi dharmaḥ, dharmaprakṛtikaś ca saṃghaḥ / sarvāṇy etāni ratnāny asaṃskṛtāni, asaṃskṛtaṃ cākāśam, ākāśasamaś ca sarvadharmanayaḥ / ya evam anugamo 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Vkn 8.22 The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Śāntendriya</s> said: '<s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṃgha</s> — this is a duality. For the <s>Buddha</s> is the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> is of the nature of <s>Dharma</s>. All these jewels are unconditioned, and the unconditioned is space, and the principle of all <s>dharmas</s> is equal to space. Such understanding — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.23 apratihatacakṣur bodhisatva āha: satkāyaḥ satkāyanirodha iti dvayam etat / satkāya eva hi nirodhaḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / tathā hi sa satkāya iti dṛṣṭiṃ nopasthāpayati, yayā dṛṣṭyā satkāya iti vā satkāyanirodha iti vā kalpayati / so 'kalpo 'vikalpo 'tyantāvikalpo nirodhasvabhāvaprāptaḥ, na saṃbhavati na vibhavaty ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Apratihatacakṣus</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: '<s>Satkāya</s> (the existing body) and <s>satkāyanirodha</s> (the cessation of the existing body)' — this is a duality. The existing body itself is cessation. For what reason? Because one who sees thus does not give rise to the view by which one would conceive 'existing body' or 'cessation of the existing body.' That which is unconceived, undiscriminated, and utterly beyond discrimination has attained the nature of cessation; it neither arises nor perishes — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.24 suvinīto bodhisatva āha: kāyavāṅmanaḥsaṃvara iti dvayam etat / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / anabhisaṃskāralakṣanā hy ete dharmāḥ / yā kāyasyānabhisaṃskāratā tallakṣaṇaiva vāganabhisaṃskāratā tallakṣaṇaiva mano'nabhisaṃskāratā / yā ca sarvadharmāṇām anabhisaṃskāratā, sā jñātavyānugantavyā / yad atrānabhisaṃskārajñānam ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Suvinīta</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Restraint of body, speech, and mind' — this is a duality. For what reason? Because these <s>dharmas</s> are characterized by non-formation. The non-formation of the body has the same characteristic as the non-formation of speech, which has the same characteristic as the non-formation of mind. The non-formation of all <s>dharmas</s> is what should be known and followed. The knowledge of non-formation herein — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.25 puṇyakṣetro bodhisatva āha: puṇyapuṇyāniñjyān saṃskāran abhisaṃskarotīti dvayam etat / yat punaḥ puṇyāpuṇyāniñjyānabhisaṃskāratā sādvayā / yā ca puṇyāpuṇyāniñjyānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā na tatra puṇyāpuṇyāniñjyāḥ saṃskārāḥ / yaivam anumārjanāyam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Puṇyakṣetra</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'One forms meritorious, demeritorious, and immovable formations' — this is a duality. But the non-formation of meritorious, demeritorious, and immovable formations is also non-dual. The intrinsic-characteristic-emptiness of meritorious, demeritorious, and immovable formations means that therein there are no meritorious, demeritorious, or immovable formations. One who thus purifies — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.26 padmavyūho bodhisatva āha: ātmasamutthānasamutthitaṃ dvayam / ātmaparijñātāvī dvayaṃ notthāpayati / advayasthitasya vijñāptir nāsti / avijñaptikaś cādvayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Padmavyūha</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: Duality arises from the arising of self. One who has fully understood the self does not give rise to duality. For one established in non-duality, there is no conceptual designation. And the absence of conceptual designation is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.27 śrīgarbho bodhisatva āha: upalambhaprabhāvitaṃ dvayam / yan na labhate tan nopalabhate, tan nāyūhati na niryūhati / tatra nāyūho na niryūho 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Śrīgarbha</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: Duality is produced by apprehension. What one does not obtain, one does not apprehend; what one does not apprehend, one neither constructs nor deconstructs. Therein there is neither construction nor deconstruction — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.28 candrottaro bodhisatva āha: tamaḥ prakāśa iti dvayam etat / atamo 'prakāśa ity advayam / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / tathā hi nirodhasamāpannasya na tamo na prakāśaḥ / evaṃlakṣaṇāś ca sarvadharmāḥ / yo 'tra samatāpraveśo 'yam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Candrottara</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Darkness and light' — this is a duality. Neither darkness nor light is non-duality. For what reason? Because for one who has entered the <s>nirodhasamāpatti</s> (cessation attainment), there is neither darkness nor light. And all <s>dharmas</s> have this same characteristic. The entry into equality herein — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.29 ratnamudrāhasto bodhisatva āha: nirvāṇe 'bhiratiḥ saṃsāre 'nabhiratir iti dvayam etat / yasya na nirvāṇe 'bhiratir na saṃsāre 'nabhiratir idam advayam / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / baddhasya hi sato mokṣaḥ prabhāvyate / yo 'tyantam evābaddhaḥ sa kiṃ mokṣaṃ paryeṣiṣyate / abaddho 'mukto bhikṣur na ratim utpādayati nāratim ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnamudrāhasta</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Delight in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and non-delight in <s>Saṃsāra</s>' — this is a duality. One who has neither delight in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> nor non-delight in <s>Saṃsāra</s> — this is non-duality. For what reason? Because liberation is spoken of only for one who is bound. One who is utterly unbound — what liberation would he seek? A <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who is neither bound nor liberated produces neither delight nor non-delight — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.30 maṇikūṭarājo bodhisatva āha: mārgaḥ kumārga iti dvayam etat / mārgapratipannasya na kumārgaḥ samudācarati / asamudācārasthitasya na mārgasaṃjñā bhavati na kumārgasaṃjñā / saṃjñāparijñātāvino hi dvaye buddhir nākrāmaty ayam asyādvayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Maṇikūṭarāja</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'The right path and the wrong path' — this is a duality. For one who has entered the right path, the wrong path does not arise. For one established in non-arising, there is neither the notion of the right path nor the notion of the wrong path.
