For one who has fully understood notions, the mind does not proceed to either of the two — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.31 satyanandī bodhisatva āha: satyaṃ mṛṣeti dvayam etat / satyadarśī satyam eva na samanupaśyati, kuto mṛṣā drakṣyati / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na hi sa māṃsacakṣuṣā paśyati, prajñācakṣuṣā paśyati / tathā ca paśyati, na vipaśyati / yatra ca na paśyanā na vipaśyanāyam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Satyānandī</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Truth and falsehood' — this is a duality. One who sees truth does not even perceive truth — how then would he see falsehood? For what reason? Because he does not see with the fleshly eye; he sees with the eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). And seeing thus, he neither sees nor fails to see. Where there is neither seeing nor failing to see — this is the entry into non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 8.32 ity evaṃ te bodhisatvāḥ svakasvakān nirdeśān nirdiśya mañjuśriyam kumārabhūtam etad avocat: katamo mañjuśriḥ bodhisatvasyādvayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having each given their own expositions, said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the prince: 'What, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is a <s>Bodhisattva's</s> entry into non-duality?'

body.text: mañjuśrīr āha: subhāṣitaṃ yuṣmākaṃ satpuruṣāḥ sarveṣām / api tu yāvad yuṣmābhir nirdiṣṭaṃ sarvam etad dvayam / ekanirdeśaṃ sthāpayitvā yaḥ sarvadharmāṇām anudāhāro 'pravyāhāro 'nudīranākīrtanānabhilapanam aprajñapanam ayam advayapraveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Well spoken, good sirs, by all of you! Yet all that you have expounded still constitutes duality. Setting aside a single exposition — that which is the non-utterance, non-speaking, non-indicating, non-announcing, non-expressing, and non-designating of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the entry into non-duality.'

body.text: Vkn 8.33 atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat: nirdiṣṭo 'smābhiḥ kulaputra svakasvako nirdeśaḥ / pratibhātu tavāpy advayadharmapraveśanirdeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the prince said this to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'We have each given our own exposition, son of good family. May you too please set forth your teaching on the entry into the <s>Dharma</s> of non-duality.'

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tūṣṇīm abhūt /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> remained silent.

body.text: atha mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrter licchaveḥ sādhukāram adāt: sādhu sādhu kulaputra ayaṃ bodhisatvānām advayadharmamukhapraveśo yatra nākṣararutaravitavijñaptipracāraḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the prince applauded <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, son of good family! This is the <s>Bodhisattvas'</s> entry into the gate of the <s>Dharma</s> of non-duality, where there is no movement of syllables, sounds, voices, or conceptual designations.'

body.text: iha nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne pañcānāṃ bodhisatvasahasrāṇām advayadharmamukhapraveśād anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt // //
body.translated_text: When this exposition was being set forth, five thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (the patient acceptance of the non-arising of all dharmas) through the entry into the gate of the <s>Dharma</s> of non-duality.

body.text: advayadharmamukhapraveśaparivarto 'ṣṭamaḥ //
body.translated_text: This concludes the eighth chapter, the chapter on entry into the gate of the <s>Dharma</s> of non-duality.

body.text: Vkn 9.1 athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhūt: kālaḥ paryantībhūtaḥ / ime ca mahāsatvā nottiṣṭhanti / kutraite paribhokṣyante /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thought: 'The mealtime is approaching its end. These great beings are not rising. Where will they eat?'

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetasā cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha: ye te bhadantaśāriputra tathāgatenāṣṭau vimokṣā ākhyātās tair vimokṣair vihara / tvaṃ mā āmiṣamrakṣitayā saṃtatyā dharmaṃ śrauṣīḥ / api tu khalu punar bhadantaśāriputra muhūrtam āgamayasva, yāvad anāsvāditapūrvabhojanaṃ bhokṣyase /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, having discerned with his mind the mental deliberation of the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has taught the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) — abide in those liberations! Do not listen to the <s>Dharma</s> with a mind preoccupied with material food! Moreover, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, wait but a moment, and you shall eat food the likes of which you have never tasted before.'

body.text: Vkn 9.2 atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samādhisamāpannaḥ tādṛśaṃ carddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskṛtavān / yad ūrdhve digbhāga ito buddhakṣetrād dvācatvāriṃśad gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya sarvagandhasugandhaṃ nāma lokadhātuṃ teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ teṣāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇām upadarśayati / tatra gandhottamakūṭo nāma tathāgata etarhi tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati / tatra ca lokadhātau yādṛśā daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu divyā mānuṣyakāś ca gandhā vānti / te tatra lokadhātau vṛkṣebhyo viśiṣṭatamā gandhā vānti / tatra lokadhātau nāsti śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nāmadheyam api / śuddhānām eva bodhisatvānāṃ saṃnipātaḥ / sa tebhyo gandhottamakūṭas tathāgato dharmaṃ deśayati / tatra ca lokadhātau sarvagandhamayāḥ kūṭāgārāḥ, sarvagandhamayāś caṅkramā udyānavimānāni / yaṃ ca te bodhisatvā āhāram āharanti tasya bhojanasya yo gandhaḥ so 'pramāṇāl lokadhātūn spharati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, at that moment, entered into such a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and performed such a feat of supernatural power that he revealed to those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and those great <s>Śrāvakas</s> a world-realm called <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> (Fragrant with All Fragrances), located in the upper direction, beyond forty-two <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-grain numbers of <s>Buddha-fields</s> from this <s>Buddha-field</s>. There the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s> (Peak of Supreme Fragrance) presently lives, endures, and sustains. In that world-realm, the divine and human fragrances that blow in all <s>Buddha-fields</s> throughout the ten directions — the fragrances that blow from the trees there are the most excellent of all. In that world-realm, there is not even the name of <s>Śrāvakas</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; there is only an assembly of pure <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to them. In that world-realm, all mansions are made of fragrance, all walkways, gardens, and palaces are made of fragrance. And the fragrance of the food that those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> eat pervades immeasurable world-realms.

body.text: tasmiṃś ca samaye bhagavān gandhottamakūṭas tathāgato bhaktāya niṣaṇṇo 'bhut sārdhaṃ tair bodhisatvaiḥ / tatra gandhavyuhāhārā nāma devaputrā mahāyānasaṃprasthitās tasya bhagavatas teṣāṃ bodhisatvānām upasthānaparicaryāyā udyuktāḥ / tatra sā sarvā parṣat taṃ lokadhātuṃ paśyati taṃ ca bhagavantaṃ tāṃś ca bodhisatvān bhaktāgraniṣaṇnān /
body.translated_text: At that time, the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>, was seated for the meal together with those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. There, <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) called <s>Gandhavyūhāhāra</s>, who had set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), were engaged in attending upon and serving that Blessed One and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. That entire assembly there beheld this world-realm and that Blessed One and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> seated at the foremost meal.

body.text: Vkn 9.3 atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tān sarvān bodhisatvān āmantrayate sma: ko yuṣmākaṃ satpuruṣāḥ utsahate 'to buddhakṣetrād bhojanam ānetum / tatra mañjuśriyo 'dhiṣṭhānena na kaścid utsahate /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> addressed all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Which of you, good sirs, is able to bring food from that <s>Buddha-field</s>?' But through the power of <s>Mañjuśrī's</s> supernatural influence, none of them was able.

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam evam āha: na tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ paryapatrapasa īdṛśyā parṣadā /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the prince: 'Are you not ashamed, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, before such an assembly as this?'

body.text: āha: nanūktaṃ kulaputra tathāgatenāśikṣito na paribhavitavya iti /
body.translated_text: He replied: 'Has not the <s>Tathāgata</s> said, son of good family, that one who has not completed training should not be treated with contempt?'

body.text: Vkn 9.4 atha vimalakīrtir licchavir anuttiṣṭhann etataḥ śayanāt puratas teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ nirmitaṃ bodhisatvaṃ nirmimīte sma / suvarṇavarṇena kāyena lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasamalaṃkṛtena tasya tādṛśo rūpāvabhāso 'bhūd yena sā sarvā parṣad dhyāmīkṛtā bhavet /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, without rising from his couch, before those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, created a magically-produced <s>Bodhisattva</s> through his supernatural emanation — with a body of golden color, adorned with the major marks and minor signs, whose radiance of form was such that it outshone that entire assembly.

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ nirmitaṃ bodhisatvam evam āha: gaccha kulaputra ūrdhaṃdigbhāge dvācatvāriṃśad gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya sarvagandhasugandho nāma lokadhātuḥ / tatra gandhottamakūṭo nāma tathāgataḥ, sa etarhi bhaktāya niṣaṇṇaḥ / tatra gatvā madvacanāt tasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvaivaṃ vada ḥ vimalakīrtir licchavir bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'lpābādhatāṃ ca paripṛcchaty alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghutthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca / evaṃ ca vadati ḥ dehi me bhagavan bhuktāvaśeṣaṃ yat sahe lokadhātau buddhakṛtyaṃ kariṣyati / eṣāṃ ca hīnādhimuktikanāṃ satvānam udārāṃ matiṃ rocayiṣyati / tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ vaistārikaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s>: 'Go, O son of good family, upward through forty-two <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. There is a world-system called <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> (Fragrance of All Fragrances). In it there is a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s> (Supreme Fragrance Peak), who is presently seated at his meal. Go there and, bowing your head at his feet on my behalf, speak thus: "<s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, bowing his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, inquires after the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, easy rising, well-being, strength, happiness, blamelessness, and comfortable abiding." And speak thus: "Please give me, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the remainder of the food, which will accomplish the <s>Buddha</s>'s work in the <s>Sahā</s> (Endurance) world-system. It will inspire lofty aspiration in those beings of inferior inclination. And the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> will be spread far and wide."'

body.text: Vkn 9.5 atha sa nirmito bodhisatvo vimalakīrter licchaveḥ sādhv iti pratiśrutya teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ purata ūrdhamukhaḥ saṃdṛśyate / na cainaṃ te bodhisatvāḥ paśyanti gacchantam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.5) Then that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s>, having assented to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> with 'Very well,' was seen rising upward in the presence of those <s>bodhisattvas</s>. But they did not see him going.

body.text: atha sa nirmito bodhisatvas taṃ sarvagandhasugandhaṃ lokadhātum anuprāptaḥ / sa tatra bhagavato gandhottamakūṭasya tathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvaivam āha: vimalakīrtir bhagavan bodhisatvo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandate / alpābādhatāṃ ca paripṛcchaty alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Then that emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> arrived at the <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> world-system. There he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>, and said: '<s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, bows his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and inquires after the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, easy rising, well-being, strength, happiness, blamelessness, and comfortable abiding.'

body.text: sa ca bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaivam āha: dehi me bhagavan bhuktāvaśeṣaṃ bhojanaṃ yad idaṃ sahe lokadhātau buddhakṛtyaṃ kariṣyati / teṣāṃ hīnādhimuktānāṃ satvānām udāreṣu buddhadharmeṣu matiṃ rocayiṣyati / bhagavataś ca nāmadheyaṃ vaistārikaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Having bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he said: 'Please give me, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the remainder of the food, which will accomplish the <s>Buddha</s>'s work in the <s>Sahā</s> world-system. It will inspire lofty aspiration in those beings of inferior inclination toward the supreme <s>Buddhadharmas</s>. And the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s name will be spread far and wide.'

body.text: Vkn 9.6 atha khalu ye tasya bhagavato gandhottamakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetre bodhisatvās te vismitās taṃ bhagavantaṃ gandhottamakūṭaṃ tathāgatam evam āhuḥ: kuto 'yaṃ bhagavan īdṛśo mahāsatva āgacchati, kva vā sa saho lokadhātuḥ, kaiṣā hīnādhimuktikatā nāma / evaṃ te bodhisatvās taṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchanti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.6) Then the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in that <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>, were amazed and asked that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>: 'From where, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, has this great being come? Where is that <s>Sahā</s> world-system? And what is this so-called "inferior inclination"?' Thus did those <s>bodhisattvas</s> question that <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: atha sa bhagavāṃs tān bodhisatvān evam āha: asti kulaputrāḥ adhodigbhāga ito buddhakṣetrād dvācatvāriṃśad gaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya saho lokadhātuḥ / tatra śākyamunir nāma tathāgato dharmaṃ deśayati hīnādhimuktikānāṃ satvānāṃ pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre / tatra vimalakīrtir nāma bodhisatvo 'cintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati / tenaiṣa nirmito bodhisatvo 'nupreṣito mama nāmadheyaparikīrtanāyāsya ca lokadhātor varṇasaṃprakāśanāya teṣāṃ ca bodhisatvānāṃ kuśalamūlottānatāyai /
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Bhagavān</s> said to those <s>bodhisattvas</s>: 'There is, O sons of good family, below this <s>Buddhakṣetra</s>, passing through forty-two <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a world-system called <s>Sahā</s> (Endurance). There the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings of inferior inclination in a <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> beset by the five corruptions. There a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Vimalakīrti</s>, established in the <s>acintyavimokṣa</s> (inconceivable liberation), teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. He has sent this emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> for the glorification of my name, for the praise of that world-system, and for the increase of the roots of merit of those <s>bodhisattvas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 9.7 atha te bodhisatvā evam āhuḥ: kiyan mahātmā sa bhagavan bodhisatvo yasyāyaṃ nirmita evam ṛddhibalavaiśāradyaprāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.7) Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said: 'How great is that <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, whose emanation has attained such supernatural power, strength, and fearlessness?'

body.text: sa bhagavān āha: tathā mahātmā sa bodhisatvo yat sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu nirmitān preṣayati / te ca nirmitā buddhakṛtyena satvānāṃ pratyupasthitā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: That <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So great is that <s>bodhisattva</s> that he sends emanations to all <s>Buddhakṣetras</s>. And those emanations serve beings with the <s>Buddha</s>'s work.'

body.text: Vkn 9.8 atha sa bhagavān gandhottamakūṭas tathāgataḥ sarvagandhasamīhite bhājane taṃ sarvagandhaparivāsitaṃ bhojanaṃ tasmai bodhisatvāya prādāt / tatra navatir bodhisatvasahasrāṇi saṃprasthitāni: gamiṣyāmo vayaṃ bhagavan taṃ sahaṃ lokadhātuṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ vandanāyaitaṃ ca vimalakīrtiṃ tāṃś ca bodhisatvān darśanāya /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.8) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>, gave to that <s>bodhisattva</s> the food fragrant with all fragrances in a vessel desired by all fragrances. Thereupon ninety thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s> set forth, saying: 'We shall go, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, to that <s>Sahā</s> world-system, to pay homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and to see that <s>Vimalakīrti</s> and those <s>bodhisattvas</s>.'

body.text: sa bhagavān āha: gacchata kulaputrāḥ yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyadhve / api tu gandhān kulaputrāḥ pratisaṃhṛtya taṃ lokadhātuṃ praviśata, mā te satvā madapramādam āpatsyante / svarūpaṃ ca pratisaṃharata, mā te sahe lokadhātau satvā madgubhūtā bhaveyuḥ / mā ca tasmin !okadhātau hīnasaṃjñām utpādya pratighasaṃjñām utpādayata / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / ākāśakṣetrāṇi hi buddhakṣetrāṇi, satvaparipākāya tu buddhā bhagavanto na sarvaṃ buddhaviṣayaṃ saṃdarśayanti /
body.translated_text: That <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Go, O sons of good family, if you now think it is the right time. But restrain your fragrances when entering that world-system, lest those beings fall into intoxication and heedlessness. And conceal your own forms, lest beings in the <s>Sahā</s> world-system become dejected. And do not generate a perception of contempt toward that world-system, nor a perception of aversion. For what reason? The <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> are like fields of space, and the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, do not display the full extent of the <s>Buddha</s>'s domain for the sake of ripening beings.'

body.text: Vkn 9.9 atha nirmito bodhisatvas tad bhojanam ādāya sārdhaṃ tair navatyā bodhisatvasahasrair buddhānubhāvena vimalakīrtyadhiṣṭhānena ca tenaiva kṣaṇalavamuhūrtena sarvagandhasugandhe lokadhātāv antarhito vimalakīrter licchaver gṛhe pratyaṣṭhāt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.9) Then the emanated <s>bodhisattva</s>, having taken that food, together with ninety thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s power and <s>Vimalakīrti</s>'s supernatural transformation, in that very instant and moment, disappeared from the <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> world-system and appeared in the house of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>.

body.text: Vkn 9.10 tatra vimalakirtir navatisiṃhāsanasahasrāṇy adhitiṣṭhati yādṛśāny eva tāni prathamakāni siṃhāsanāni / tatra te bodhisatvā niṣaṇṇāḥ / sa ca nirmitas tad bhojanaparipūrṇaṃ bhājanaṃ vimalakīrter licchaver upanāmayati sma / tasya bhojanasya gandhena sarvā vaiśālī mahānagarī nirdhūpitābhūd yāvat sāhasro lokadhātuḥ sugandhagandhīkṛto 'bhūt / tatra vaiśālakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ somacchatraś ca nāma licchavīnām adhipatis taṃ gandham āghrāyāścaryaprāpto 'dbhutaprāptaḥ prahlāditakāyacetāḥ sārdhaṃ paripūrṇaiś caturaśītyā licchavisahasraiḥ / tenaiva ca bhojanagandhena bhūmāvacarā devaputrāḥ kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarāś ca devāḥ saṃcoditā vimalakīrter licchaver gṛham upasaṃkrāntā abhūvan /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.10) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> supernaturally created ninety thousand lion-thrones just like the previous lion-thrones. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> sat upon them. And the emanation offered the vessel full of food to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>. The fragrance of that food perfumed the entire great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, and even the thousand-fold world-system became fragrant with its sweet scent. The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, and the <s>Licchavi</s> chief named <s>Somacchattra</s>, upon smelling that fragrance, were filled with wonder and amazement, their bodies and minds delighted. Together with a full eighty-four thousand <s>Licchavis</s>, [they came]. And the <s>devaputras</s> dwelling on the earth, the gods of the desire realm, and the gods of the form realm, stirred by the fragrance of that food, all came to the house of <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>.

body.text: Vkn 9.11 atha vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ sthaviraṃ śāriputraṃ tāṃś ca mahāśrāvakān etad avocat: paribhuṅgdhvaṃ bhadantāḥ idaṃ tathāgatāmṛtabhojanaṃ mahākaruṇābhāvitam / mā ca pradeśacaryāyāṃ cittam upanibandhata, mā na śakyata dakṣiṇāṃ śodhayitum /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.11) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> and those great <s>śrāvakas</s>: 'Partake, venerable ones, of this food — the <s>amṛta</s> (immortal nectar) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, imbued with great compassion. But do not confine your minds to a limited scope, lest you be unable to purify the offering.'

body.text: Vkn 9.12 tatra keṣāṃcic chrāvakāṇām etad abhavat: ita evaṃ parīttād bhojanāt katham iyam īdṛśī parṣat paribhokṣyata iti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.12) Then some of the <s>śrāvakas</s> thought: 'How will such a great assembly partake of such a small amount of food?'

body.text: tān sa nirmito bodhisatvaḥ śrāvakān etad avocat: mā yūyam āyuṣmantaḥ svaprajñāpuṇyais tathāgataprajñāpuṇyāni samīkārṣṭa / syāc caturṇāṃ mahāsamudrāṇāṃ kṣayaḥ, na tv evāsya bhojanasya kaścit parikṣayaḥ / sacet sarvasatvā api sumerumātrair ālopaiḥ kalpaṃ paribhuñjīran, tathāpy asya kṣayo na syāt / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / akṣayaśīlasamādhiprajñānirjātasyedaṃ tathāgatasya pātrāvaśeṣaṃ bhojanaṃ naitac chakyaṃ kṣapayitum /
body.translated_text: The emanated <s>bodhisattva</s> said to those <s>śrāvakas</s>: 'Do not, venerable ones, measure the wisdom and merit of the <s>Tathāgata</s> by your own wisdom and merit! Even if the four great oceans were to be exhausted, this food would never be exhausted. If all beings were to eat morsels the size of <s>Sumeru</s> for an entire <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), even then this would not be exhausted. For what reason? This is the remainder of the food of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, born from inexhaustible morality, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — it cannot be exhausted.'

body.text: Vkn 9.13 atha tato bhojanāt sarvā sā parṣat tṛptā kṛtā / na ca tāvad bhojanaṃ kṣīyate / yaiś ca bodhisatvaiḥ śrāvakaiḥ śakrabrahmalokapālais tadanyaiś ca satvais tad bhojanaṃ bhuktam, teṣāṃ tādṛśaṃ sukhaṃ kāye 'vakrāntaṃ yādṛśaṃ sarvasukhapratimaṇḍite lokadhātau bodhisatvānāṃ sukham / sarvaromakūpebhyaś ca teṣāṃ tādṛśo gandhaḥ pravāti / tadyathāpi nāma tasminn eva sarvagandhasugandhe lokadhātau vṛkṣāṇāṃ gandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.13) Then from that food the entire assembly was satisfied. And the food was not diminished. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahma</s>, world-guardians, and other beings who had eaten that food — such happiness entered their bodies as the happiness of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the world-system adorned with all happiness. And from all their pores there wafted such fragrance as the fragrance of the trees in that very <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> world-system.

body.text: Vkn 9.14 atha vimalakīrtir licchavir jānann eva tān bhagavato gandhottamakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrād āgatān bodhisatvān etad avocat: kidṛśī kulaputrāḥ gandhottamakūṭasya tathāgatasya dharmadeśanā /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.14) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, knowing well those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had come from the <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>, said to them: 'What is the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s> like, O sons of good family?'

body.text: ta evam āhuḥ: na sa tathāgato 'kṣaraniruktyā dharmaṃ deśayati / tenaiva gandhena te bodhisatvā vinayaṃ gacchanti / yatra yatraiva gandhavṛkṣe te bodhisatvā niṣīdanti, tatas tatas tādṛśo gandhaḥ pravāti yat samanantarāghrāte gandhe sarvabodhisatvaguṇākaraṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhante yasya samādheḥ samanantarapratilambhāt sarveṣāṃ bodhisatvaguṇā jāyante /
body.translated_text: They said: 'That <s>Tathāgata</s> does not teach the <s>Dharma</s> through syllabic speech. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> are disciplined by that very fragrance. Wherever those <s>bodhisattvas</s> sit beneath a fragrant tree, from there such a fragrance emanates that immediately upon smelling it, they attain the <s>samādhi</s> called "Mine of All <s>Bodhisattva</s> Qualities" (<s>sarvabodhisatvaguṇākara</s>), upon the attainment of which all the qualities of a <s>bodhisattva</s> arise.'

body.text: Vkn 9.15 atha te bodhisatvā vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocan: iha punar bhagavāñ śākyamuniḥ kīdṛśīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ prakāśayati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.15) Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'And how does the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> here manifest his <s>Dharma</s>-teaching?'

body.text: āha: durdamāḥ satpuruṣāḥ ime satvāḥ / teṣāṃ durdamānāṃ satvānāṃ khaṭuṅkadurdamadamathakathām eva prakāśayati / katamaḥ punaḥ khaṭuṅkadurdamānāṃ damathaḥ, katamā ca khaṭuṅkadurdamadamathakathā / tadyatheme nirayāḥ, iyaṃ tiryagyoniḥ, ayaṃ yamalokaḥ, ime 'kṣaṇāḥ, iyaṃ hīnendriyopapartiḥ, idaṃ kāyaduścaritam, ayaṃ kāyaduścaritasya vipākaḥ, idaṃ vāgduścaritam, ayaṃ vāgduścaritasya vipākaḥ, idaṃ manoduścaritam, ayaṃ manoduścaritasya vipākaḥ, ayaṃ prāṇātipātaḥ, idam adattādānam, ayaṃ kāmamithyācāraḥ, ayaṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ, iyaṃ piśunā vāk / iyaṃ paruṣā vācā, ayaṃ saṃbhinnapralāpaḥ, iyam abhidhyā, ayaṃ vyāpādaḥ, iyaṃ mithyādṛṣṭiḥ, ayam eṣām eṣa vipākaḥ, idaṃ mātsaryam, idaṃ dauḥśīlyam, ayaṃ krodhaḥ, idaṃ kauśīdyam, ayaṃ vikṣepaḥ, idaṃ dauḥprajñyam, idaṃ dauḥprajñyasya phalam / ayaṃ prātimokṣaśikṣāvyatikramaḥ, ayaṃ prātimokṣaḥ, idaṃ karaṇīyam, idam akaraṇīyam, ayaṃ yogaḥ / idaṃ pradhānam, idam āvaraṇam, idam anāvaraṇam, iyam āpattiḥ, iyam anāpattiḥ, idam āpattivyutthānam, ayaṃ mārgaḥ / ayaṃ kumārgaḥ, idaṃ kuśalam, idam akuśalam, idaṃ sāvadyam, idam anavadyam, idaṃ sāsravam, idam anāsravam, idaṃ laukikam, idaṃ lokottaram, idaṃ saṃskṛtam, idam asaṃskṛtam, ayaṃ saṃkleśaḥ, idaṃ vyavadānam, ayaṃ saṃsāraḥ, idaṃ nirvāṇam /
body.translated_text: He said: 'These beings, O virtuous ones, are difficult to tame. For these beings who are difficult to tame, he manifests the teaching of the taming of the stubborn and difficult. And what is the taming of the stubborn, and what is the teaching of the taming of the stubborn? Namely: these are the hells, this is the animal realm, this is the world of <s>Yama</s>, these are the inopportune states, this is rebirth with deficient faculties, this is bodily misconduct and this is the ripening of bodily misconduct, this is verbal misconduct and this is the ripening of verbal misconduct, this is mental misconduct and this is the ripening of mental misconduct, this is killing, this is stealing, this is sexual misconduct, this is lying, this is slander, this is harsh speech, this is frivolous talk, this is covetousness, this is malice, this is wrong view, this is their ripening, this is avarice, this is immorality, this is anger, this is laziness, this is distraction, this is lack of wisdom and this is the fruit of lack of wisdom. This is the transgression of the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> training, this is the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, this is what should be done, this is what should not be done, this is what is appropriate. This is effort, this is obstruction, this is non-obstruction, this is an offense, this is a non-offense, this is recovery from an offense, this is the path, this is the wrong path, this is wholesome, this is unwholesome, this is blameworthy, this is blameless, this has outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>), this is free from outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), this is worldly, this is supramundane, this is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), this is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), this is defilement, this is purification, this is <s>saṃsāra</s>, this is <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: ity evam anekadharmaparibhāṣaṇatayā khaṭuṅkāśvasadṛśacittāḥ satvā avasthāpyante / tadyathā khaṭuṅko hayo gajo vā yāvan marmavedhena damathaṃ gacchati, evam eveha durdamāḥ khaṭuṅkāḥ satvās te sarvaduḥkhaparibhāṣaṇakathābhir damathaṃ gacchanti /
body.translated_text: 'Thus, through this enumeration of many <s>dharmas</s>, beings whose minds are like stubborn horses are controlled. Just as a stubborn horse or elephant is tamed by piercing its vital points, so too are these stubborn and difficult-to-tame beings here tamed through discourses that enumerate all sufferings.'

body.text: Vkn 9.16 te bodhisatvā āhuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhagavataḥ śākyamuner yatra hi nāma pratisaṃhṛtya buddhamāhātmyaṃ daridralūhatayā khaṭuṅkān satvān vinayati / ye 'pi bodhisatvā ihaivaṃ pratikaṣṭe buddhakṣetre prativasanti teṣām apy acintyā mahākaruṇā /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.16) Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said: 'Wonderful is the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, who, having concealed the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s majesty, disciplines stubborn beings through the appearance of poverty and wretchedness. And those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who dwell in this very harsh <s>buddhakṣetra</s> — their great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) too is inconceivable.'

body.text: vimalakīrtir āha: evam eva satpuruṣāḥ tathaitad yathā vadatha / ye 'pīha bodhisatvāḥ pratyājātāḥ, dṛḍhā teṣāṃ mahākaruṇā / te bahutaram iha lokadhātāv ekajanmanā kariṣyanti satvārtham / na tv eva tatra sarvagandhasugandhe lokadhātau kalpasahasreṇa satvārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'Just so, O virtuous ones. It is exactly as you say. Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are reborn here — their great compassion is firm. The benefit they accomplish for beings in a single birth in this world-system is more than what could be accomplished in a thousand <s>kalpas</s> (eons) in that All-Fragrances (<s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s>) world-system.'

body.text: Vkn 9.17 tat kasmād dhetoḥ / iha hi satpuruṣāḥ sahe lokadhātau daśa kuśaloccayā dharmāḥ, ye 'nyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu na saṃvidyante, yāṃś ca te parigṛhṇanti / katame daśa / yad idaṃ dānasaṃgraho daridreṣu, śīlasaṃgraho duḥśīleṣu, kṣāntisaṃgrahaḥ pratihateṣu, vīryasaṃgrahaḥ kuśīdeṣu, dhyānasaṃgraho vikṣiptacitteṣu, prajñāsaṃgraho duḥprajñeṣu, aṣṭākṣaṇasamatikramadeśanākṣaṇaprāpteṣu, mahāyānadeśanā prādeśikacaryāsu, kuśalamūlasaṃgraho 'navaropitakuśalamūleṣu, satatasamitaṃ satvaparipākaś caturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiḥ / imān daśa kuśaloccayān dharmān pratigṛhṇanti ye tadanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu na saṃvidyante /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.17) 'For what reason? Because, O virtuous ones, in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system there are ten <s>dharmas</s> of the accumulation of merit that are not found in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, and which they embrace. What are these ten? Namely: the collection of generosity (<s>dāna</s>) toward the poor; the collection of morality (<s>śīla</s>) toward the immoral; the collection of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) toward the hostile; the collection of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) toward the lazy; the collection of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) toward the distracted in mind; the collection of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) toward the unwise; the teaching of how to transcend the eight inopportune states for those who have attained the inopportune; the teaching of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to those engaged in limited practices; the collection of roots of merit for those who have not planted roots of merit; and the constant and continuous ripening of beings through the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>). They embrace these ten <s>dharmas</s> of the accumulation of merit, which are not found in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 9.18 te bodhisatvā āhuḥ: katamair dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisatvo 'kṣaṭo 'nupahataḥ sahāl lokadhātoś cyutvā pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ gacchati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 9.18) Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> asked: 'Endowed with what <s>dharmas</s> does a <s>bodhisattva</s>, after passing from this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, go unharmed and uninjured to a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>?'

body.text: vimalakīrtir āha: aṣṭābhiḥ kulaputraḥ dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisatvaḥ sahāl lokadhātoś cyutvākṣaṭo 'nupahataḥ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ gacchati / katamair aṣṭābhiḥ / yad uta sarvasatvānāṃ mayā hitaṃ kartavyam, na caiṣāṃ sakāśāt kiṃcid dhitaṃ paryeṣitavyam, sarvasatvaduḥkhaṃ cānenotsoḍhavyaṃ sarvaṃ cānena kuśalamūlaṃ sarvasatvānām utsraṣṭavyam, sarvasatveṣv apratighātaḥ, sarvabodhisatveṣu śāstṛprema, aśrutānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ śrutānāṃ ca śravaṇād apratikṣepaḥ, anīrṣukatā paralābheṣu svalābhenānabhimananācittanidhyaptiḥ, ātmaskhalitapratyavekṣā parasyāpattyacodanatā apramādaratasya ca sarvaguṇasamādanam / ebhir aṣṭābhir dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisatvaḥ sahāl lokadhātoś cyutvākṣaṭo 'nupahataḥ pariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ gacchati /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'Endowed with eight <s>dharmas</s>, O sons of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, after passing from this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, goes unharmed and uninjured to a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. What are these eight? Namely: "I must act for the benefit of all beings, yet I should not seek any benefit from them"; "I must bear the sufferings of all beings, yet I should dedicate all my roots of merit to all beings"; unobstructedness toward all beings; affection as for the Teacher toward all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; non-rejection upon hearing <s>dharmas</s> previously unheard as well as those already heard; non-jealousy regarding the gains of others, with the mental resolve not to take pride in one's own gains; examining one's own faults without charging others with offenses; and the undertaking of all qualities for one who delights in heedfulness. Endowed with these eight <s>dharmas</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, after passing from this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, goes unharmed and uninjured to a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.'

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśrīś ca kumārabhūtas tasyāṃ parṣadi saṃnipatitāyāṃ tathā dharmaṃ deśayato yathā paripūrṇasya prāṇisahasrasyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni, daśānāṃ ca bodhisatvasahasrāṇām anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt // //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> and <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful taught the <s>Dharma</s> in that gathered assembly in such a way that a full thousand beings generated the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and ten thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s> attained the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). //

body.text: nirmitabhojanānayanaparivarto nāma navamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, called <s>Nirmitabhojanānayanaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on Bringing the Magically Created Food). //

body.text: Vkn 10.1 tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavata āmrapālīvane dharmaṃ deśayataḥ sa maṇḍalamāḍo vipulaś ca vistīrṇaś ca saṃsthito 'bhūt / sā ca parṣat suvarṇavarṇā saṃdṛśyate sma / athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat: kasyedaṃ bhagavan pūrvanimittaṃ yad idam āmrapālīvanam evaṃ vistīrṇaṃ saṃsthitaṃ sarvā ca parṣat suvarṇavarṇā saṃdṛśyate /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.1) At that time, while the <s>Bhagavān</s> was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in <s>Āmrapālī</s>'s grove, the circumference of the assembly had become vast and extensive. And that entire assembly appeared golden-colored. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What is this portent, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that <s>Āmrapālī</s>'s grove has become so vast and the entire assembly appears golden-colored?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: eṣa ānanda vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśrīś ca kumārabhūto mahatyā parṣadā parivṛtau tathāgatasyāntikam upasaṃkramiṣyataḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Ānanda</s>, it is <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> and <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful who are approaching the <s>Tathāgata</s>, surrounded by a great assembly.'

body.text: Vkn 10.2 atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam etad avocat: gamiṣyāmo vayaṃ mañjuśrīḥ bhagavato 'ntikam / ime ca mahāsatvās tathāgataṃ drakṣyanti vandiṣyante ca /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.2) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful: 'Let us go, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. These <s>mahāsattvas</s> shall see and worship the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: āha: gacchāma kulaputra yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Let us go, O son of good family. Now is the time, as you see fit.'

body.text: atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tādṛśam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskaroti sma / yathā tāṃ sarvāvatīṃ parṣadaṃ sārdhaṃ taiḥ siṃhāsanair dakṣiṇe pāṇau pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya tāṃ parṣadaṃ dharaṇitale pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ saptakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte 'sthāt /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> performed such a supernatural feat that he placed that entire assembly together with those lion-thrones in the right palm of his hand and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he set that assembly down upon the ground, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> seven times, and stood to one side.

body.text: atha ye te bodhisatvā gandhottamakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrād āgatāḥ, te cānye ca tebhyaḥ siṃhāsanebhyo 'vatīrya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhir vanditvaikānte pratyatiṣṭhan / evaṃ śakrabrahmalokapālā devaputrāś ca bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhir vanditvaikānte pratyatiṣṭhan /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who had come from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>, and the others too, descended from those lion-thrones, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and stood to one side. Likewise the <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s>, and <s>devaputras</s> bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood to one side.

body.text: atha sa bhagavāṃs tān bodhisatvān dharmyayā kathaya pratisaṃmodyaivam āha: nisīdata kulaputrāḥ sveṣu sveṣu siṃhāsaneṣu /
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Bhagavān</s>, having greeted those <s>bodhisattvas</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, said: 'Sit down, O sons of good family, on your own lion-thrones.'

body.text: te bhagavatānujñātā nyaṣidan /
body.translated_text: They, with the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s permission, sat down.

body.text: Vkn 10.3 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma: dṛṣṭaṃ te śāriputra eṣām agrasatvānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ vikrīḍitam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.3) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Have you seen, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the miraculous play (<s>vikrīḍita</s>) of these foremost beings, these <s>bodhisattvas</s>?'

body.text: āha: dṛṣṭaṃ bhagavan /
body.translated_text: He said: 'I have seen it, <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text: bhagavān āha: tataḥ kā te saṃjñotpannā /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What perception arose in you from that?'

body.text: āha: acintyā saṃjñā me bhagavan tatrodapadyata yathā cintayituṃ tulayituṃ gaṇayituṃ na śaknomi tādṛśīṃ teṣām acintyāṃ kriyāṃ paśyāmi /
body.translated_text: He said: 'An inconceivable perception arose in me, <s>Bhagavān</s>. I cannot think, compare, or reckon [it] — such is the inconceivable activity of those [<s>Bodhisattvas</s>] that I behold.'

body.text: Vkn 10.4 athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat: anāghrātapūrvaṃ bhagavan gandham ājighrāmi / kasyaiṣa īdṛśo gandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.4) Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I smell a fragrance never before smelled, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Whose is this kind of fragrance?'

body.text: āha: eṣām eva ānanda bodhisatvānāṃ sarvaromakūpebhyo gandhaḥ kāyāt pravāti /
body.translated_text: He said: 'This fragrance, <s>Ānanda</s>, wafts from the bodies of these very <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, from all their pores.'

body.text: śāriputro 'py āha: asmākam apy āyuṣmann ānanda sarvaromakūpebhya īdṛśo gandhaḥ pravāti /
body.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> too said: 'From all our pores too, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, such a fragrance wafts forth.'

body.text: āha: kuto 'sya gandhasya prādurbhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: He asked: 'Whence is the appearance of this fragrance?'

body.text: āha: vimalakīrtinā licchavinā gandhottamakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāt sarvagandhasugandhāl lokadhātor bhojanam ānītam / tad yāvadbhir bhuktaṃ sarveṣām īdṛśo gandhaḥ kāyāt pravāti /
body.translated_text: He said: '<s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> brought food from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s> (Supreme Fragrance Heap), from the world-realm called <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> (All-Fragrance Perfumed). Whoever has eaten of it — from all of them such a fragrance wafts from the body.'

body.text: Vkn 10.5 athāyuṣmān ānando vimalakīrtiṃ bodhisatvam evam āha: kiyacciraṃ punar eṣa kulaputra gandho 'nuvartiṣyate /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.5) Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'How long, O son of good family, will this fragrance persist?'

body.text: āha: yāvad etad bhojanaṃ na pariṇataṃ bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Until this food is digested.'

body.text: ānanda āha: kiyaccireṇa punar etad bhojanaṃ pariṇaṃsyati /
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'And how long will it take for this food to be digested?'

body.text: āha: saptabhiḥ saptāhaiḥ pariṇaṃsyati / upari cāsya saptāham ojaḥ sphariṣyati / na cājīrṇadoso bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: He said: 'It will be digested in seven weeks. And for an additional week beyond that, its vital nourishment (<s>ojas</s>) will pervade [the body]. And there will be no fault of indigestion.'

body.text: Vkn 10.6 yaiś ca bhadantānanda bhikṣubhir anavakrāntaniyāmair etad bhojanaṃ bhuktaṃ teṣām avakrāntaniyāmānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati / yaiḥ punar avakrāntaniyāmair bhuktaṃ teṣāṃ nāparimuktacittānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati / yair anutpāditabodhicittaiḥ satvaiḥ paribhuktaṃ teṣām utpāditabodhicittānām pariṇaṃsyati / yair utpāditabodhicittair bhuktaṃ teṣāṃ nāpratilabdhakṣāntikānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati / yaiḥ punaḥ pratilabdhakṣāntikair bhuktaṃ teṣām ekajātipratibaddhānāṃ pariṇaṃsyati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.6) 'Moreover, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, for those monks who have eaten this food but have not yet entered upon the certainty [of the path] (<s>niyāma</s>), it will be digested when they have entered upon the certainty. For those who have already entered upon the certainty, it will be digested when their minds are fully liberated. For those beings who have eaten it but have not yet generated the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), it will be digested when they have generated the thought of awakening. For those who have generated the thought of awakening, it will be digested when they have attained the acceptance [of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>] (<s>kṣānti</s>). And for those who have attained that acceptance, it will be digested when they are bound to one more birth (<s>ekajātipratibaddha</s>).'

body.text: Vkn 10.7 tadyathāpi nāma bhadantānanda svādur nāma bhaiṣajyam, tat tāvat kauṣṭhagataṃ na pariṇamati yāvan na sarvagataṃ viṣam apagataṃ bhavati / tataḥ paścāt tad bhaiṣajyaṃ pariṇamati / evam eva bhadantānanda tāvad eva tad bhojanaṃ na pariṇataṃ bhavati yāvat sarvakleśaviṣaṃ na nirviṣaṃ bhavati / tataḥ paścāt tad bhojanaṃ pariṇamati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.7) 'Just as, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, there is a medicine called "Delicious" (<s>Svādu</s>) — that medicine, once in the stomach, does not digest until all the poison throughout [the body] has been dispelled; only then does that medicine digest. In the same way, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, that food does not digest until all the poison of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) has been rendered harmless; only then does that food digest.'

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat: buddhakṛtyaṃ bhagavan etad bhojanaṃ karoti /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This food, <s>Bhagavān</s>, performs the work of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhakṛtya</s>)!'

body.text: āha: evam etad ānanda evam etad yathā vadasi /
body.translated_text: He said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is, just as you say.'

body.text: Vkn 10.8 santy ānanda buddhakṣetrāṇi yeṣu bodhisatvā buddhakṛtyaṃ kurvanti / santi buddhakṣetrāṇi yeṣu bodhivṛkṣo buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti / santi buddhakṣetrāṇi yeṣu tathāgatalakṣaṇarūpadarśanaṃ buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti / evaṃ gaganam antarīkṣaṃ buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti / tādṛśas teṣāṃ satvānāṃ vinayo bhavati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.8) 'There are <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>Ānanda</s>, in which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work. There are <s>Buddha</s>-fields in which the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree performs the <s>Buddha</s>'s work. There are <s>Buddha</s>-fields in which the sight of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s form adorned with the marks performs the <s>Buddha</s>'s work. In the same way, the sky, the atmosphere, performs the <s>Buddha</s>'s work. Such is the discipline (<s>vinaya</s>) of those beings.'

body.text: Vkn 10.9 evaṃ svapnapratibhāsadakacandrapratiśrutkāmāyāmarīcyupamopanyāsākṣaravibhaktinirdeśāḥ satvānāṃ buddhakṛtyaṃ kurvanti / santi buddhakṣetrāṇi yatrākṣaravijñaptir buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti / santy ānanda buddhakṣetrāṇi tādṛśāni pariśuddhāni yatrānudāhāratāpravyāhāratānirdeśatānabhilāpyatā teṣāṃ satvānāṃ buddhakṛtyaṃ karoti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.9) 'In the same way, presentations through similes of dream, reflection, water-moon, echo, illusion, mirage, and the analysis of syllables perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work for beings. There are <s>Buddha</s>-fields where the communication through syllables performs the <s>Buddha</s>'s work. And there are <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>Ānanda</s>, so completely purified that silence, non-speaking, non-teaching, and inexpressibility perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work for those beings.'

body.text: Vkn 10.10 na kaścid ānanda īryāpatho na kaścid upabhogo yo buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ satvavinayāya buddhakṛtyaṃ na karoti / ye cema ānanda catvāro mārāś caturāśītiś ca kleśamukhaśatasahasrāṇi yaiḥ satvāḥ saṃkliśyante, sarvais tair buddhā bhagavanto buddhakṛtyaṃ kurvanti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.10) 'There is no deportment, <s>Ānanda</s>, and no experience of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> that does not perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work for the disciplining of beings. These four <s>Māras</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, and the eighty-four thousand gates of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) by which beings are defiled — through all of them the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work.'

body.text: Vkn 10.11 idam ānanda sarvabuddhadharmapraveśaṃ nāma dharmamukhaṃ yatra yatra dharmamukhe praviṣṭo bodhisatvaḥ sarvodāravyūhaguṇasamanvāgateṣu buddhakṣetreṣu nāvalīyate nāvanamati / sarvodāravyūhaguṇasamanvāgateṣu ca buddhakṣetreṣu na kṛṣyati nonnamati / tathāgatānāṃ ca sakāśe so 'dhimātraṃ gauravam utpādayati / āścaryam idaṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sarvadharmasamatādhimuktānāṃ satvaparipācanatayā buddhakṣetranānātvadarśanam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.11) 'This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Dharma</s>-gate called "Entry into All <s>Buddha</s>-Dharmas" (<s>sarvabuddhadharmapraveśa</s>). A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has entered into this <s>Dharma</s>-gate does not shrink or bow down before <s>Buddha</s>-fields endowed with all the most excellent array of qualities; nor is he drawn to or elated by <s>Buddha</s>-fields endowed with all the most excellent array of qualities. He generates supreme reverence in the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. This is the wonder of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> — that for those who are devoted to the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, there is the display of the diversity of <s>Buddha</s>-fields for the purpose of maturing beings.'

body.text: Vkn 10.12 tadyathā ānanda bhavati buddhakṣetrāṇām aparāparaguṇanānātvam, na punaḥ khagapathasaṃchāditasya buddhakṣetrasyākāśanānātvam / evam eva ānanda bhavati tathāgatānaṃ rupakāyanānātvam, na punas tathāgatānām asaṅgajñānanānātvam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.12) 'Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is a diversity of qualities, each different from one another, among <s>Buddha</s>-fields, but there is no diversity of space for the <s>Buddha</s>-field that is traversed by the sky-path — in the same way, <s>Ānanda</s>, there is diversity among the form-bodies (<s>rūpakāya</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, but there is no diversity among the unattached knowledge (<s>asaṅgajñāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 10.13 samā hy ānanda sarvabuddhā rūpeṇa varṇena tejasā vapuṣā lakṣaṇaiḥ kulamāhātmyena śīlena samādhinā prajñayā vimuktyā vimuktijñānadarśanena balair vaiśāradyair buddhadharmair mahāmaitryā mahākaruṇayā hitaiṣitayeryayā caryayā pratipadāyuḥpramāṇena dharmadeśanayā satvaparipākena satvavimuktyā kṣetrapariśuddhyā sarvabuddhadharmaparipūrayā / tenocyate samyaksaṃbuddha iti tathāgata iti buddha iti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.13) 'For all <s>Buddhas</s> are equal, <s>Ānanda</s>, in form, complexion, radiance, body, marks [of a great being], greatness of clan, morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, the vision of liberation-knowledge, powers (<s>bala</s>), confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas, great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), benevolent intent, conduct, practice, lifespan, teaching of <s>Dharma</s>, maturation of beings, liberation of beings, purification of [<s>Buddha</s>-]fields, and the fulfillment of all <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas. Therefore they are called <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened), <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone), and <s>Buddha</s> (Awakened).'

body.text: eṣām ānanda trayāṇāṃ padānāṃ yo 'rthavistarapadavibhaṅgaḥ sa tvayā kalpasthitikenāpi na sukaraḥ paryavāptum / trisāhasraparyāpannā apy ānanda satvās tvatsadṛśā bhaveyur agrā bahuśrutānāṃ smṛtidhāriṇīpratilabdhānām, te 'pi sarve satvā ānandasadṛśā eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ padānām arthaviniścayaṃ śrutasmṛtidhāriṇīlabdhānām arthaviniścayanirdeśaṃ kalpenāpi na śaknuyuḥ paryavāptum, yad idaṃ samyaksaṃbuddha iti tathāgata iti buddha iti / evam apramāṇā hy ānanda buddhabodhiḥ, evam acintyaṃ tathāgatānāṃ prajñāpratibhānam /
body.translated_text: 'The detailed explanation, the analysis word by word, of the meaning of these three terms, <s>Ānanda</s> — even you, living for an entire <s>kalpa</s>, could not easily complete it. Even if all the beings within a <s>trisāhasra</s> (triple-thousand) world system were like you, <s>Ānanda</s> — foremost among the learned, having attained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) — if all those beings, equal to <s>Ānanda</s>, having gained the retention of what they heard, [tried to give] a definitive exposition of the meaning of these three terms — <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, and <s>Buddha</s> — even in a <s>kalpa</s> they could not complete it. So immeasurable, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the awakening of the <s>Buddhas</s>; so inconceivable is the eloquence of wisdom (<s>prajñāpratibhāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 10.14 athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat: adyāgreṇāhaṃ bhagavan na bhūyo 'gro bahuśrutānām ity ātmānaṃ pratijñāsyāmi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.14) Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'From this day forward, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I shall no longer claim to be the foremost among the learned.'

body.text: bhagavān āha: mā tvam ānanda avalīnacittam utpādaya / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / śrāvakān saṃdhāya tvaṃ mayā ānanda agro bahuśrutānāṃ nirdiṣṭaḥ, na bodhisatvān / tiṣṭhantv ānanda bodhisatvāḥ / na te paṇḍitenāvagāhayitavyāḥ / śakyo hy ānanda sarvasāgarāṇāṃ gādhaḥ pramātum, na tv eva śakyo bodhisatvānāṃ prajñājñānasmṛtidhāraṇīpratibhānasya gādhaḥ pramātum / upekṣakā yūyam ānanda bodhisatvacaryāyāṃ bhavatha / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / ya ima ānanda vimalakīrtinā licchavinaikapūrvabhakte vyūhāḥ saṃdarśitāḥ, te sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhair ṛddhiprāptaiḥ sarvarddhivikurvitaprātihāryaiḥ kalpakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi na śakyāḥ saṃdarśayitum /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do not generate a sunken mind, <s>Ānanda</s>. Why? Because, <s>Ānanda</s>, I designated you as the foremost among the learned with reference to <s>Śrāvakas</s>, not to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Set aside the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Ānanda</s> — they should not be fathomed by a wise person. For it is possible, <s>Ānanda</s>, to measure the depth of all the oceans, but it is not possible to measure the depth of the wisdom, knowledge, mindfulness, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and eloquence of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Be equanimous, <s>Ānanda</s>, regarding the conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Why? Because these displays manifested by <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> in a single morning meal — all the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> who have attained supernatural powers, even with all their miraculous transformations and displays, could not manifest them in hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 10.15 atha ye te bodhisatvā bhagavato gandhottamakūṭasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāt sarvagandhasugandhāl lokadhātor agataḥ, te sarve prāñjalībhūtvā tathāgatasya namasyantaḥ, evaṃ ca vācam abhāsanta: pratiniḥsṛjāmo vayaṃ bhagavan tān manasikārān yair asmābhir iha buddhakṣetre hīnasaṃjñotpāditā / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / acintyo hi bhagavan buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhaviṣayaḥ / upāyakauśalyena satvaparipākāya yathā yathecchanti tathā tathā kṣetravyūhān ādarśayanti / dehi bhagavan asmabhyaṃ dharmaprābhṛtaṃ yathā vayaṃ tatra sarvagandhasugandhe lokadhātau gatā bhagavantam anusmarema /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.15) Then those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had come from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhottamakūṭa</s>, from the world-realm <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s>, all joined their palms, bowed to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and spoke thus: 'We renounce, <s>Bhagavān</s>, those mental dispositions by which we had generated a perception of inferiority regarding this <s>Buddha</s>-field. Why? Because the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> is indeed inconceivable! Through their skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), for the maturation of beings, they display whatever <s>Buddha</s>-field arrays they wish. Give us, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a gift of <s>Dharma</s>, so that having gone to the world-realm <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s>, we may remember the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 10.16 bhagavān āha: asti kulaputrāḥ kṣayākṣayo nāma bodhisatvānāṃ vimokṣaḥ / tatra yuṣmābhiḥ śikṣitavyam / sa punaḥ katamaḥ / kṣayam ucyate saṃskṛtam, akṣayam asaṃskṛtam / tad bodhisatvena saṃskṛtaṃ ca na kṣapayitavyam, asaṃskṛte ca na pratiṣṭhātavyam /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.16) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There is, sons of good family, a liberation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> called "Exhaustion-Inexhaustibility" (<s>Kṣayākṣaya</s>). Therein you should train. And what is it? "Exhaustion" refers to the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>); "inexhaustibility" refers to the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). A <s>Bodhisattva</s> should neither exhaust the conditioned nor take a stand in the unconditioned.'

body.text:
Vkn 10.17 tatra saṃskṛtasyākṣayatā, yad idaṃ mahāmaitryā acyavanatā, mahākaruṇāyā anutsargaḥ, adhyāśayasaṃprasthitasarvajñatācittasyāsaṃpramoṣaḥ, satvaparipākeṣv aparikhedaḥ, saṃgrahavastūnām ariñcanā, saddharmaparigrahāya kāyajīvitaparityāgaḥ, kuśalamūleṣv atṛptiḥ, pariṇāmanākauśalyapratiṣṭhā, dharmaparyeṣṭāv akauśīdyam, dharmadeśanāsv anācāryamuṣṭiḥ, tathāgatadarśanapūjāvastuny autsukyam, saṃcintyopapattiṣv anuttrāsaḥ, saṃpattivipattiṣv anunnāmāvanāmatā, aśikṣiteṣv aparibhavaḥ, śikṣiteṣu śāstṛpremā, kleśākīrṇānāṃ yoniśa upasaṃhāraḥ, vivekaratiṣv atanmayatā, ātmasaukhye 'nadhyavasānam, parasaukhyena tanmayatā, dhyānasamādhisamāpattiṣv avīcisaṃjñā, saṃsāra udyānavimānasaṃjñā, yācanakeṣu kalyāṇamitrasaṃjñā, sarvasvaparityāge sarvajñatāparipūrisaṃjñā, duḥśīleṣu paritrāṇasaṃjñā, pāramitāsu mātāpitṛsaṃjñā, bodhipakṣyeṣu dharmeṣu svaparivārasaṃjñā, aparyāptīkṛtāḥ sarvakuśalamūlasaṃbhārāḥ, sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇānāṃ svakṣetraniṣpādanatā, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanaparipūryai nirargaḍayajñayajanatā, kāyavākcittālaṃkāratā sarvapāpākaraṇatayā, kāyavākpariśuddhyā cittapariśuddhyā cāsaṃkhyeyakalpasaṃsaraṇatā, cittaśūratayāpramāṇabuddhaguṇaśravaṇenāsaṃsīdanatā, kleśaśatrunigrahāya prajñāśastragrahaṇatā, sarvasatvabhārodvahanatāyai skandhadhātvāyatanaparijñā, uttaptavīryatā mārasainyadharṣaṇārtham, nirmānatā dharmaparyeṣṭyai, jñānaparyeṣṭidharmagrāhyatāyā alpecchasaṃtuṣṭitā, sarvalokapriyatāyai sarvalokadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭatā, lokānuvartanatāyai sarveryāpathāvikopanatā, sarvakriyāsaṃdarśanatāyā abhijñotpādanatā, sarvaśrutadhāraṇatāyai dhāraṇīsmṛtijñānatā, sarvasatvasaṃśayacchedanatāyā indriyaparāparajñānatā, asaṅgādhiṣṭhānatā dharmadeśanatāyai, asaṅgapratibhānatā pratibhānaprāptapratilambhatayā, devamanuṣyasaṃpattyanubhavatā daśakuśalakarmapariśuddhitayā, brahmapathapratiṣṭhānatā caturapramāṇotpādanatāyai,
buddhasvarapratilambhatā dharmadeśanādhyeṣaṇānumodanāsādhukārapradānena, buddheryāpathapratilambhatā kāyavāṅmanaḥsamyamaviśeṣagāmitayā sarvadharmātanmayatayā, bodhisatvasaṃghakarṣaṇatayā mahāyānasamādāpanatā, sarvaguṇāvipraṇāśatayā cāpramādaḥ / evaṃ hi kulaputrāḥ etaddharmādhimukto bodhisatvaḥ saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.17) Therein, the inexhaustibility of the conditioned is as follows: not falling away from great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness); not abandoning great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion); not losing the mind set on <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) through superior intention; unwearied effort in the ripening of beings; not relinquishing the means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>); abandoning body and life for the sake of embracing the true <s>Dharma</s>; insatiability regarding roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>); being established in skill of dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>); diligence in the quest for the <s>Dharma</s>; holding nothing back in <s>Dharma</s>-teaching; eagerness in matters of seeing and worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s>; fearlessness regarding deliberate rebirth; neither elation nor depression in prosperity and adversity; not despising the untrained; affection as for a teacher toward the trained; judicious guidance of those beset with defilements; not being absorbed in the delight of solitude; non-attachment to personal happiness; being absorbed in the happiness of others; regarding <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments), perceiving them as <s>Avīci</s> [hell]; regarding <s>saṃsāra</s>, perceiving it as a pleasure-garden and celestial palace; regarding beggars, perceiving them as spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>); regarding the abandonment of all possessions, perceiving it as the fulfillment of <s>sarvajñatā</s>; regarding the immoral, perceiving them as those to be protected; regarding the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), perceiving them as mother and father; regarding <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>), perceiving them as one's own retinue; insatiable accumulations of all roots of merit; accomplishing one's own field through all the qualities of all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>; performing unrestricted sacrifice for the fulfillment of the [thirty-two] marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and [eighty] secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>); adorning body, speech, and mind through the non-commission of all evil; wandering through incalculable <s>kalpas</s> with purification of body, speech, and mind; through courage of mind, not sinking upon hearing the immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-qualities; taking up the weapon of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) to vanquish the enemy of defilements; thorough knowledge of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) for bearing the burden of all beings; blazing vigor for overcoming <s>Māra</s>'s armies; humility for seeking the <s>Dharma</s>; few desires and contentment for the comprehension of <s>dharmas</s> in the pursuit of knowledge; non-involvement with worldly <s>dharmas</s> for the sake of being dear to all the world; non-disturbance of all deportments for conforming to the world; generating the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) for displaying all activities; knowledge of <s>dhāraṇī</s> and memory for retaining all that is heard; knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of faculties for cutting through the doubts of all beings; unattached empowerment for teaching the <s>Dharma</s>; unattached eloquence from having attained analytical knowledge (<s>pratibhāna</s>); experiencing the prosperity of gods and humans through purification of the ten wholesome courses of action; being established in the <s>Brahmā</s>-path for generating the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>); attaining the <s>Buddha</s>-voice through requesting, rejoicing in, and praising <s>Dharma</s>-teachings; attaining the <s>Buddha</s>'s deportment through excellence in restraint of body, speech, and mind; through non-involvement with all <s>dharmas</s>; attracting the assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> through encouraging the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; and heedfulness through not losing any qualities. Thus, O sons of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> with such conviction in these <s>dharmas</s> does not exhaust the conditioned.

body.text:
Vkn 10.18 kathaṃ punar asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhate / yadā śūnyatāparijayaṃ ca karoti / na ca śūnyatāṃ sākṣātkaroti / ānimittaparijayaṃ ca karoti / na cānimittaṃ sākṣātkaroti / apraṇihitaparijayaṃ ca karoti, na cāpraṇihitaṃ sākṣātkaroti / anabhisaṃskāraparijayaṃ ca karoti, na cānabhisaṃskāraṃ sākṣātkaroti / anityam iti ca pratyavekṣate, na ca kuśalamūlais tṛpyate / duḥkham iti ca pratyavekṣate, saṃcintya copapadyate / anātmeti ca pratyavekṣate, na catmatāṃ parityajati / śāntam iti ca pratyavekṣate, na cātyantaśāntim utpādayati / viviktam iti ca pratyavekṣate, kāyacittena codyujyate / anālayam iti ca pratyavekṣate, śukladharmālayaṃ ca na vijahāti / anupādānam iti ca pratyavekṣate, upāttaṃ ca satvānāṃ bhāraṃ vahati / anāsravam iti ca pratyavekṣate, saṃsārapravṛttiṃ copayāti / apracāram iti ca pratyavekṣate, pracarati satvaparipākāya / nairātmyam iti ca pratyavekṣate, satvamahākaruṇāṃ ca notsṛjati / ajātiṃ ca pratyavekṣate, śrāvakaniyāme ca na patati / riktam iti ca tuccham iti cāsārakam iti cāsvāmikam iti cāniketam iti ca pratyavekṣate, ariktapuṇyaś
cātucchajñānaś ca paripūrṇasaṃkalpaś ca svayambhūjñānābhiṣiktaś ca svayambhūjñāne cābhiyukto nītārtho buddhavaṃśe pratiṣṭhito bhavati / evaṃ hi kulaputrāḥ evaṃ dharmādhimukto bodhisatvo 'saṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhate saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.18) How then does one not abide in the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)? One masters emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), yet does not directly realize emptiness. One masters signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), yet does not directly realize signlessness. One masters wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), yet does not directly realize wishlessness. One masters non-formation (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>), yet does not directly realize non-formation. One contemplates impermanence, yet is not satisfied with roots of merit. One contemplates suffering, yet takes deliberate rebirth. One contemplates non-self (<s>anātman</s>), yet does not abandon self-sacrifice [for others]. One contemplates peace, yet does not produce final cessation. One contemplates seclusion, yet strives with body and mind. One contemplates non-clinging (<s>anālaya</s>), yet does not forsake reliance on wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. One contemplates non-attachment (<s>anupādāna</s>), yet bears the burden of beings already taken up. One contemplates freedom from outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), yet enters into the process of <s>saṃsāra</s>. One contemplates non-activity (<s>apracāra</s>), yet acts for the ripening of beings. One contemplates selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), yet does not abandon great compassion for beings. One contemplates non-arising (<s>ajāti</s>), yet does not fall into the <s>śrāvaka</s>'s fixed course. One contemplates that [<s>dharmas</s> are] empty, worthless, without essence, without owner, and without abode — yet one possesses non-empty merit, non-worthless knowledge, fulfilled intention, is anointed by self-born knowledge (<s>svayambhūjñāna</s>), is engaged in self-born knowledge, established in the definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>), and stands in the lineage of the <s>Buddhas</s>. Thus, O sons of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> with such conviction in these <s>dharmas</s> neither abides in the unconditioned nor exhausts the conditioned.

body.text:
Vkn 10.19 puṇyasaṃbhārābhiyuktatvad asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, jñanasaṃbhārābhiyuktatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / mahāmaitrīsamanvāgatatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / satvaparipācanatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, buddhadharmābhilāṣitvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / buddhalakṣaṇaparipūraṇatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, sarvajñajñānaparipūraṇārthaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / upāyakuśalatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, prajñāsunirīkṣitatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / buddhakṣetrapariśuddhyartham asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, buddhādhiṣṭhānatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / satvārthānubhavanād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, dharmārthasaṃdarśanāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / kuśalamūlasaṃbhāratvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, kuśalamūlavāsanatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / praṇidhānaparipūraṇārtham asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, apraṇihitatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / āśayapariśuddhatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, adhyāśayapariśuddhatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / pañcābhijñāvikrīḍitatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, buddhajñānaṣaḍabhijñatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / pāramitāsaṃbhāraparipūraṇārtham asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, aparipūrṇakālatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / dharmadhanasamudānayanatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, prādeśikadharmānarthikatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / sarvabhaiṣajyasamudānayanatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, yathārhabhaiṣajyaprayojanāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / dṛḍhapratijñayā asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, pratijñottāraṇatvāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / dharmabhaiṣajyasamudānayanatvād asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, yathāpītvaradharmabhaiṣajyaprayojanāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / sarvasatvakleśavyādhiparijñānām asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati, sarvavyādhiśamanāt saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati / evaṃ hi kulaputrāḥ bodhisatvaḥ saṃskṛtaṃ na kṣapayati, asaṃskṛte na pratitiṣṭhati
/ ayam ucyate kṣayākṣayo nāma bodhisatvānāṃ vimokṣaḥ / tatra yuṣmābhiḥ satpuruṣāḥ yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.19) Because of engagement with the accumulation of merit (<s>puṇyasaṃbhāra</s>), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of engagement with the accumulation of knowledge (<s>jñānasaṃbhāra</s>), he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of being endowed with great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of being endowed with great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of ripening beings, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of aspiration for <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of fulfilling the <s>Buddha</s>-marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), he does not abide in the unconditioned; for the sake of fulfilling omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>), he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of being well-examined by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of purifying <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of the empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of experiencing the welfare of beings, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of demonstrating the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of accumulating roots of merit, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of the habituation of roots of merit, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of fulfilling vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of wishlessness, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of purity of intention, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of purity of superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>), he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of sporting with the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of the six <s>abhijñās</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, he does not exhaust the conditioned. For the sake of fulfilling the accumulation of <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), he does not abide in the unconditioned; because the time [for fulfillment] is not yet complete, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of gathering the wealth of the <s>Dharma</s>, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of not desiring partial <s>dharmas</s>, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of gathering all medicines, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of applying medicines as appropriate, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of firm resolution, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of fulfilling his resolutions, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of gathering the medicine of the <s>Dharma</s>, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of applying the medicine of the <s>Dharma</s> as speedily needed, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Because of knowing the diseases of the defilements of all beings, he does not abide in the unconditioned; because of curing all diseases, he does not exhaust the conditioned. Thus, O sons of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not exhaust the conditioned and does not abide in the unconditioned. This is called the liberation of <s>bodhisattvas</s> named <s>kṣayākṣaya</s> (exhaustion-inexhaustibility). Therein, O good sirs, you should apply yourselves.

body.text: Vkn 10.20 atha khalu te bodhisatvā imaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭā udagra āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā bhagavataḥ pūjākarmaṇe teṣāṃ ca bodhisatvānām asya dharmaparyāyasya pūjākarmaṇe sarvam imaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ sarvacūrṇagandhadhupavyūhaiḥ puṣpaiś ca jānumātraṃ saṃchādya bhagavataś ca parṣanmaṇḍalam abhikīrtiṃ kṛtvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhir vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triṣpradakṣiṇīkṛtyodānam udānayanta iha buddhakṣetre 'ntarhitās tena kṣaṇalavamuhūrtena tatra sarvagandhasugandhe lokadhātau pratyupasthitāḥ // //
body.translated_text: (Vkn 10.20) Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having heard this teaching, were delighted, uplifted, elated, joyful, and filled with pleasure and happiness. For the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, of those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, they covered this entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world system) knee-deep with arrays of all powdered incense and flowers. Having proclaimed the glory of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s assembly, having paid homage with their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, and having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, they uttered this solemn utterance: disappearing from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, in that very instant they arrived at that <s>Sarvagandhasugandha</s> world-system. //

body.text: kṣayākṣayo nāma dharmaprābhṛtaparivarto daśamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth chapter, called <s>Kṣayākṣayadharmaprābhṛtaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on the Dharma-Gift of Exhaustion-Inexhaustibility). //

body.text: Vkn 11.1 atha khalu bhagavān vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat: yadā tvaṃ kulaputra tathāgatasya darśanakāmo bhavasi, tadā kathaṃ tvaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyasi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.1) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'When you, O son of good family, desire to see the <s>Tathāgata</s>, how do you see the <s>Tathāgata</s>?'

body.text: evam ukte vimalakīrtir licchavir bhagavantam etad avocat: yadāhaṃ bhagavan tathāgatasya darśanakāmo bhavāmi, tadā tathāgatam apaśyanayā paśyāmi / pūrvāntato 'jātam aparāntato 'saṃkrāntaṃ pratyutpanne 'dhvany asaṃsthitaṃ paśyāmi / tat kasya hetoḥ / rūpatathatāsvabhāvam arūpam, vedanātathatāsvabhāvam avedanām, saṃjñātathatāsvabhāvam asaṃjñam, saṃskāratathatāsvabhāvam asaṃskāram, vijñānatathatāsvabhāvam avijñānam, caturdhātvasaṃprāptam ākāśadhātusamam, ṣaḍāyatanānutpannaṃ cakṣuḥpathasamatikrāntaṃ śrotrapathasamatikrāntaṃ ghrāṇapathasamatikrāntaṃ jihvāpathasamatikrāntaṃ kāyapathasamatikrāntaṃ manaḥpathasamatikrāntam, traidhātukāsaṃsṛṣṭam, trimalāpagatam, trivimokṣānugatam, trividyānuprāptam, aprāptaṃ saṃprāptam, sarvadharmeṣv asaṅgakoṭīgataṃ bhūtakoṭyakoṭikam, tathatāpratiṣṭhitaṃ tadanyonyavisaṃyuktam, na hetujanitaṃ na pratyayādhīnam, na vilakṣaṇaṃ na salakṣaṇam, naikalakṣaṇaṃ na nānālakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'When I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, desire to see the <s>Tathāgata</s>, I see the <s>Tathāgata</s> by way of not-seeing. I see him as unborn from the prior limit, as not passing on to the posterior limit, as not abiding in the present time. For what reason? I see the own-nature of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of form as formless, the own-nature of the <s>tathatā</s> of feeling as unfelt, the own-nature of the <s>tathatā</s> of perception as unperceived, the own-nature of the <s>tathatā</s> of formations as unformed, the own-nature of the <s>tathatā</s> of consciousness as unconscious; as not attaining the four elements, as equal to the space element; as unarisen from the six sense-bases, as having transcended the path of the eye, having transcended the path of the ear, having transcended the path of the nose, having transcended the path of the tongue, having transcended the path of the body, having transcended the path of the mind; as unsullied by the three realms, as free from the three stains; as following the three liberations (<s>trivimokṣa</s>), as having reached the three knowledges (<s>trividyā</s>); as unattained yet fully attained; as having arrived at the limit of non-attachment regarding all <s>dharmas</s>, as being the very pinnacle of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>); as established in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), as mutually disjoined from all that is other; as not produced by causes, not dependent on conditions; as neither having different characteristics nor having the same characteristics, as neither having a single characteristic nor having manifold characteristics.'

body.text: na lakṣyate na saṃlakṣyate na vilakṣyate, nārvāṅ na pāre na madhye, neha na tatra, neto nānyataḥ, na jñānavijñeyo na vijñānapratiṣṭhitaḥ, atamo 'prakāśaḥ, anāmānimittam, na durbalo na balavān, na deśastho na pradeśasthaḥ, na śubho nāśubhaḥ, na saṃskṛto nāsaṃskṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'He is not characterized, not recognized, not distinguished; not on this side, not on the far side, not in between; not here, not there; not hence, not elsewhere; not knowable by knowledge, not established in consciousness; without darkness, without light; without name, without sign; neither weak nor strong; not in a place nor in a part of a place; neither auspicious nor inauspicious; neither conditioned nor unconditioned.'

body.text: nāpi kenacid arthena vacanīyaḥ, na dānato na mātsaryataḥ, na śīlato na dauḥśīlyataḥ, na kṣāntito na vyāpādataḥ, na vīryato na kauśīdyataḥ, na dhyānato na vikṣepataḥ, na prajñāto na dauḥprajñyataḥ, na vacanīyo nāvacanīyaḥ, na satyato na mṛṣātaḥ, na nairyāṇikato nānairyāṇikataḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Nor is he to be described by any meaning: not through generosity and not through avarice; not through morality and not through immorality; not through patience and not through malice; not through vigor and not through laziness; not through meditation and not through distraction; not through wisdom and not through lack of wisdom; neither describable nor indescribable; not through truth and not through falsehood; not through leading to the goal and not through leading astray.'

body.text: na gamānīyo nāgamanīyaḥ, sarvarutavyāhārasamucchinnaḥ, na kṣetrabhūto nākṣetrabhūtaḥ, na dakṣiṇārho na dakṣiṇāśodhayitā, agrāhyaḥ, aparāmṛṣṭaḥ, aniketaḥ, asaṃskṛtaḥ, saṃkhyāpagataḥ, samatayā samaḥ, dharmatayā tulyaḥ, atulyavīryaḥ, tulanāsamatikrāntaḥ, na krānto na cākrāntaḥ, na samatikrāntaḥ, na dṛṣṭaśrutaparijñātaḥ, sarvagranthivigataḥ, sarvajñajñānasamatāprāptaḥ, sarvasatvasamaḥ, sarvadharmanirviśeṣaprāptaḥ, sarvato 'navadyaḥ, niṣkiṃcanaḥ, niṣkaṣāyaḥ, niṣkalaḥ, nirvikalpaḥ, akṛtaḥ, ajātaḥ, anutpannaḥ, abhūtaḥ, asaṃbhūtaḥ, na bhaviṣyati, nirbhayaḥ, niṣkleśaḥ, niḥśokaḥ, niṣprītikaḥ, nīrūrmikaḥ, sarvavyavahāranirdeśair avacanīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'He is not to be gone to and not to be come from; with all speech and expression utterly cut off; neither a field nor a non-field; neither worthy of offerings nor a purifier of offerings; ungraspable, untouched, without abode, unconditioned; gone beyond enumeration; equal through equality; identical through the nature of <s>Dharma</s>; of incomparable vigor, having transcended all comparison; neither gone beyond nor not gone beyond; not surpassed; not known through what is seen, heard, or understood; free from all knots; having reached the equality of omniscient knowledge; equal toward all beings; having attained non-differentiation regarding all <s>dharmas</s>; irreproachable in all respects; without possessions, without passion, without parts, without conceptualization; unmade, unborn, unarisen, unexistent, unproduced; he will not be; fearless, free from defilements, free from grief, free from pleasure, free from agitation; indescribable by any conventional designation.'

body.text: īdṛśo bhagavan tathāgatasya kāyaḥ / sa tathaiva draṣṭavyaḥ / ya evaṃ paśyanti, te samyak paśyanti / ye tv anyathā paśyanti, te mithyā paśyanti /
body.translated_text: 'Such, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. It should be seen in just this way. Those who see thus — they see rightly. Those who see otherwise — they see wrongly.'

body.text: Vkn 11.2 athāyuṣmāñ śāriputro bhagavantam etad avocat: katamasmād bhagavan buddhakṣetrāc cyutau vimalakīrtiḥ kulaputra idaṃ buddhakṣetram āgataḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.2) Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'From which <s>buddhakṣetra</s> did this son of good family <s>Vimalakīrti</s> pass away and come to this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: etam eva tvaṃ śāriputra satpuruṣaṃ paripṛccha ḥ kutas tvaṃ cyutvehopapanna iti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Ask this virtuous man yourself, <s>Śāriputra</s>: "From where did you pass away and come to be reborn here?"'

body.text: athāyuṣmāñ śāriputro vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat: kutas tvaṃ kulaputra cyutyehopapannaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'From where, O son of good family, did you pass away and come to be reborn here?'

body.text: vimalakīrtir āha: yaḥ sthavireṇa dharmaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ, kaccit tasya dharmasya cyutir upapattir vā /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'The <s>dharma</s> that the elder has directly realized — does that <s>dharma</s> have any passing away or rebirth?'

body.text: āha: na tasya dharmasya kācic cyutir upapattir vā /
body.translated_text: He said: 'That <s>dharma</s> has no passing away or rebirth whatsoever.'
