body.text: āha: evam acyutikānām anutpattikānāṃ bhadantaśāriputra sarvadharmāṇāṃ kutas tavaivaṃ bhavati ḥ kutas tvaṃ cyutvehopapanna iti / yaṃ bhadantaśāriputra nirmitāṃ striyaṃ puruṣaṃ vā pṛccheḥ ḥ kutas tvaṃ cyutvehopapanna iti / sa kiṃ vyākuryāt /
body.translated_text: He said: 'If, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are of such a nature — without passing away and without arising — then how can you think: "From where did you pass away and come to be reborn here?" If, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, you were to ask a magically created woman or man: "From where did you pass away and come to be reborn here?" — what would that one answer?'

body.text: āha: na kulaputra nirmitasya cyutir nopapattiḥ, sa kiṃ vyākariṣyati /
body.translated_text: He said: 'A magical creation, O son of good family, has no passing away and no rebirth. What would it answer?'

body.text: āha: nanu bhadantaśāriputra nirmitasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmās tathāgatena nirdiṣṭāḥ /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Has not the <s>Tathāgata</s> declared, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of magical creations?'

body.text: āha: evam etat kulaputra /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Indeed so, O son of good family.'

body.text: āha: nirmitasvabhāveṣu bhadantaśāriputra sarvadharmeṣu ḥ kutas tvaṃ cyutvehopapanna iti / cyutir iti bhadantaśāriputra abhisaṃskārakṣanaIakṣaṇapadam etat / upapattir ity abhisaṃskāraprabandha eṣaḥ / tatra bodhisatvaś cyavate, na kuśalamūlābhisaṃskāraṃ kṣapayati / upapadyate ca, na cākuśalaṃ prabadhnāti /
body.translated_text: He said: 'If, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of magical creations, then [the question] "From where did you pass away and come to be reborn here?" — "passing away," venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is a term for the momentary characteristic of conditioned activity; "rebirth" is the continuity of conditioned activity. In this regard, a <s>bodhisattva</s> passes away without exhausting the conditioning of roots of merit, and is reborn without perpetuating unwholesomeness.'

body.text: Vkn 11.3 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma: akṣobhyasya śāriputra tathāgatasya sakāśād āgata eṣa kulaputro 'bhiratyā Iokadhātoḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.3) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'This son of good family, <s>Śāriputra</s>, has come from the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, from the world-system <s>Abhirati</s>.'

body.text: āha: āścaryaṃ bhagavan yad eṣa satpuruṣas tāvatpariśuddhād buddhakṣetrād āgatyehaivaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭe buddhakṣetre 'bhiramate /
body.translated_text: He said: 'It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that this virtuous man, having come from such a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, takes delight in this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> that is so polluted with many faults.'

body.text: vimalakīrtir āha: tat kiṃ manyase bhadantaśāriputra api nu sūryaraśmayo 'ndhakāreṇa sārdhaṃ ramante /
body.translated_text: <s>Vimalakīrti</s> said: 'What do you think, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> — do the rays of the sun take delight together with darkness?'

body.text: āha: no hīdaṃ kulaputra, na tayor yogo 'sti / sahodgate hi sūryamaṇḍale sarvaṃ tamo 'payānti /
body.translated_text: He said: 'No indeed, O son of good family. There is no conjunction between them. When the solar disc rises, all darkness departs.'

body.text: āha: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ punaḥ sūryo jambūdvīpa udayate /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Then for what reason does the sun rise over <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?'

body.text: āha: yāvad evāvabhāsakaraṇāya tamo'paghātaya ca /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Precisely for the purpose of illumination and the dispelling of darkness.'

body.text: āha: evam eva śāriputra saṃcintya bodhisatvā apariśuddheṣu buddhakṣetreṣūpapadyante satvānāṃ pariśodhanāya / na ca kleśaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃvasanti, kleśāndhakāraṃ ca vidhamanti sarvasatvānām /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Just so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> deliberately take rebirth in impure <s>buddhakṣetras</s> for the purification of beings. They do not dwell together with defilements, but rather dispel the darkness of defilements for all beings.'

body.text: Vkn 11.4 atha sā sarvā parṣat paritṛṣitābhut: paśyema vayaṃ tam abhiratiṃ lokadhātuṃ taṃ cākṣobhyaṃ tathāgataṃ tāṃś ca bodhisatvāṃs tāṃś ca mahāśrāvakān /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.4) Then that entire assembly became eager: 'Let us see that world-system <s>Abhirati</s> and that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s> and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and those great <s>śrāvakas</s>!'

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyāḥ sarvasyāḥ parṣadaś cetasa cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāya vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat: darśaya kulaputra asyāḥ parṣadas tām abhiratiṃ lokadhātuṃ taṃ cākṣobhyaṃ tathāgatam / draṣṭukameyam parsat /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the mental deliberation of that entire assembly, said to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'Show this assembly, O son of good family, that world-system <s>Abhirati</s> and that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>! This assembly wishes to see them.'

body.text: atha vimalakīrter licchaver etad abhavat: yan nv aham itaś cāsanān nottiṣṭheyam / tāṃ cābhiratiṃ lokadhātum anekabodhisatvaśatasahasrāṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsurādhyuṣitāṃ sacakravāḍaparikhāṃ sanadītaḍāgotsasaraḥsamudraparikhāṃ sasumerugirikūṭaparvatāṃ sacandrasūryajyotiṣāṃ sadevanāgayakṣagandharvabhavanāṃ sabrahmabhavanapārisadyāṃ sagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭramanuṣyāṃ sastryāgārāṃ sabodhisatvasaśrāvakaparṣadam, akṣobhyasya tathāgatasya bodhivṛkṣam, akṣobhyaṃ ca tathāgataṃ sāgaropamāyāṃ mahāparṣadi niṣaṇṇaṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānam, api tāni padmāni yāni daśasu dikṣu buddhakṛtyaṃ kurvanti satvānām, api tāni trīṇi ratnamayāni sopānāni yāni jambūdvīpam upādāya trayastriṃśadbhavanam abhyudgatāni yaiḥ sopānair devās trayastriṃśato jambūdvīpam avataranty akṣobhyaṃ tathāgataṃ darśanāya vandanāyai paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya jāmbudvīpakāś ca manuṣyās trayastriṃśadbhavanam abhirohanti devāṃs trayastriṃśato darśanāya / evam apramāṇaguṇasamuditāṃ tām abhiratiṃ lokadhātum apskandham upādāya yāvad akaniṣṭhabhavanaṃ bhārgavacakram iva paricchidya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā puṣpadāmam ivādāyemāṃ lokadhātuṃ praveśayeyam / praveśya cāsyāḥ sarvasyāḥ parṣado darśayeyam /
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>: 'Without rising from this seat, I shall take that world-system <s>Abhirati</s> — with its many hundreds of thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, inhabited by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Asuras</s>, with its <s>Cakravāḍa</s> mountain-ring, with its rivers, ponds, springs, streams, and ocean-ring, with its <s>Sumeru</s> and mountain-peaks and ranges, with its suns, moons, and constellations, with its abodes of <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s>, with its <s>Brahma</s>-abodes and assemblies, with its villages, cities, market-towns, settlements, kingdoms, and human inhabitants, with its women's quarters, with its assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>śrāvakas</s>, the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s> himself seated in an ocean-like great assembly teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, and also those lotuses that perform the <s>Buddha</s>'s work in the ten directions for beings, and also those three jeweled stairways extending from <s>Jambudvīpa</s> up to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven by which the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods descend to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> to see, worship, and attend upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s> and hear the <s>Dharma</s>, and the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> ascend to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven to see those gods — that world-system <s>Abhirati</s> endowed with immeasurable virtues, including the water-mass up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven, having cut it off like a potter's wheel with my right hand and taken it up like a flower-garland, I shall bring it into this world-system and show it to this entire assembly.'

body.text: Vkn 11.5 atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samādhim samāpannaḥ, tādṛśaṃ carddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskṛtavān yas tam abhiratiṃ lokadhatuṃ paricchidya dakṣiṇena pāninā gṛhītvemaṃ sahaṃ lokadhātuṃ praveśayati sma /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.5) Then <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, at that very moment, entered into such a <s>samādhi</s> and performed such a supernatural feat that he cut off that world-system <s>Abhirati</s> and, taking it with his right hand, brought it into this <s>Sahā</s> world-system.

body.text: Vkn 11.6 tatra ye divyacakṣuṣo 'bhijñāpratilabdhāḥ śrāvakā bodhisatvā devamanuṣyāś ca, te mahāntam utkrośam utkrośanti sma: knyāmahe bhagavan kriyāmahe sugata / trāya ca tathāgata iti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.6) Thereupon, those <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>devas</s>, and humans who had attained the superknowledge of the divine eye cried out in great alarm: 'We are being carried away, <s>Bhagavān</s>! We are being carried away, <s>Sugata</s>! Save us, <s>Tathāgata</s>!'

body.text: tān bhagavān vinayanārtham evam āha: na mamātra vṛṣabhitā vimalakīrtinā bodhisatvena kriyamāṇānām /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to them for the purpose of their discipline: 'This is not my doing. It is being done by the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vimalakīrti</s>.'

body.text: tatra ye punar anye devamanuṣyāḥ, te na jānanti na paśyanti ḥ kuto vayaṃ kriyāmaha iti / na hy abhiratyā lokadhātor imaṃ sahaṃ lokadhātuṃ praveśitāyā ūnatvaṃ na pūrṇatvam abhūt / na cāsya lokadhātor utpīḍo na saṃbādhaḥ / nāpy abhiratyā lokadhātor ūnabhāvaḥ / yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt saṃdṛśyate /
body.translated_text: However, those other <s>devas</s> and humans who did not possess that superknowledge neither knew nor saw: 'Where are we being carried to?' For when the world-system <s>Abhirati</s> was brought into this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, there was neither diminishment nor fullness in this world-system, nor was there any crowding or constriction. Nor was there any diminishment in the world-system <s>Abhirati</s>. It appeared just as it had before.

body.text: Vkn 11.7 atha bhagavāñ śākyamunis tāṃ sarvāṃ parṣadam āmantrayate sma: paśyata mārṣāḥ abhiratiṃ lokadhātum akṣobhyaṃ ca tathāgatam etāṃś ca kṣetravyūhāñ śrāvakavyūhān bodhisatvavyūhāṃś ca /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.7) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> addressed that entire assembly: 'Look, O noble ones, at the world-system <s>Abhirati</s> and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, and these arrays of the field, arrays of <s>śrāvakas</s>, and arrays of <s>bodhisattvas</s>!'

body.text: ta āhuḥ: paśyāmo bhagavan iti /
body.translated_text: They said: 'We see them, <s>Bhagavān</s>!'

body.text: āha: īdṛśaṃ mārsāḥ buddhakṣetraṃ parigrahītukāmena bodhisatvenākṣobhyasya tathāgatasya bodhisatvacaryāyām anuśikṣitavyam /
body.translated_text: He said: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to embrace such a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> should train in the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>.'

body.text: asmin punar abhiratilokadhātusaṃdarśanarddhiprātihārye 'kṣobhyasya ca tathāgatasya saṃdarśane 'smin sahe lokadhātau caturdaśānām ayutānāṃ devamānuṣikāyāḥ prajāyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni / sarvaiś cābhiratyāṃ lokadhātau praṇidhānam utpāditam upapattaye / te sarve bhagavatā vyākṛtā abhiratyāṃ lokadhātāv upapattaye / iti hi vimalakīrtir licchavir yāvān iha sahe lokadhātau satvaparipākaḥ kartavyas taṃ sarvaṃ kṛtvā punar eva tām abhiratiṃ lokadhātuṃ yathasthāne sthāpayamāsa /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, through the display of this miraculous feat of showing the world-system <s>Abhirati</s> and the manifestation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, one hundred and forty thousand beings of the human and divine assembly generated the mind of supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And all of them formed the aspiration to be reborn in the world-system <s>Abhirati</s>. They were all given a prediction by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for rebirth in the world-system <s>Abhirati</s>. Thus <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, having accomplished all the ripening of beings that was to be done here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, returned that world-system <s>Abhirati</s> to its original place.

body.text: Vkn 11.8 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma: dṛṣṭā te śāriputra abhiratir lokadhātuḥ sa cākṣobhyas tathagataḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.8) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Did you see, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the world-system <s>Abhirati</s> and that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>?'

body.text: āha: dṛṣṭā me bhagavan / sarvasatvānāṃ tādṛśā buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhā bhavantu / sarvasatvāś cedṛśyarddhyā samanvāgatā bhavantāṃ yādṛśyā vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ kulaputraḥ / ebhir api ca sulabdhā lābhāḥ / ye vayam īdṛśān satpuruṣān labhāmahe darśanāya / teṣam api satvānāṃ sulabdhā lābhā bhaviṣyanti, ya etarhi tathāgatasya tiṣṭhato vā parinirvṛtasya vemaṃ dharmaparyāyam antaśaḥ śroṣyanti / kaḥ punar vādaḥ, ye śrutvādhimokṣyante pratyeṣyanty udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanty adhimokṣyanti pravartayiṣyanti parebhyaś ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti bhāvanāyogam anuyuktāś ca bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: He said: 'I have seen it, <s>Bhagavān</s>. May all beings have such arrays of <s>buddhakṣetra</s> qualities! May all beings be endowed with such supernatural powers as those of the <s>Licchavi</s> son of good family <s>Vimalakīrti</s>! And well-gained indeed are the gains of us who have obtained the sight of such a noble person. Well-gained too will be the gains of those beings who, whether the <s>Tathāgata</s> is still living or has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will hear even so much as this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma). How much more so for those who, having heard it, will have faith in it, will investigate it, will take it up, will retain it, will recite it, will comprehend it, will aspire to it, will propagate it, will explain it extensively to others, and will devote themselves to the practice of meditation upon it!'

body.text: Vkn 11.9 te dharmaratnanidhānaprāptā bhaviṣyanti, yeṣām ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo hastagato bhaviṣyati / tathāgatasahāyās te bhaviṣyanti, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ svādhyāsyante / dharmasaṃrakṣakās te bhaviṣyanti, ya etaddharmādhimuktānām upasthānaparicaryāṃ kariṣyanti / gṛhagatas teṣāṃ tathāgato bhaviṣyati, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sulikhitaṃ kṛtvā dhārayiṣyanti satkariṣyanti / sarvapuṇyaparigṛhītās te bhaviṣyanti, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyam anumodiṣyante / mahādharmayajñaṃ te yajiṣyanti, ya ito dharmaparyāyād antaśaś catuṣpadikām api gāthāṃ saṃvaram api parebhyo vistareṇa deśayiṣyanti / tad eva teṣāṃ bhagavan vyākaraṇaṃ yeṣām iha dharmaparyāye kṣāntī rucir matiḥ prekṣā dṛṣṭir adhimuktir muktiś ca bhaviṣyati // //
body.translated_text: (Vkn 11.9) 'Those in whose hands this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will come — they will have obtained a treasury of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>. Those who will study this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — they will be companions of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Those who will serve and attend upon those who have faith in this <s>Dharma</s> — they will be protectors of the <s>Dharma</s>. Those who, having copied this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> well, will retain it and honor it — in their homes the <s>Tathāgata</s> will be present. Those who will rejoice in this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — they will be embraced by all merit. Those who will teach others extensively even a single four-line verse from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — they will have performed the great <s>Dharma</s>-sacrifice. That itself, <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall be their prediction — those in whom there will be patience, delight, understanding, discernment, vision, aspiration, and liberation with regard to this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>.' //

body.text: abhiratilokadhātvānayanākṣobhyatathāgatadarśanaparivarta ekādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh chapter, called <s>Abhiratilokadhātvānayanākṣobhyatathāgatadarśanaparivarta</s> (The Chapter on Bringing the World-System <s>Abhirati</s> and Seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>). //

body.text: Vkn 12.1 atha khalu śakro devānām indro bhagavantam etad avocat: bahuni me bhagavan tathāgatasyāntikān mañjuśriyaś ca kumārabhūtasyāntikād dharmaparyāyaśatasahasrāṇi śrutāni / na ca me jātv evam acintyavimokṣavikurvitadharmanayapraveśaśrutapūrvo yādṛśa iha dharmaparyāye nirdiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.1) Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I have heard hundreds of thousands of <s>dharmaparyāyas</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s> and from <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful. But never before have I heard an entry into the <s>Dharma</s>-method of the miraculous play of <s>acintyavimokṣa</s> (inconceivable liberation) such as has been set forth in this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 12.2 niḥsaṃśayaṃ te satvā evaṃ dharmabhājanā bhaviṣyanti, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyam udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti / kaḥ punar vādaḥ / ye bhāvanāyogam anuyuktā bhaviṣyanti, pithitās teṣāṃ sarvāpāyāḥ, anāvṛtās teṣāṃ sarve sugatipathāḥ, dṛṣṭās te sarvabuddhaiḥ, nihatās taiḥ sarvaparapravādinaḥ, parājitās taiḥ sarvamārāḥ, viśodhitās tair bodhimārgāḥ, pratiṣṭhitās te bodhimaṇḍe, tathāgatagatisamavasaraṇās te bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.2) 'Without doubt, those beings who will take up this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, retain it, recite it, and comprehend it will be vessels of the <s>Dharma</s>. How much more so for those who will devote themselves to the practice of meditation upon it — all lower rebirths will be blocked for them, all paths to fortunate destinies will be opened for them, they will be seen by all <s>Buddhas</s>, all rival debaters will be struck down by them, all <s>Māras</s> will be defeated by them, the path to enlightenment will be purified by them, they will be established on the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening), and they will arrive at the course of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 12.3 ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, aham api bhagavan teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇām upasthānaparicaryāṃ kariṣyāmi sārdhaṃ sarvaparivāreṇa / yatra ca grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣv ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ pracariṣyati deśayiṣyati saṃprakāśayiṣyati, tatrāhaṃ saparivāro dharmaśravaṇāyopasaṃkrāmiṣyāmi / aprasannānāṃ ca kulaputrāṇāṃ prasādam utpādayiṣyāmi, prasannānāṃ ca dhārmikiṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.3) 'I too, <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with my entire retinue, will perform service and attendance upon those sons of good family who will retain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. And wherever — in villages, cities, market-towns, settlements, kingdoms, or capital cities — this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will be practiced, taught, and explained, there I shall come together with my retinue to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And I shall generate faith in the sons of good family who lack faith, and for those who have faith I shall provide the <s>Dharma</s>-protection, shelter, and guardianship.'

body.text: Vkn 12.4 evam ukte bhagavāñ śakraṃ devānām indram etad avocat: sādhu sādhu devānam indra, subhāṣitaṃ te 'numodate tathāgataḥ / yā devānām indra atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhir iha dharmaparyāya uddiṣṭā / tasmād iha devendra atītānāgatapratyutpannās tena kulaputreṇa va kuladuhitrā vā buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūjitā bhaviṣyanti, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyam udgrahīṣyaty antaśaḥ pustakalikhitam api kariṣyati vācayiṣyati likhiṣyati paryavāpsyati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.4) When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, O lord of the <s>devas</s>! The <s>Tathāgata</s> approves your well-spoken words. The enlightenment of the past, future, and present <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, is set forth in this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Therefore, lord of the <s>devas</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, or will even copy it into a manuscript, or will recite it, or will write it, or will comprehend it — by them the past, future, and present <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, will have been worshipped.'

body.text: Vkn 12.5 yaś ca punar devendra kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vemaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ tathāgatapūrṇaṃ tadyathāpi nāmekṣuvanaṃ vā naḍavanaṃ vā veṇuvanaṃ vā tilavanaṃ vaivaṃ śālivanaṃ vā pratipūrṇaṃ kalpaṃ vā kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā satkuryād gurukuryān mānayet pūjayet tāṃs tathāgatān sarvapūjābhiḥ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ, parinirvṛtānāṃ ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānām ekaikasya tathāgatasya pūjākarmaṇa ekaghanasyāvikopitasya śarīrasya sarvaratnamayaṃ stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayec caturmahādvīpikalokadhātupramāṇaṃ yāvad brahmalokam uccaistvena yaṣṭicchatrapatākābhir udviddhopaśobhitam evaṃ sarvatathāgatānāṃ pratyekaṃ stūpaṃ kārayet, sa ca tatra kalpaṃ vā kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā pūjāṃ kuryāt sarvapuṣpaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ sarvadhvajapatākābhiḥ sarvatūryatāḍāvacarasaṃpravāditena pūjāṃ kuryāt, tat kiṃ manyase devānām indra api nu sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tato nidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasunuyāt /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.5) 'Furthermore, lord of the <s>devas</s>, if a son of good family or daughter of good family were to fill this entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra</s> (triple-thousand great-thousand) world-system, packed with <s>Tathāgatas</s> as densely as a field of sugarcane, or a thicket of reeds, or a bamboo grove, or a field of sesame, or a paddy field, and were to honor, respect, revere, and worship those <s>Tathāgatas</s> with all forms of worship and all provisions of comfort for a <s>kalpa</s> or for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>; and after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, were to erect for each and every <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the worship of each one's undivided and intact bodily relics, a <s>stūpa</s> made entirely of precious substances, as vast as the four-continent world-system in extent, reaching up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world in height, adorned and beautified with pinnacles, parasols, and banners; and were to make offerings to all those <s>stūpas</s> of every <s>Tathāgata</s> for a <s>kalpa</s> or for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>, with all flowers, all fragrances, all banners and flags, and with the sounding of all instruments and music — what do you think, lord of the <s>devas</s>, would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit from that?'

body.text: āha: bahu bhagavan bahu sugata, nāsya puṇyaskandhasya śakyaḥ paryanto 'dhigantuṃ kalpakoṭīśatasahasrair api /
body.translated_text: He said: 'Much indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Much indeed, <s>Sugata</s>! The limit of that mass of merit could not be reached even in hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 12.6 bhagavān āha: ārocayāmi te devānām indra, prativedaya / ataḥ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasunuyāt, ya imam acintyavimokṣanirdeśaṃ dharmaparyāyam udgṛhṇīyād dhārayed vācayet paryavāpnuyāt / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / dharmanirjātā hi devendra buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhiḥ, sā dharmeṇaiva śakyā pūjayitum, nāmiṣeṇa / tad anenāpi te devendra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: I declare to you, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods — make this known! That son of good family or daughter of good family would produce far greater merit, who would master, retain, recite, and fully comprehend this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, the Exposition of Inconceivable Liberation (<s>Acintyavimokṣanirdeśa</s>). For what reason? For the <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, is born from the <s>Dharma</s>, and it can be honored only through <s>Dharma</s>, not through material offerings. By this method too, O lord of the gods, should this be understood.

body.text: Vkn 12.7 bhūtapūrvaṃ devānām indra atīte 'dhvany asaṃkhyeye kalpe 'saṃkhyeyatare vipule 'pramāṇe 'cintye yad āsīt tena kālena tena samayena bhaisajyarājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān mahāvyūhe lokadhātau viśodhane kalpe / tasya khalu punar devānām indra bhaiṣajyarājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya viṃśatir antarakalpa āyuḥpramāṇam abhūt / ṣaṭtriṃśac cāsya koṭīniyutāni śrāvakānāṃ saṃgho 'bhūt / dvādaśakoṭyo bodhisatvānāṃ saṃgho 'bhūt / tena ca devānām indra kālena tena samayena ratnacchatro nāma rājābhūc cakravartī saptaratnasamanvāgataś caturdvīpeśvaraḥ / paripūrṇaṃ cāsya putrasahasram abhūc chūrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām /
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, in the past course [of time], in an incalculable <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), more incalculable still, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable — at that time, in that era, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> (Medicine King), an <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, Well-Gone, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, in the world-realm called <s>Mahāvyūha</s> (Great Array), in the <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Viśodhana</s> (Purification). And furthermore, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, the lifespan of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. His <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) numbered thirty-six <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyutas</s> (hundreds of billions). His <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> numbered twelve <s>koṭīs</s>. And at that time, in that era, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, there was a king named <s>Ratnacchatra</s> (Jeweled Parasol), a wheel-turning sovereign (<s>cakravartin</s>) endowed with the seven treasures, lord of the four continents. And he had a full thousand sons — heroic, of excellent form, crushers of enemy armies.

body.text: Vkn 12.8 tena khalu punaḥ samayena rājñā ratnacchatreṇa sa bhagavān bhaiṣajyarājas tathāgataḥ pañcāntarakalpān satkṛtaḥ saparivāraḥ sarvasukhopadhānena / iti hi devānām indra teṣāṃ pañcānām antarakalpānām atyayena sa rājā ratnacchatras tat putrasahasram āmantrayate sma: yat khalu mārṣāḥ jānīta, kṛtā mayā tathāgatasya pūjā, yūyam idānīṃ tathāgatasya pūjāṃ kuruta / iti hi devānām indra te rājakumārāḥ pitū rājño ratnacchatrasya ḥ sādhv iti pratiśrutya sarve sahitāḥ samagrā aparān pañcāntarakalpāṃs taṃ bhagavantaṃ bhaiṣajyarājaṃ tathāgataṃ satkurvanti sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ /
body.translated_text: At that time, King <s>Ratnacchatra</s> honored that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, together with his retinue, with every provision of comfort, for five intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. Then indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, at the end of those five intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, King <s>Ratnacchatra</s> addressed his thousand sons: 'Know this, good sirs — I have completed my worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; now you should make offerings to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, those princes, having replied to their father King <s>Ratnacchatra</s>, 'Very well,' all together in unison honored that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, with every provision of comfort for another five intermediate <s>kalpas</s>.

body.text: Vkn 12.9 tataś caiko rājakumāraḥ somacchatro nāma / tasyaikākino rahogatasyaitad abhūt: asti tv asyāḥ pujāyā anyodāratā viśiṣṭatarā pūjeti /
body.translated_text: Then one prince named <s>Somacchatra</s> (Moon Parasol) — while alone in seclusion, this thought occurred to him: 'Is there perhaps some other, more excellent and distinguished worship than this?'

body.text: tasyāntarīkṣād devatā buddhādhiṣṭhānenaivam āha: dharmapūjā satpuruṣa sarvapūjābhyo viśiṣyate /
body.translated_text: A <s>devatā</s> (deity), through the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, spoke to him from the sky thus: 'Worship of the <s>Dharma</s>, O good man, is superior to all [other] forms of worship.'

body.text: sa evam āha: katamā punaḥ sā dharmapūjeti /
body.translated_text: He said: 'But what is this worship of the <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.text: devatāha: etam eva tvaṃ satpuruṣa tathāgataṃ bhaiṣajyarājam upasaṃkramya paripṛccha ḥ katamā sā dharmapūjeti / sa te bhagavān vyākariṣyati /
body.translated_text: The <s>devatā</s> said: 'Go, O good man, to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> himself and ask: "What is worship of the <s>Dharma</s>?" That Blessed One will explain it to you.'

body.text: atha devānām indra sa somacchatro rājakumāro yena bhagavān bhaiṣajyarājas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt / ekāntasthitaś ca somacchatro rājakumāras taṃ bhagavantaṃ bhaiṣajyarājaṃ tathāgatam etad avocat: dharmapūjā dharmapūjeti bhagavan ucyate / katamā sā dharmapūjeti /
body.translated_text: Then, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, Prince <s>Somacchatra</s> approached the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. Having approached and having venerated the feet of the Blessed One with his head, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, Prince <s>Somacchatra</s> said this to the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>: 'Blessed One, one speaks of "worship of the <s>Dharma</s>, worship of the <s>Dharma</s>." What is this worship of the <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.text: Vkn 12.10 sa bhagavān āha: dharmapūjā kulaputra yā tathāgatabhāṣitānāṃ sūtrāntānāṃ gambhīrāṇāṃ gambhīrāvabhāsānāṃ sarvalokapratyanīkānāṃ duravagāhānāṃ durdṛśānāṃ duranubodhānāṃ sūkṣmāṇāṃ nipuṇānāṃ nirupalambhānām bodhisatvapiṭakāntargatānāṃ dhāraṇīsūtrāntarājamudrāmudritānām avivartacakrasūcakānām ṣaṭpāramitānirjātānāṃ saṃgṛhītagrahāṇāṃ bodhipakṣyadharmānugatānāṃ / bodhyaṅgāhārāṇāṃ satvamahākaruṇāvatārāṇāṃ mahāmaitrīnirdeśānāṃ māradṛṣṭigatavigatānāṃ pratītyasamutpādanirdiṣṭānām
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Worship of the <s>Dharma</s>, O son of good family, is [worship] of the <s>sūtrāntas</s> (discourses) spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — profound, illuminating the profound, contrary to the whole world, difficult to fathom, difficult to see, difficult to comprehend, subtle, refined, beyond apprehension, contained within the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>piṭaka</s> (collection), sealed with the seal of the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>sūtrānta</s>-king, indicating the wheel of non-regression, produced from the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), comprising all [that is to be] grasped, in accord with the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya-dharma</s>),

body.text: Vkn 12.11 nirātmaniḥsatvanirjīvaniṣpudgalānāṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārāṇāṃ bodhimaṇḍāhārakāṇāṃ dharmacakrapravartakānāṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvasaṃstutapraśastānāṃ saddharmavaṃśānupaccherttṝṇāṃ dharmagañjasaṃdhārakānāṃ dharmāgrapūjāvatīrṇānāṃ sarvāryajanaparigṛhītānāṃ sarvabodhisatvacaryāpraśāsakānāṃ bhūtārthadharmapratisaṃcitāvatārāṇāṃ dharmoddānānityaduḥkhānātmaśāntanirjātānāṃ duḥśīlaujoghaṭṭakānāṃ sarvaparapravādikudṛṣṭyupalambhābhiniviṣṭatrāsakarāṇāṃ sarvabuddhapraśastānāṃ saṃsāravipakṣāṇāṃ nirvāṇasukhasaṃdarśakānām / evaṃrūpāṇāṃ sūtrāntānāṃ yā deśanā saṃprakāśanā dhāraṇā pratyavekṣaṇā saddharmasaṃgrahaḥ, iyam ucyate dharmapūjeti /
body.translated_text: nourishing the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), entering into the great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) for beings, displaying great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), free from the views of <s>Māra</s>, teaching dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), without self, without being, without life, without person, [teachings of] emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), and non-formation (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>), nourishing the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), setting in motion the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, praised and lauded by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, preserving the lineage of the true <s>Dharma</s> without interruption, maintaining the treasury of <s>Dharma</s>, descending into the supreme worship of <s>Dharma</s>, embraced by all noble ones, guiding all <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices, assembled from the meaning of true reality, produced from the <s>Dharma</s> summaries of impermanence, suffering, non-self, and peace, striking against those of bad conduct, causing fear in all those attached to the wrong views and apprehension of other doctrines, praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>, opposed to <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), and displaying the bliss of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — the teaching, proclamation, retention, contemplation, and gathering of such <s>sūtrāntas</s> as these: this is called worship of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 12.12 punar aparaṃ kulaputra dharmapūjā yā dhārmeṣu dharmanidhyaptiḥ, dharmapratipattiḥ, pratītyasamutpādānulomatā, sarvāntadṛṣṭivigamaḥ, ajātānutpādakṣāntiḥ, nairātmyaniḥsatvatāvatāraḥ, hetupratyayāvirodhaḥ, avigrahaḥ, avivādaḥ, amamatvam, mamakāravigamaḥ, arthapratiśaraṇatā na vyañjanapratiśaraṇatā, jñanapratiśaraṇatā na vijñanapratiśaraṇatā, nītārthasūtrāntapratiśaraṇatā na neyārthasaṃvṛtyabhiniveśaḥ, dharmatāpratiśaraṇatā na pudgaladṛṣṭyupalambho na grāhyābhiniviṣṭatā, yathāvaddharmānugamaḥ, anālayapraveśaḥ, ālayasamudghātaḥ, avidyāvyupaśamo yāvaj jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsavyupaśamaḥ / evaṃ ca dvādaśāṅgaṃ pratītyasamutpādam avekṣyate, akṣayābhinirhāreṇa cābhinirharati, satvāvekṣayā ca dṛṣṭinirapekṣaḥ / iyam api kulaputra ucyate 'nuttarā dharmapūjeti /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O son of good family, worship of the <s>Dharma</s> is: reflection upon the <s>Dharma</s> in [all] dharmas, practice of the <s>Dharma</s>, conformity to dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), abandonment of all extreme views, patience regarding the unborn and unarisen (<s>ajātānutpāda-kṣānti</s>), entry into non-self and non-being, non-opposition to causes and conditions, freedom from contention, freedom from dispute, absence of possessiveness, abandonment of "mine"-making, reliance on meaning rather than on the letter, reliance on knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) rather than on consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), reliance on <s>sūtrāntas</s> of definitive meaning rather than attachment to those of provisional meaning through conventional [interpretation], reliance on the nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>) rather than apprehension of a person-view, and not being attached to what is to be grasped, following dharmas as they truly are, entering into non-attachment (<s>anālaya</s>), uprooting attachment (<s>ālaya</s>), cessation of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), up to the cessation of old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, despair, and distress. And thus one contemplates the twelvefold dependent origination, and brings it forth with an inexhaustible bringing-forth, and [remains] free from views while regarding beings — this too, O son of good family, is called the unsurpassed worship of the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 12.13 iti hi devānām indra sa somacchatro rājakumāras tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyarājasya tathāgatasyāntikād imāṃ dharmapūjāṃ śrutvānulomikīṃ dharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabhate sma / yathāprāvṛtaiś ca vastrābharaṇais taṃ bhagavantaṃ chādayati, evaṃ vācam abhāṣat: ahaṃ bhagavan utsahe tathāgatasya saddharmaparigrahāya saddharmapūjākaraṇatāyai saddharmaṃ parirakṣitum / tasya me bhagavāṃs tathādhiṣṭhānaṃ karotu / yathāhaṃ nihatamārapratyarthiko bhagavataḥ saddharmaṃ parigṛhnīyām /
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, Prince <s>Somacchatra</s>, having heard of this worship of the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, attained the conformity-patience regarding dharmas (<s>anulomikī dharma-kṣānti</s>). And covering that Blessed One with the garments and ornaments he was wearing, he spoke these words: 'Blessed One, I am able to undertake the preservation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s true <s>Dharma</s>, to perform the worship of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and to protect the true <s>Dharma</s>. May the Blessed One confer such empowerment upon me, that I may overcome the adversaries of <s>Māra</s> and preserve the true <s>Dharma</s> of the Blessed One.'

body.text: tasya sa tathāgato 'dhyāśayaṃ viditvā vyākṛtavān paścime kāle saddharmanagarapālarakṣāyai /
body.translated_text: That <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing his superior intention, gave him the prediction — for the guarding and protection of the city of the true <s>Dharma</s> in the future time.

body.text: Vkn 12.14 sa khalu punar devānām indra somacchatro rājakumāras tasya tathāgatasya tiṣṭhata eva śraddhayāgārād anagārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ sann ārabdhavīryo viharati sma kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu / tenārabdhavīryeṇa kuśaladharmapratiṣṭhitena na cirāt pañcābhijñā utpāditāḥ / gatiṃgataś ca dhāraṇīnām abhūd anācchedyapratibhānaḥ / sa tasya bhagavataḥ parinirvṛtasyābhijñādhāraṇībalena paripūrṇān daśāntarakalpāṃs tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyarājasya tathāgatasya pravṛttaṃ dharmacakram anuvartayati sma / tena khalu punar devānām indra somacchatreṇa bhikṣuṇā saddharmaparigrahābhiyuktena daśakoṭīśatāni satvānām avaivartikāni kṛtāny abhūvann anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, caturdaśa ca prāṇiniyutāni śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikāni, apramāṇāś ca satvāḥ svargopagāḥ kṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, Prince <s>Somacchatra</s>, while that <s>Tathāgata</s> was still living, went forth from home into homelessness out of faith, and dwelt with vigorous effort in wholesome dharmas. Through his vigorous effort, established in wholesome dharmas, before long he produced the five supernatural knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). He attained mastery of <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (mnemonic codes) and unimpeded eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>). Through the power of his supernatural knowledges and <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, for a full ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing) of that Blessed One, the bhikṣu <s>Somacchatra</s> continued to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> set in motion by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>. And indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, the bhikṣu <s>Somacchatra</s>, devoted to the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s>, rendered one thousand <s>koṭī</s>-hundreds (one hundred trillion) of beings irreversible from supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi</s>), and fourteen <s>niyutas</s> (millions) of living beings were established in the vehicles of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and immeasurable beings were led to rebirth in heaven.

body.text: Vkn 12.15 syāt khalu punas te devānām indra anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena ratnacchatro nāma rājābhūc cakravartī, na khalu punas te devānām indra evaṃ draṣṭavyam / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / ratnārciḥ sa tathāgatas tena kālena tena samayena ratnacchatro nāma rājābhūc cakravartī / yat punas tad rājño ratnacchatrasya putrasahasram abhūt / ime te bhādrakalpikā bodhisatvā abhūvan / yad iha bhadrakalpe paripūrṇaṃ buddhasahasram utpatsyate yataś catvāra utpannāḥ śeṣā utpatsyante, krakucchandapramukhā yāvad rocaparyavasānāḥ, roco nāma tathāgataḥ paścimako bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.15) You might think, O lord of gods, that the king <s>Ratnacchattra</s>, the <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), at that time was someone else. But you should not regard it so. For what reason? That <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnārcis</s> was, at that time, the king <s>Ratnacchattra</s>, the <s>cakravartin</s>. And those thousand sons of king <s>Ratnacchattra</s> — they were the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon). In this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s>, a full thousand <s>Buddhas</s> will arise, of whom four have already arisen and the rest will arise, beginning with <s>Krakucchanda</s> and ending with <s>Roca</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Roca</s> will be the last.

body.text: syāt khalu punas te devānām indra evam anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena somacchatro nāma rājakumāro 'bhūd yena tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyarājasya tathāgatasya saddharmaḥ parigṛhīta iti / na khalu punas ta evaṃ draṣṭavyam / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena somacchatro nāma rājakumāro 'bhūvam / tad anenāpi te devendra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam / yāvatyas tathāgatānāṃ pūjāḥ, dharmapūjā tāsām agryākhyāyate, jyeṣṭhā śreṣṭhā varā pravarā praṇītottarā niruttarākhyāyata iti / tasmād iha devānām indra dharmapūjayā māṃ pūjayata, mā āmiṣapūjayā / dharmasatkāreṇa māṃ satkuruta, mā āmiṣasatkāreṇa /
body.translated_text: You might also think, O lord of gods, that prince <s>Somacchattra</s>, who preserved the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, was someone else. But you should not regard it so. For what reason? I myself was, at that time, prince <s>Somacchattra</s>. Therefore, O lord of gods, by this teaching too you should know: among all forms of worship of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Dharma</s>-worship is declared to be the foremost — it is declared the highest, most excellent, supreme, surpassing, exalted, and unsurpassed. Therefore, O lord of gods, worship me with <s>Dharma</s>-worship, not with material worship! Honor me with <s>Dharma</s>-reverence, not with material reverence!'

body.text: Vkn 12.16 tatra bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisatvam āmantrayate sma: imāṃ te 'haṃ maitreya asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīsamudānītām anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim anuparīndāmi, yathema evaṃrūpā dharmaparyāyā yuṣmadadhiṣṭhānena parigraheṇa tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya paścime kāle paścime samaye jambūdvīpe vaistārikā bhaveyuḥ, nāntardhīyeran / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / bhaviṣyanti maitreya anāgate 'dhvani kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraś ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāś cāvaropitakuśalā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ saṃprasthitāḥ / te 'śravaṇād asya dharmaparyāyasya mā parihāsyanta iti / imān evaṃrūpān sūtrāntāñ śrutvātīva prema ca prasādaṃ ca pratilapsyante, mūrdhnā ca pratigrahīṣyanti / teṣāṃ tvaṃ maitreya tathārūpāṇāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ cānurakṣāyā imān evaṃrūpān sūtrāntāṃs tasmin kāle vaistārikān kuryāḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.16) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'I entrust to you, <s>Maitreya</s>, this <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), which has been accumulated over innumerable <s>koṭis</s> (billions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), so that by your supernatural support and protection, such <s>Dharma</s>-discourses as these may become widely spread in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in the last age, in the final time, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and may not disappear. For what reason? In the future, <s>Maitreya</s>, there will be sons and daughters of good family, as well as <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, who have planted roots of merit and set forth toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Lest they be deprived by not hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — upon hearing such <s>sūtrāntas</s> as these, they will be filled with great affection and devotion, and will receive them upon the crown of their heads. You, <s>Maitreya</s>, should make such <s>sūtrāntas</s> widely known at that time, for the protection of such sons and daughters of good family.'

body.text: Vkn 12.17 dve ime maitreya bodhisatvānāṃ mudre / katame dve / vicitrapadavyañjanaprasādamudrā ca gambhīradharmanayānuttrāsayathābhūtāvatārapraveśamudrā ca / ime maitreya bodhisatvānāṃ dve mudre / tatra maitreya ye bodhisatvā vicitrapadavyañjanaprasādagurukāḥ, ta ādikarmikā bodhisatvā veditavyāḥ / ye punar imaṃ maitreya gambhīraṃ sūtrāntam arūpalepaṃ yamakavyatyastanihārapadapuṭaprabhedaṃ pravartayiṣyanti śrosyanty adhimokṣyante vedayiṣyanti, ime bodhisatvāś ciracaritabrahmacaryā veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.17) 'There are, <s>Maitreya</s>, two seals (<s>mudrā</s>) of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. What are the two? The seal of delight in elegant words and phrases, and the seal of fearless entry into the profound <s>Dharma</s>-method as it truly is. These, <s>Maitreya</s>, are the two seals of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Among them, <s>Maitreya</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who value delight in elegant words and phrases should be known as beginners. But those, <s>Maitreya</s>, who will set in motion, will hear, will have confidence in, and will understand this profound <s>sūtrānta</s> — free from attachment to form, with its exposition unfolding through intertwined paired phrases — these <s>bodhisattvas</s> should be known as those who have long practiced the holy life.'

body.text:
Vkn 12.18 tatra maitreya dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyām ādikarmikā bodhisatvā ātmānaṃ kṣiṇvanti / na ca gambhīreṣu dharmeṣu nidhyaptiṃ gacchanti / katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām / aśrutapūrvāṃś ca gambhīrān sūtrāntāñ śrutvottrasyanti / saṃśayaprāptāś ca bhavanti, nānumodante / uttari ca pratikṣipante: ya ete 'smābhiḥ pūrvaṃ na śrutapūrvāḥ kuta ime 'dhunāgatāḥ / ye ca te kulaputrā gambhīradharmasūtrāntadhārakā gambhīradharmabhājanā gambhīradharmadeśayitāraḥ, tān na sevante na bhajante na paryupāsante, agauravāś ca teṣu bhavanti, antarāntarā ca teṣām avarṇam api niścārayanti / ābhyāṃ maitreya dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyām ādikarmikā bodhisatvā ātmānaṃ kṣiṇvanti / na ca gambhīreṣu dharmeṣu nidhyaptiṃ gacchanti /
Vkn 12.19 dvābhyāṃ maitreya kāraṇābhyāṃ gambhīrādhimuktiko bodhisatva ātmānaṃ kṣiṇoti / na cānutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiṃ pratilabhate / katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām / tāṃś cādikarmikān aciracaritān bodhisatvān avamanyate paribhavati na grāhayati na vivecayati nānuśāsti / tayaiva ca gambhīrādhimuktyā śikṣāyām agauravo bhavati / lokāmiṣadānena ca satvān anugṛhṇāti, na dharmadānena / ābhyāṃ maitreya dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ gambhīrādhimuktiko bodhisatva ātmānaṃ kṣiṇoti / na ca kṣipram anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiṃ pratilabhate /
body.translated_text:
(Vkn 12.18) 'Therein, <s>Maitreya</s>, beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> injure themselves through two causes and do not attain discernment in the profound <s>dharmas</s>. What are these two? First, upon hearing profound <s>sūtrāntas</s> that they have never heard before, they become frightened. Filled with doubt, they do not rejoice but rather reject them, saying: "We have never heard these before — where have they suddenly come from?" Second, those sons of good family who uphold the profound <s>Dharma sūtrāntas</s>, who are vessels of the profound <s>Dharma</s>, and who teach the profound <s>Dharma</s> — they do not attend upon them, do not honor them, do not serve them, are disrespectful toward them, and from time to time even speak ill of them. Through these two causes, <s>Maitreya</s>, beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> injure themselves and do not attain discernment in the profound <s>dharmas</s>.
(Vkn 12.19) Through two causes, <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of profound inclination injures himself and does not attain the <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance) regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>. What are the two? First, he despises and belittles beginner <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have not long practiced — he does not guide them, does not educate them, and does not instruct them. Second, being proud of his own profound inclination, he is disrespectful toward the training. And he benefits beings with worldly material gifts, not with the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. Through these two causes, <s>Maitreya</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of profound inclination injures himself and does not quickly attain the <s>kṣānti</s> regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: Vkn 12.20 evam ukte maitreyo bodhisatvo bhagavantam etad avocat: āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvat subhāṣitaṃ bhagavataḥ / vayaṃ bhagavan etāṃś ca doṣān vivarjayiṣyāmaḥ / imāṃ ca tathāgatasyāsaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasamudānītām anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ parirakṣiṣyāmo dhārayiṣyāmaḥ / teṣāṃ cānāgatānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ bhājanībhūtānām imān evaṃrūpān sūtrāntān hastagatān kariṣyāmaḥ / smṛtiṃ caiṣām upasaṃhariṣyāmo yayā smṛtyemān evaṃrūpān sūtrāntān rocayiṣyanty udgrahīṣyanti paryavāpsyanti dhārayiṣyanti pravartayiṣyanti likhiṣyanti pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa deśayiṣyanti / teṣāṃ ca vayaṃ bhagavan upastambhaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / ye ca khalu punar bhagavan tasmin kāla imān evaṃrupān sūtrāntān rocayiṣyanti pravartayiṣyanti / veditavyam etad bhagavan maitreyasya bodhisatvasyādhiṣṭhānam iti /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.20) When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how well-spoken is the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s>! We, <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall avoid these faults. And we shall protect and uphold this <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> accumulated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> over innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. And for those sons and daughters of good family in the future who are worthy vessels, we shall place such <s>sūtrāntas</s> as these in their hands. And we shall impart to them the mindfulness by which they will delight in, take up, master, uphold, propagate, copy, and teach extensively to others such <s>sūtrāntas</s> as these. And we, <s>Bhagavān</s>, shall give them support. And those, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who at that time will delight in and propagate such <s>sūtrāntas</s> as these — this should be known, <s>Bhagavān</s>, as the supernatural support of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>.'

body.text: atha bhagavān maitreyasya bodhisatvasya sādhukāram adāt: sādhu sādhu maitreya, subhāṣitā ta iyaṃ vāk / anumodate tathāgato 'nujānāti ca subhāsitam /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> his approval: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Maitreya</s>! Well-spoken is this word of yours. The <s>Tathāgata</s> rejoices and approves of your well-spoken words.'

body.text: Vkn 12.21 atha te bodhisatvā ekasvareṇa vācam abhāṣanta: vayam api bhagavan tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasyānyonyebhyo buddhakṣetrebhya āgatyemāṃ tathāgatabuddhabodhiṃ vaistārikīṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / teṣāṃ ca kulaputrāṇām ārocayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.21) Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> spoke in unison: 'We too, <s>Bhagavān</s>, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, coming from our respective <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, shall make this <s>Tathāgata</s>-awakening widely known. And we shall proclaim it to those sons of good family.'

body.text: Vkn 12.22 atha catvāro mahārājāno bhagavantam etad avocan: yatra yatra bhagavan grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣv ima evaṃrūpā dharmaparyāyāḥ pracariṣyanti deśayiṣyanti prakāśayiṣyanti, tatra tatra vayaṃ bhagavan catvāro mahārājāḥ sabalāḥ savāhanāḥ saparivārā dharmaśravaṇāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmaḥ / tasya ca dharmabhāṇakasya samantato yojanaśataṃ rakṣāṃ saṃvidhāṣyāmaḥ, yathā tasya dharmabhāṇakasya na kaścid avatāraprekṣy avatāragaveṣy avatāraṃ lapsyate /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.22) Then the four great kings (<s>Mahārājas</s>) said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Wherever, <s>Bhagavān</s> — in villages, cities, market-towns, kingdoms, or royal capitals — these <s>Dharma</s>-discourses will be circulated, taught, and proclaimed, there we, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the four great kings, with our armies, vehicles, and retinues, shall come for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. And we shall provide protection for a hundred <s>yojanas</s> all around that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, so that no one looking for a vulnerability, seeking a vulnerability, shall find a vulnerability in that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher.'

body.text: Vkn 12.23 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma: udgṛhāṇa tvam ānanda imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhāraya vācaya pareṣāṃ ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśaya /
body.translated_text: (Vkn 12.23) There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Take up this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, <s>Ānanda</s>, retain it, recite it, and make it widely known to others in detail.'

body.text: āha: udgṛhīto me bhagavan ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ / kiṃ bhagavan asya dharmaparyāyasya nāmadheyam / kathaṃ caainaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: He said: 'I have taken up this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, <s>Bhagavān</s>. But what, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the name of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse? And how shall I retain it?'

body.text: bhagavān āha: tasmāt tarhi tvam ānanda imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ vimalakīrtinirdeśaṃ yamakapuṭavyatyastanihāram acintyadharmavimokṣaparivartam ity api dhārayemaṃ dharmaparyāyam // //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should retain this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse as the <s>Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s> (Teaching of <s>Vimalakīrti</s>), also known as <s>Yamakapuṭavyatyastanihāra</s> (The Exposition through Intertwined Paired Phrases), and also as the <s>Acintyadharmavimokṣaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Inconceivable <s>Dharma</s>-Liberation). Retain this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.' //

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān / āttamanā vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśrīś ca kumārabhūta āyuṣmāṃś cānandas te ca mahāśrāvakāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti // //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, <s>Vimalakīrti</s> the <s>Licchavi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the eternally youthful, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, and that entire assembly including <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> — the whole world rejoiced at the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. //

body.text: nigamanaparīndanāparivarto nāma dvādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth chapter, called <s>Nigamanaparīndanā</s> (Conclusion and Entrustment). //

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hy avadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodho evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and their cessation — thus speaks the great ascetic (<s>mahāśramaṇa</s>). //

body.text: deyadharmo 'yaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyino bhikṣuśīladhvajasya yad atra puṇyaṃ tad bhavatv ācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṃgamaṃ kṛtvā sakalasatvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalāvāptaya iti //
body.translated_text: This religious gift belongs to <s>Bhikṣu</s> <s>Śīladhvaja</s>, a follower of the excellent <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Whatever merit is herein, may it — with teachers, preceptors, mother and father going first — be for the attainment of the fruit of supreme knowledge (<s>anuttarajñāna</s>) by the entire mass of beings. //

body.text: śrīmadgopāladevarājye saṃvat 12 bhādradine 29 likhiteyam upasthāyakacāṇḍokasyeti //
body.translated_text: This was written during the reign of the glorious King <s>Gopāladeva</s>, in the year 12, on the 29th day of <s>Bhādra</s>, by the attendant <s>Cāṇḍoka</s>. //
